1.17.s:
.. śatānīka uvāca .. ..
brūhi me vista rādbrahmanpratipatkṛtyamādarāt ..
brahmapūjāvidhānaṃ ca pūjane yacca vai phalam..1..
1.17.d:
॥ शतानीक उवाच ॥ ॥
ब्रूहि मे विस्त राद्ब्रह्मन्प्रतिपत्कृत्यमादरात् ॥
ब्रह्मपूजाविधानं च पूजने यच्च वै फलम्॥1॥
1.17.m:
Śatānīka said:
Tell me in detail, O brahmin, with care, about the duty on the pratipat, / the ritual of worship of Brahmā, and the fruit [gained] in that worship.

1.17.s:
.. sumaṃturuvāca .. ..
śṛṇuṣvaikamanā rājankathayāmyeṣa śāṃtidam ..
pūrvamekārṇave ghore naṣṭe sthāvarajaṃgame .. 2 ..
1.17.d:
॥ सुमंतुरुवाच ॥ ॥
शृणुष्वैकमना राजन्कथयाम्येष शांतिदम् ॥
पूर्वमेकार्णवे घोरे नष्टे स्थावरजंगमे ॥ 2 ॥
1.17.m:
Sumantu said:
Listen with single-minded attention, O king; I shall relate that which brings peace. / Formerly, when the immovable and movable had perished in the terrible single ocean,

1.17.s:
svayaṃbhūrabhavaddevaḥ surajyeṣṭhaścaturmukhaḥ ..
sasarja lokāndevāṃśca bhūtāni vividhāni ca ..3..
1.17.d:
स्वयंभूरभवद्देवः सुरज्येष्ठश्चतुर्मुखः ॥
ससर्ज लोकान्देवांश्च भूतानि विविधानि च ॥3॥
1.17.m: the Self-born god, eldest of the gods, the four-faced one, appeared; / he created the worlds, the gods, and diverse beings

1.17.s:
kāyena manasā vācā jaṃgamasthāvarāṇi ca ..
pitā yaḥ sarvadevānāṃ bhūtānāṃ ca pitāmahaḥ .. 4 ..
1.17.d:
कायेन मनसा वाचा जंगमस्थावराणि च ॥
पिता यः सर्वदेवानां भूतानां च पितामहः ॥ 4 ॥
1.17.m: by body, mind, and speech, both movable and immovable— / he who is the father of all gods and the grandfather of beings.

1.17.s:
tasmādeṣa sadā pūjyo yato lokaguruḥ paraḥ ..
sṛjatyeṣa jagatkṛtsnaṃ pāti saṃharate tathā ..5..
1.17.d:
तस्मादेष सदा पूज्यो यतो लोकगुरुः परः ॥
सृजत्येष जगत्कृत्स्नं पाति संहरते तथा ॥5॥
1.17.m: Therefore he is ever to be worshipped, because he is the supreme teacher of the world; / he creates the entire universe, protects it, and destroys it.

1.17.s:
rudro'sya manaso jāto viṣṇurjāto'sya vakṣasaḥ ..
mukhebhyaścaturo vedā vedāṃgāni ca kṛtsnaśaḥ .. 6 ..
1.17.d:
रुद्रोऽस्य मनसो जातो विष्णुर्जातोऽस्य वक्षसः ॥
मुखेभ्यश्चतुरो वेदा वेदांगानि च कृत्स्नशः ॥ 6 ॥
1.17.m: Rudra was born from his mind, Viṣṇu was born from his chest, / and from his mouths the four Vedas and the Vedāṅgas in their entirety.

1.17.s:
devāpsarasagaṃdharvāḥ sayakṣoragarākṣasāḥ ..
pūjayaṃti sadā vīra viriṃciṃ suranāyakam ..7..
1.17.d:
देवाप्सरसगंधर्वाः सयक्षोरगराक्षसाः ॥
पूजयंति सदा वीर विरिंचिं सुरनायकम् ॥7॥
1.17.m: Gods, apsarases, and gandharvas, along with yakṣas, uragas, and rākṣasas, / ever worship Viriñci, the leader of the gods, O hero.

1.17.s:
sarvo brahmamayo lokaḥ sarvaṃ brahmaṇi saṃsthitam..
tasmātsamarcayedbrahmanya icchecchreya ātmanaḥ .. 8 ..
1.17.d:
सर्वो ब्रह्ममयो लोकः सर्वं ब्रह्मणि संस्थितम्॥
तस्मात्समर्चयेद्ब्रह्मन्य इच्छेच्छ्रेय आत्मनः ॥ 8 ॥
1.17.m: The entire world consists of Brahmā; everything is established in Brahmā; / therefore one who desires his own welfare should thoroughly worship Brahmā.

1.17.s:
yo na pūjayate bhaktyā surajyeṣṭhaṃ sureśvaram ..
na sa nākasya rājyasya na ca mokṣasya bhājanam .. 9 ..
1.17.d:
यो न पूजयते भक्त्या सुरज्येष्ठं सुरेश्वरम् ॥
न स नाकस्य राज्यस्य न च मोक्षस्य भाजनम् ॥ 9 ॥
1.17.m: Whoever does not worship the eldest of gods, the lord of gods, with devotion, / is not fit for heaven, for sovereignty, nor for liberation.

1.17.s:
yastu pūjayate bhaktyā viriṃciṃ bhuvaneśvaram ..
sa nākarājyamokṣeṣu kṣipraṃ bhavati bhājanam .. 1.17.10 ..
1.17.d:
यस्तु पूजयते भक्त्या विरिंचिं भुवनेश्वरम् ॥
स नाकराज्यमोक्षेषु क्षिप्रं भवति भाजनम् ॥ 1.17.10 ॥
1.17.m: But whoever worships Viriñci, the lord of the worlds, with devotion, / swiftly becomes fit for heaven, sovereignty, and liberation.

1.17.s:
tasmātsaumyamanā bhūtvā yāvajjīvaṃ pratijñayā ..
arcayitvā sadā devamāpannopi naro nṛpa .. 11 ..
1.17.d:
तस्मात्सौम्यमना भूत्वा यावज्जीवं प्रतिज्ञया ॥
अर्चयित्वा सदा देवमापन्नोपि नरो नृप ॥ 11 ॥
1.17.m: Therefore, having become gentle-minded, with a lifelong vow, / ever worshipping the god even when fallen into misfortune, O man, O king,

1.17.s:
varaṃ dehaparityāgo varaṃ narakasambhavaḥ ..
na tvevāpūjya bhuṃjaṃti devaṃ vai padmasaṃbhavam .. 12 ..
1.17.d:
वरं देहपरित्यागो वरं नरकसम्भवः ॥
न त्वेवापूज्य भुंजंति देवं वै पद्मसंभवम् ॥ 12 ॥
1.17.m: better is abandoning the body, better is birth in hell, / than that people eat without having worshipped the lotus-born god.

1.17.s:
sadā pūjayate yastu vīra bhaktyā pitāmaham ..
manuṣyacarmaṇā naddhaḥ sa vedhā nātra saṃśayaḥ..13..
1.17.d:
सदा पूजयते यस्तु वीर भक्त्या पितामहम् ॥
मनुष्यचर्मणा नद्धः स वेधा नात्र संशयः॥13॥
1.17.m: The man who always worships the Grandfather with devotion, O hero, / is Brahmā himself covered in human skin; of this there is no doubt.

1.17.s:
na hi vedho'rcanātkiṃcitpuṇyamabhyadhikaṃ bhavet ..
iti vijñāya yatnena pūjanī yaḥ sadā vidhiḥ .. 14 ..
1.17.d:
न हि वेधोऽर्चनात्किंचित्पुण्यमभ्यधिकं भवेत् ॥
इति विज्ञाय यत्नेन पूजनी यः सदा विधिः ॥ 14 ॥
1.17.m: Indeed, no religious merit can be greater than worship of Brahmā; / knowing this, Brahmā should always be worshipped with effort.

1.17.s:
yo brahmāṇaṃ dveṣṭi mohātsarvadevanamaskṛtam ..
naro narakagāmī syāttasya saṃbhāṣaṇādapi .. 15 ..
1.17.d:
यो ब्रह्माणं द्वेष्टि मोहात्सर्वदेवनमस्कृतम् ॥
नरो नरकगामी स्यात्तस्य संभाषणादपि ॥ 15 ॥
1.17.m: A man who hates Brahmā, who is bowed to by all the gods, out of delusion, / goes to hell even from merely speaking with him.

1.17.s:
brahmaṇorcāṃ pratiṣṭhāpya sarvayatnairvidhānataḥ ..
yatpuṇyaṃ phalamāpnoti tadekāgramanāḥ śṛṇu .. 16 ..
1.17.d:
ब्रह्मणोर्चां प्रतिष्ठाप्य सर्वयत्नैर्विधानतः ॥
यत्पुण्यं फलमाप्नोति तदेकाग्रमनाः शृणु ॥ 16 ॥
1.17.m: Having consecrated an image of Brahmā with every effort according to the ritual rules, / hear with single-minded attention the meritorious fruit he attains:

1.17.s:
sarvayajñatapodānatīrthavedeṣu yatphalam ..
tatphalaṃ koṭiguṇitaṃ labhedvedhaḥ pratiṣṭhayā .. 17 ..
1.17.d:
सर्वयज्ञतपोदानतीर्थवेदेषु यत्फलम् ॥
तत्फलं कोटिगुणितं लभेद्वेधः प्रतिष्ठया ॥ 17 ॥
1.17.m: Whatever fruit is found in all sacrifices, austerities, gifts, holy places, and Vedas, / he gains that fruit multiplied a crore of times by establishing Brahmā.

1.17.s:
kañjajaṃ sthāpayedyastu kṛtvā śālāṃ manoramām ..
sarvāṃgamodita puṇyaṃ koṭikoṭiguṇaṃ labhet .. 18 ..
1.17.d:
कञ्जजं स्थापयेद्यस्तु कृत्वा शालां मनोरमाम् ॥
सर्वांगमोदित पुण्यं कोटिकोटिगुणं लभेत् ॥ 18 ॥
1.17.m: He who sets up the Lotus-Born [Brahmā] after constructing a delightful hall / obtains merit that brings joy to all limbs, multiplied a crore of crores.

1.17.s:
mātṛjānpitṛjāṃścaiva yāṃ caivodvahate striyam ..
kulaikaviṃśamuttārya brahmaloke mahīyate .. 19 ..
1.17.d:
मातृजान्पितृजांश्चैव यां चैवोद्वहते स्त्रियम् ॥
कुलैकविंशमुत्तार्य ब्रह्मलोके महीयते ॥ 19 ॥
1.17.m: Saving the relatives on his mother’s side, on his father’s side, and the wife he marries— / twenty-one generations in all—he is glorified in the world of Brahmā.

1.17.s:
bhuktvā tu vipulānbhogānpralaye samupasthite ..
jñānayogaṃ samāsādya sa tatraiva vimucyate .. 1.17.20 ..
1.17.d:
भुक्त्वा तु विपुलान्भोगान्प्रलये समुपस्थिते ॥
ज्ञानयोगं समासाद्य स तत्रैव विमुच्यते ॥ 1.17.20 ॥
1.17.m: Having enjoyed extensive pleasures, when the cosmic dissolution arrives, / attaining the yoga of knowledge, he is liberated right there.

1.17.s:
atha vā rājyamākāṃkṣejjāyate saṃbhavāṃtare ..
saptadvīpasamudrāyāḥ kṣiteradhipatirbhavet .. 21 ..
1.17.d:
अथ वा राज्यमाकांक्षेज्जायते संभवांतरे ॥
सप्तद्वीपसमुद्रायाः क्षितेरधिपतिर्भवेत् ॥ 21 ॥
1.17.m: Or if he should desire kingship, being born in another rebirth, / he becomes the ruler of the earth containing the seven continents and oceans.

1.17.s:
trisaṃdhyaṃ yo japedbrahma kṛtvāṣṭadala paṃkajam ..
paurṇamāsyāṃ pratipadi tasya puṇyaphalaṃ śṛṇu .. 22 ..
1.17.d:
त्रिसंध्यं यो जपेद्ब्रह्म कृत्वाष्टदल पंकजम् ॥
पौर्णमास्यां प्रतिपदि तस्य पुण्यफलं शृणु ॥ 22 ॥
1.17.m: Hear the meritorious fruit of him who, having made an eight-petalled lotus, / mutters the prayer to Brahmā at the three junctures of the day on the full moon and the first day [of the fortnight]:

1.17.s:
anenaiva sa dehena brahmā saṃtiṣṭhate kṣitau ..
pāpahā sarvamartyānāṃ darśanātsparśanādapi .. .. 23 ..
1.17.d:
अनेनैव स देहेन ब्रह्मा संतिष्ठते क्षितौ ॥
पापहा सर्वमर्त्यानां दर्शनात्स्पर्शनादपि ॥ ॥ 23 ॥
1.17.m: In this very body he abides as Brahmā on the earth, / destroying the sins of all mortals by sight and even by touch.

1.17.s:
uddhṛtya divi saṃsthāpya kulānāmekaviṃśatim ..
taiḥ kulaiḥ sahito nityaṃ modate gogato nṛpa .. 24 ..
1.17.d:
उद्धृत्य दिवि संस्थाप्य कुलानामेकविंशतिम् ॥
तैः कुलैः सहितो नित्यं मोदते गोगतो नृप ॥ 24 ॥
1.17.m: Having delivered twenty-one generations and established them in heaven, / together with those generations he continually rejoices, having reached the realm of rays, O king.

1.17.s:
apyekavāraṃ yo bhaktyā pūjayetpadma saṃbhavam ..
padmasthaṃ mūrtimaṃtaṃ vā brahmalokaṃ sa gacchati ..25..
1.17.d:
अप्येकवारं यो भक्त्या पूजयेत्पद्म संभवम् ॥
पद्मस्थं मूर्तिमंतं वा ब्रह्मलोकं स गच्छति ॥25॥
1.17.m: Even if one worships the Lotus-Born [Brahmā] with devotion once, / seated on a lotus or in an embodied form, he goes to the world of Brahmā.

1.17.s:
puṇyakṣayātkṣitiṃ prāpya bhavetkṣitipatirmahān ..
vedavedāṃgatattvajño brāhmaṇaścāpi jāyate.. .. 26 ..
1.17.d:
पुण्यक्षयात्क्षितिं प्राप्य भवेत्क्षितिपतिर्महान् ॥
वेदवेदांगतत्त्वज्ञो ब्राह्मणश्चापि जायते॥ ॥ 26 ॥
1.17.m: Upon the exhaustion of that merit, reaching the earth, he becomes a great king; / or he is born as a brāhmaṇa who knows the reality of the Vedas and Vedāṅgas.

1.17.s:
na tattapobhiratyugrairna ca sarvairmahāmakhaiḥ ..
gacchedbrahmapuraṃ divyaṃ mukttvā bhaktiparātmakān ..27..
1.17.d:
न तत्तपोभिरत्युग्रैर्न च सर्वैर्महामखैः ॥
गच्छेद्ब्रह्मपुरं दिव्यं मुक्त्त्वा भक्तिपरात्मकान् ॥27॥
1.17.m: One cannot go to the divine city of Brahmā through extremely fierce austerities / nor through all great sacrifices, except for those whose souls are devoted to bhakti.

1.17.s:
mṛddārveṣṭakaśailairvā yaḥ kuryādbrahmaṇo gṛham ..
triḥsaptakulasaṃyukto brahmaloke mahīyate .. 28 ..
1.17.d:
मृद्दार्वेष्टकशैलैर्वा यः कुर्याद्ब्रह्मणो गृहम् ॥
त्रिःसप्तकुलसंयुक्तो ब्रह्मलोके महीयते ॥ 28 ॥
1.17.m: He who builds a house for Brahmā out of clay, wood, bricks, or stones, / endowed with thrice-seven generations, is glorified in the world of Brahmā.

1.17.s:
mṛnmayātkoṭiguṇitaṃ phalaṃ dārviṣṭakāmaye ..
iṣṭakādviguṇa puṇyaṃ kṛte śailamaye gṛhe .. 29 ..
1.17.d:
मृन्मयात्कोटिगुणितं फलं दार्विष्टकामये ॥
इष्टकाद्विगुण पुण्यं कृते शैलमये गृहे ॥ 29 ॥
1.17.m: A crore times more fruit is attained from one made of wood and brick than from a clay one; / double the merit of brick is gained when a house made of stone is built.

1.17.s:
krīḍamānopi yaḥ kuryācchālāṃ vai brahmaṇo nṛpa ..
brahmaloke sa labhate vimānaṃ sarvakāmikam .. 1.17.30 ..
1.17.d:
क्रीडमानोपि यः कुर्याच्छालां वै ब्रह्मणो नृप ॥
ब्रह्मलोके स लभते विमानं सर्वकामिकम् ॥ 1.17.30 ॥
1.17.m: Even in play, O king, he who builds a hall for Brahmā / obtains a celestial chariot yielding all desires in the world of Brahmā,

1.17.s:
puṣpamālāparikṣiptaṃ kiṃkiṇījālabhūṣitam ..
dolāvikṣepasaṃpannaṃ ghaṃṭācāmarabhūṣitam .. 31 ..
1.17.d:
पुष्पमालापरिक्षिप्तं किंकिणीजालभूषितम् ॥
दोलाविक्षेपसंपन्नं घंटाचामरभूषितम् ॥ 31 ॥
1.17.m: encircled with garlands of flowers, adorned with a lattice of tinkling bells, / provided with swaying swings, decorated with bells and chowries,

1.17.s:
muktādāmavitānena śobhitaṃ sūryasuprabham ..
apsarogaṇasaṃkīrṇaṃ sarvakāmasukhapradam .. 32 ..
1.17.d:
मुक्तादामवितानेन शोभितं सूर्यसुप्रभम् ॥
अप्सरोगणसंकीर्णं सर्वकामसुखप्रदम् ॥ 32 ॥
1.17.m: beautified with canopies of pearl strands, possessing the brilliant radiance of the sun, / crowded with hosts of apsarases, granting every desire and pleasure.

1.17.s:
tatroṣitvā mahābhogī krīḍamānaḥ sadā suraiḥ ..
punarāgatya lokesminrājā bhavati dhārmikaḥ .. 33 ..
1.17.d:
तत्रोषित्वा महाभोगी क्रीडमानः सदा सुरैः ॥
पुनरागत्य लोकेस्मिन्राजा भवति धार्मिकः ॥ 33 ॥
1.17.m: Dwelling there as one enjoying great pleasures, always sporting with the gods, / having returned to this world, he becomes a righteous king.

1.17.s:
paśyanpariharañjantūnmṛdupūrvaṃ mahīpate ..
śanaiḥ saṃmārjanaṃ kurvaṃścāndrāyaṇaphalaṃ vrajet .. 34 ..
1.17.d:
पश्यन्परिहरञ्जन्तून्मृदुपूर्वं महीपते ॥
शनैः संमार्जनं कुर्वंश्चान्द्रायणफलं व्रजेत् ॥ 34 ॥
1.17.m: Watching and sparing living creatures, gently, O lord of the earth, / slowly sweeping, he attains the fruit of a cāndrāyaṇa penance.

1.17.s:
vastrapūtena toyena yaḥ kuryādupalepanam ..
paśyanpariharañjatūṃścāṃdrāyaṇaphalaṃ labhet .. 35 ..
1.17.d:
वस्त्रपूतेन तोयेन यः कुर्यादुपलेपनम् ॥
पश्यन्परिहरञ्जतूंश्चांद्रायणफलं लभेत् ॥ 35 ॥
1.17.m: He who smears [the floor] with water purified by cloth, / watching and avoiding living creatures, attains the fruit of a cāndrāyaṇa penance.

1.17.s:
nairaṃtaryeṇa yaḥ kuryātpakṣaṃ saṃmārjanārcanam ..
yugakoṭiśataṃ sāgraṃ brahmaloke mahīyate .. 36 ..
1.17.d:
नैरंतर्येण यः कुर्यात्पक्षं संमार्जनार्चनम् ॥
युगकोटिशतं साग्रं ब्रह्मलोके महीयते ॥ 36 ॥
1.17.m: He who continuously performs sweeping and worship for a fortnight / is glorified in the world of Brahmā for more than a hundred crores of yugas.

1.17.s:
tasyāṃte sa caturvedaḥ surūpaḥ priyadarśanaḥ ..
āḍhyaḥ sarvaguṇopeto rājā bhavati dhārmikaḥ .. 37 ..
1.17.d:
तस्यांते स चतुर्वेदः सुरूपः प्रियदर्शनः ॥
आढ्यः सर्वगुणोपेतो राजा भवति धार्मिकः ॥ 37 ॥
1.17.m: At the end of that, he becomes a righteous king, knowing the four Vedas, / handsome, pleasant to behold, rich, and endowed with all virtues.

1.17.s:
kapaṭenāpi yaḥ kuryādbrahmaśālāṃ sumānada ..
saṃmārjanādi vai karma so'pi prāpnoti tatphalam .. 38 ..
1.17.d:
कपटेनापि यः कुर्याद्ब्रह्मशालां सुमानद ॥
संमार्जनादि वै कर्म सोऽपि प्राप्नोति तत्फलम् ॥ 38 ॥
1.17.m: Even deceitfully, O giver of great honour, he who performs the work of sweeping and so on / in the hall of Brahmā, even he obtains that fruit.

1.17.s:
tāvaddhamaṃti saṃsāre duḥkhaśokabhayaplutāḥ ..
na bhavaṃti suraśreṣṭhe yāvadraktā mahīpate .. 39 ..
1.17.d:
तावद्धमंति संसारे दुःखशोकभयप्लुताः ॥
न भवंति सुरश्रेष्ठे यावद्रक्ता महीपते ॥ 39 ॥
1.17.m: They wander in saṃsāra overcome with pain, grief, and fear / only as long as they are not devoted to the best of gods, O lord of the earth.

1.17.s:
samāsaktaṃ yathā cittaṃ jantorviṣayagocare ..
yadyevaṃ brahmaṇi nyastaṃ ko na mucyeta bandhanāt .. 1.17.40 ..
1.17.d:
समासक्तं यथा चित्तं जन्तोर्विषयगोचरे ॥
यद्येवं ब्रह्मणि न्यस्तं को न मुच्येत बन्धनात् ॥ 1.17.40 ॥
1.17.m: Just as a creature's mind is attached to sense objects, / if it were directed in that way toward Brahmā, who would not be released from bondage?

1.17.s:
khaṇḍasphuṭitasaṃskāraṃ śālāyāṃ yaḥ karoti vai ..
arāmāvasathādyeṣu labhate mauktikaṃ phalam .. 41 ..
1.17.d:
खण्डस्फुटितसंस्कारं शालायां यः करोति वै ॥
अरामावसथाद्येषु लभते मौक्तिकं फलम् ॥ 41 ॥
1.17.m: He who performs repairs of broken and cracked parts in the hall, / in groves, rest-houses, and the like, obtains the fruit of liberation.

1.17.s:
nāsti brahmasamo devo nāsti brahmasamo guruḥ ..
nāsti brahmasamaṃ jñānaṃ nāsti vedhaḥsamaṃ tapaḥ .. 42 ..
1.17.d:
नास्ति ब्रह्मसमो देवो नास्ति ब्रह्मसमो गुरुः ॥
नास्ति ब्रह्मसमं ज्ञानं नास्ति वेधःसमं तपः ॥ 42 ॥
1.17.m: There is no god equal to Brahmā; there is no guru equal to Brahmā; / there is no knowledge equal to Brahmā; there is no austerity equal to Brahmā.

1.17.s:
pratipadyādisarveṣu divaseṣūtsaveṣu ca ..
parvakāleṣu puṇye paurṇamāsyāṃ viśeṣataḥ .. 43 ..
1.17.d:
प्रतिपद्यादिसर्वेषु दिवसेषूत्सवेषु च ॥
पर्वकालेषु पुण्ये पौर्णमास्यां विशेषतः ॥ 43 ॥
1.17.m: On all days starting with the first lunar day, on festivals, / and on sacred juncture days, especially on the full moon,

1.17.s:
śaṃkhabheryādinirghoṣairmahadbhigeṃyasaṃyutaiḥ ..
kuryānnīrājanaṃ deve surajyeṣṭhe caturmukhe .. 44 ..
1.17.d:
शंखभेर्यादिनिर्घोषैर्महद्भिगेंयसंयुतैः ॥
कुर्यान्नीराजनं देवे सुरज्येष्ठे चतुर्मुखे ॥ 44 ॥
1.17.m: with great sounds of conches, kettledrums, and other instruments accompanied by singing, / one should perform the waving of lamps before the god, the eldest of the gods, the four-faced one.

1.17.s:
yāvatparvāṇi vidhinā kuryā nnīrājanaṃ nṛpa ..
tāvadyugasahasrāṇi brahmaloke mahīyate .. 45 ..
1.17.d:
यावत्पर्वाणि विधिना कुर्या न्नीराजनं नृप ॥
तावद्युगसहस्राणि ब्रह्मलोके महीयते ॥ 45 ॥
1.17.m: For as many juncture days as one performs the waving of lamps according to the ritual rules, O king, / for that many thousands of yugas he is glorified in the world of Brahmā.

1.17.s:
snānakāle trisaṃdhyaṃ tu yaḥ kuryānnṛtyavādanam ..
gītaṃ vā mukhavādyaṃ vā tasya puṇya phalaṃ śṛṇu .. 46 ..
1.17.d:
स्नानकाले त्रिसंध्यं तु यः कुर्यान्नृत्यवादनम् ॥
गीतं वा मुखवाद्यं वा तस्य पुण्य फलं शृणु ॥ 46 ॥
1.17.m: Hear the meritorious fruit of him who performs dance and instrumental music / or singing or mouth-music at the bath time at the three junctures of the day:

1.17.s:
yāvantyahāni kurute geyanṛtyādivādanam ..
tāvadyugasahasrāṇi brahmaloke mahīyate .. 47 ..
1.17.d:
यावन्त्यहानि कुरुते गेयनृत्यादिवादनम् ॥
तावद्युगसहस्राणि ब्रह्मलोके महीयते ॥ 47 ॥
1.17.m: For as many days as he performs singing, dance, and instrumental music, / for that many thousands of yugas he is glorified in the world of Brahmā.

1.17.s:
kapilāpañcagavyena kuśavāriyutena ca ..
snāpayenmaṃtrapūtena brāhmaṃ snānaṃ hi tatsmṛtam .. 48 ..
1.17.d:
कपिलापञ्चगव्येन कुशवारियुतेन च ॥
स्नापयेन्मंत्रपूतेन ब्राह्मं स्नानं हि तत्स्मृतम् ॥ 48 ॥
1.17.m: One should bathe [him] with the five bovine products of a brown cow along with kuśa grass and water, / purified by mantras; that is recalled as the bath of Brahmā.

1.17.s:
kapilāpaṃcagavyena dadhikṣīraghṛtena ca ..
snānaṃ śataguṇaṃ jñeyamitareṣāṃ narādhipa .. 49 ..
1.17.d:
कपिलापंचगव्येन दधिक्षीरघृतेन च ॥
स्नानं शतगुणं ज्ञेयमितरेषां नराधिप ॥ 49 ॥
1.17.m: The bath with the five bovine products of a brown cow, with curd, milk, and clarified butter, / should be known to be a hundred times superior to those of others, O ruler of men.

1.17.s:
devāgnikāryamuddiśya kapilāmāharetsadā ..
brahmakṣatraviśaścaiva na śūdrastu kadācana .. 1.17.50 ..
1.17.d:
देवाग्निकार्यमुद्दिश्य कपिलामाहरेत्सदा ॥
ब्रह्मक्षत्रविशश्चैव न शूद्रस्तु कदाचन ॥ 1.17.50 ॥
1.17.m: One should always acquire a brown cow for the purpose of the rites of the gods and fire; / brāhmaṇas, kṣatriyas, and vaiśyas may do so, but a śūdra never.

1.17.s:
kāpilaṃ yaḥ pibecchūdro devakāryārthanirmitam ..
sa pacyeta mahāghore suciraṃ narakārṇave .. 51 ..
1.17.d:
कापिलं यः पिबेच्छूद्रो देवकार्यार्थनिर्मितम् ॥
स पच्येत महाघोरे सुचिरं नरकार्णवे ॥ 51 ॥
1.17.m: A śūdra who drinks [the milk] of a brown cow designated for the purpose of the rites of the gods / will boil for a very long time in a terrifying ocean of hell.

1.17.s:
varṣakoṭisahasraistu yatpāpaṃ samupārjitam ..
surajyeṣṭhaghṛtābhyaṃgāddahetsarvaṃ na saṃśayaḥ .. 52 ..
1.17.d:
वर्षकोटिसहस्रैस्तु यत्पापं समुपार्जितम् ॥
सुरज्येष्ठघृताभ्यंगाद्दहेत्सर्वं न संशयः ॥ 52 ॥
1.17.m: Whatever sin has been accumulated over thousands of crores of years, / from anointing the eldest of the gods with clarified butter, he burns it all, without doubt.

1.17.s:
kalpakoṭisahasraistu yatpāpaṃ samupārjitam ..
pitāmahaghṛtasnānaṃ dahatyagniriveṃdhanam.53..
1.17.d:
कल्पकोटिसहस्रैस्तु यत्पापं समुपार्जितम् ॥
पितामहघृतस्नानं दहत्यग्निरिवेंधनम्.53॥
1.17.m: Whatever sin has been accumulated over thousands of crores of kalpas, / bathing the Grandfather with clarified butter burns it as fire burns fuel.

1.17.s:
ghṛtasnānaṃ pratipadi sakṛtkṛtvā tu kāṃjajam ..
kulaikaviṃśamuttārya viṣṇuloke mahī yate ..54..
1.17.d:
घृतस्नानं प्रतिपदि सकृत्कृत्वा तु कांजजम् ॥
कुलैकविंशमुत्तार्य विष्णुलोके मही यते ॥54॥
1.17.m: Having once performed the bath with clarified butter for the Lotus-Born [Brahmā] on the first lunar day, / having delivered twenty-one generations, he is glorified in the world of Viṣṇu.

1.17.s:
ayutaṃ yo gavāṃ dadyādbhaktyā vai vedapārage ..
vastrahemādiyuktānāṃ kṣīrasnānena yatphalam ..55..
1.17.d:
अयुतं यो गवां दद्याद्भक्त्या वै वेदपारगे ॥
वस्त्रहेमादियुक्तानां क्षीरस्नानेन यत्फलम् ॥55॥
1.17.m: The fruit that one obtains who gives ten thousand cows with devotion to a master of the Vedas, / endowed with garments, gold, and the like, is gained by a bath with milk.

1.17.s:
sakṛdājyena payasā snapayettu yaḥ ..
gāṃgeyena sa yānena yāti brahmasalokatām .. 56 ..
1.17.d:
सकृदाज्येन पयसा स्नपयेत्तु यः ॥
गांगेयेन स यानेन याति ब्रह्मसलोकताम् ॥ 56 ॥
1.17.m: He who bathes [him] once with clarified butter and with milk / goes in a golden vehicle to dwelling in the same world as Brahmā.

1.17.s:
snāpya dadhnā sakṛdvīra kañjajaṃ viṣṇumāpnuyāt ..
madhunā snapayitvā tu vīraloke mahīyate .. 57 ..
1.17.d:
स्नाप्य दध्ना सकृद्वीर कञ्जजं विष्णुमाप्नुयात् ॥
मधुना स्नपयित्वा तु वीरलोके महीयते ॥ 57 ॥
1.17.m: Having bathed the Lotus-Born [Brahmā] once with curd, O hero, one attains Viṣṇu; / and having bathed [him] with honey, he is glorified in the world of heroes.

1.17.s:
snānamikṣuraseneha yo viriṃceḥ samācaret ..
sa yāti lokaṃ savitastu tejasā bhāsayannabhaḥ .. 58 ..
1.17.d:
स्नानमिक्षुरसेनेह यो विरिंचेः समाचरेत् ॥
स याति लोकं सवितस्तु तेजसा भासयन्नभः ॥ 58 ॥
1.17.m: He who performs here the bathing of Viriñci with sugarcane juice / goes to the realm of Savitṛ, illuminating the firmament with his splendour.

1.17.s:
śuddhodakena yo bhaktyā snāpayetpadmasaṃbhavam ..
utsṛjya pāpakalilaṃ sa yātyeva salokatām .. 59 ..
1.17.d:
शुद्धोदकेन यो भक्त्या स्नापयेत्पद्मसंभवम् ॥
उत्सृज्य पापकलिलं स यात्येव सलोकताम् ॥ 59 ॥
1.17.m: He who bathes the Lotus-born with pure water through devotion, / casting off the stain of sin, he indeed attains companionship with him in his realm.

1.17.s:
vastrapūtena toyena snapayedyaḥ sakṛdvibhum ..
sa sarvakālaṃ tṛptātmā lokavaśyatvamā pnuyāt .. 1.17.60 ..
1.17.d:
वस्त्रपूतेन तोयेन स्नपयेद्यः सकृद्विभुम् ॥
स सर्वकालं तृप्तात्मा लोकवश्यत्वमा प्नुयात् ॥ 1.17.60 ॥
1.17.m: He who bathes the all-pervading Lord even once with water purified by cloth, / having his soul ever satisfied, attains mastery over the world.

1.17.s:
sarvauṣadhībhiryo bhaktyā snapayetpadmasaṃbhavam ..
kāṃcanena vimānena brahmaloke mahīyate .. 61 ..
1.17.d:
सर्वौषधीभिर्यो भक्त्या स्नपयेत्पद्मसंभवम् ॥
कांचनेन विमानेन ब्रह्मलोके महीयते ॥ 61 ॥
1.17.m: He who bathes the Lotus-born through devotion with all medicinal herbs / is honoured in the realm of Brahmā by means of a golden celestial chariot.

1.17.s:
gandhacandanatoyena snāpayedyoṃbujodbhavam ..
rudralokamavāpnoti tejasā hemasannibhaḥ .. 62 ..
1.17.d:
गन्धचन्दनतोयेन स्नापयेद्योंबुजोद्भवम् ॥
रुद्रलोकमवाप्नोति तेजसा हेमसन्निभः ॥ 62 ॥
1.17.m: He who bathes the Lotus-born with water [scented with] perfume and sandalwood / attains the realm of Rudra, resembling gold in splendour.

1.17.s:
pāṭalotpalapadmāni karavīrāṇi sarvadā ..
snānakāle prayojyāni sthirāṇi surabhīṇi ca .. 63 ..
1.17.d:
पाटलोत्पलपद्मानि करवीराणि सर्वदा ॥
स्नानकाले प्रयोज्यानि स्थिराणि सुरभीणि च ॥ 63 ॥
1.17.m: Pāṭala blossoms, blue water-lilies, lotuses, and oleanders, / enduring and fragrant, should always be employed at the time of bathing.

1.17.s:
eṣāmekatamaṃ snānaṃ bhaktyā kṛtvā tu vedhasi ..
vidhūya pāpakalilaṃ vidhiloke mahīyate .. 64 ..
1.17.d:
एषामेकतमं स्नानं भक्त्या कृत्वा तु वेधसि ॥
विधूय पापकलिलं विधिलोके महीयते ॥ 64 ॥
1.17.m: Having performed even one of these baths for the Creator with devotion, / shaking off the stain of sin, one is honoured in the realm of the Creator.

1.17.s:
karpūrāgarutoyena snapayedyastu kañjajam ..
sarvapāpaviśuddhātmā brahmaloke mahīyate .. 65 ..
1.17.d:
कर्पूरागरुतोयेन स्नपयेद्यस्तु कञ्जजम् ॥
सर्वपापविशुद्धात्मा ब्रह्मलोके महीयते ॥ 65 ॥
1.17.m: He who bathes the Lotus-born with water [scented with] camphor and agallochum, / his soul purified of all sins, is honoured in the realm of Brahmā.

1.17.s:
gāyatrīśatajaptena vimalenāṃbhasā vibhum ..
snapayitvā sakṛdbhaktyā brahmalokamavā pnuyāt .. 66 ..
1.17.d:
गायत्रीशतजप्तेन विमलेनांभसा विभुम् ॥
स्नपयित्वा सकृद्भक्त्या ब्रह्मलोकमवा प्नुयात् ॥ 66 ॥
1.17.m: Having bathed the all-pervading Lord once through devotion with pure water / over which the Gāyatrī has been recited a hundred times, one attains the realm of Brahmā.

1.17.s:
vibhuṃ śītāṃbunā snāpya dhāroṣṇapayasā tataḥ ..
tataḥ paścād ghṛtasnānaṃ kṛtvā pāpairvimucyate .. 67 ..
1.17.d:
विभुं शीतांबुना स्नाप्य धारोष्णपयसा ततः ॥
ततः पश्चाद् घृतस्नानं कृत्वा पापैर्विमुच्यते ॥ 67 ॥
1.17.m: Having bathed the all-pervading Lord with cold water, then with warm milk fresh from the udder, / and after that having performed a bath with clarified butter, one is freed from sins.

1.17.s:
etatsnānatrayaṃ kṛtvā pūjayitvā tu bhaktitaḥ ..
aśvamedhasahasrasya phalaṃ prāpnoti mānavaḥ .. 68 ..
1.17.d:
एतत्स्नानत्रयं कृत्वा पूजयित्वा तु भक्तितः ॥
अश्वमेधसहस्रस्य फलं प्राप्नोति मानवः ॥ 68 ॥
1.17.m: Having performed this threefold bath and worshipped him with devotion, / a man obtains the fruit of a thousand horse sacrifices.

1.17.s:
mṛtkuṃbhaistāmrajaiḥ kuṃbhaiḥ snānaṃ śataguṇaṃ bhavet ..
raupye lakṣottaraṃ proktaṃ haimaiḥ koṭiguṇaṃ bhavet .. 69 ..
1.17.d:
मृत्कुंभैस्ताम्रजैः कुंभैः स्नानं शतगुणं भवेत् ॥
रौप्ये लक्षोत्तरं प्रोक्तं हैमैः कोटिगुणं भवेत् ॥ 69 ॥
1.17.m: With pots made of copper rather than earthen pots, the bath yields a hundredfold [fruit]; / in a silver [pot] it is declared to be a hundred thousand times more, and with golden ones it becomes ten million times as much.

1.17.s:
brahmaṇo darśanaṃ puṇyaṃ darśanātsparśanaṃ param ..
sparśanādarcanaṃ śreṣṭhaṃ ghṛtasnātamataḥ param .. 1.17.70 ..
1.17.d:
ब्रह्मणो दर्शनं पुण्यं दर्शनात्स्पर्शनं परम् ॥
स्पर्शनादर्चनं श्रेष्ठं घृतस्नातमतः परम् ॥ 1.17.70 ॥
1.17.m: The sight of Brahmā is meritorious; touch is superior to sight; / worship is better than touch; superior even to that is [the sight of] him bathed in clarified butter.

1.17.s:
vācikaṃ mānasaṃ pāpaṃ ghṛtasnānena dehinām ..
kṣiṇute padmajo yasmāttasmātsnānaṃ samācaret .. 71 ..
1.17.d:
वाचिकं मानसं पापं घृतस्नानेन देहिनाम् ॥
क्षिणुते पद्मजो यस्मात्तस्मात्स्नानं समाचरेत् ॥ 71 ॥
1.17.m: Since the Lotus-born destroys the vocal and mental sin / of embodied beings through the bath of clarified butter, therefore one should perform that bath.

1.17.s:
snapayitvārcayedbhaktyā yathā tacchṛṇu bhārata ..
śucivastradharaḥ snātaḥ kṛtanyāsaśca bhārata .. 72 ..
1.17.d:
स्नपयित्वार्चयेद्भक्त्या यथा तच्छृणु भारत ॥
शुचिवस्त्रधरः स्नातः कृतन्यासश्च भारत ॥ 72 ॥
1.17.m: Having bathed him, how one should worship him with devotion—hear that, O descendant of Bharata: / wearing clean garments, having bathed, and having performed the placement of mantras, O descendant of Bharata,

1.17.s:
caturhastaṃ likhetpadmaṃ caturbhāgavibhāgitam ..
madhye tasya likheccakraṃ dalairdvādaśabhiścitam .. 73 ..
1.17.d:
चतुर्हस्तं लिखेत्पद्मं चतुर्भागविभागितम् ॥
मध्ये तस्य लिखेच्चक्रं दलैर्द्वादशभिश्चितम् ॥ 73 ॥
1.17.m: one should draw a four-cubit lotus divided into four parts; / in its centre one should draw a wheel adorned with twelve petals.

1.17.s:
sarojāni tato nyasya akṣarāṇi samantataḥ ..
akṣaraṃ vihitaṃ cānyatpatrabhāge prakīrtitam .. 74 ..
1.17.d:
सरोजानि ततो न्यस्य अक्षराणि समन्ततः ॥
अक्षरं विहितं चान्यत्पत्रभागे प्रकीर्तितम् ॥ 74 ॥
1.17.m: Then, having placed lotuses, [one deposits] syllables all around; / and another syllable is prescribed and taught on the petal-portion.

1.17.s:
nānāvarṇakasaṃyogāllikheccaivānupūrvaśaḥ ..
kṛṣṇotkaṭaṃ tu madhyaṃ syātpītaraktaṃ tathā param .. 75 ..
1.17.d:
नानावर्णकसंयोगाल्लिखेच्चैवानुपूर्वशः ॥
कृष्णोत्कटं तु मध्यं स्यात्पीतरक्तं तथा परम् ॥ 75 ॥
1.17.m: One should draw it successively with a combination of various colours: / the centre should be predominantly black, and the outer part yellow and red.

1.17.s:
sitaṃ śuddhaṃ tu karttavyaṃ madhyabhāge tu vartulam ..
prabhākuṇḍalakairbāhyairveṣṭayeccakranāyakam ..76..
1.17.d:
सितं शुद्धं तु कर्त्तव्यं मध्यभागे तु वर्तुलम् ॥
प्रभाकुण्डलकैर्बाह्यैर्वेष्टयेच्चक्रनायकम् ॥76॥
1.17.m: In the central part a pure white circle should be made; / one should surround the lord of wheels with outer circles of radiance.

1.17.s:
evamālikhya yatnena mūlamantraṃ tato nyaset ..
mūrdhnaḥ pādatalaṃ yāvatpraṇavaṃ vinyasedbudhaḥ .. 77 ..
1.17.d:
एवमालिख्य यत्नेन मूलमन्त्रं ततो न्यसेत् ॥
मूर्ध्नः पादतलं यावत्प्रणवं विन्यसेद्बुधः ॥ 77 ॥
1.17.m: Having drawn it thus with care, the wise man should then place the root mantra; / he should deposit the Praṇava from the crown of the head down to the soles of the feet.

1.17.s:
nādarūpaṃ nyasettāvadyāvacchabdasya śūnyatā ..
tatkāraṃ vinyasenmūrdhni sakāraṃ mukhamaṇḍale .. 78 ..
1.17.d:
नादरूपं न्यसेत्तावद्यावच्छब्दस्य शून्यता ॥
तत्कारं विन्यसेन्मूर्ध्नि सकारं मुखमण्डले ॥ 78 ॥
1.17.m: He should deposit it in the form of sound until the silence of the sound [is reached]. / He should place the syllable 'tat' on the crown of the head, and the syllable 'sa' on the circle of the face,

1.17.s:
vikāraṃ kaṇṭhadeśe tu tukāraṃ sarvasaṃdhiṣu ..
vakāraṃ hṛdi madhye tu rekāraṃ pārśvayordvayoḥ .. 79 ..
1.17.d:
विकारं कण्ठदेशे तु तुकारं सर्वसंधिषु ॥
वकारं हृदि मध्ये तु रेकारं पार्श्वयोर्द्वयोः ॥ 79 ॥
1.17.m: the syllable 'vi' in the throat region, and the syllable 'tu' in all the joints; / the syllable 'va' in the middle of the heart, and the syllable 're' on the two flanks;

1.17.s:
ṇakāraṃ dakṣiṇe kukṣau yakāraṃ vāmasaṃjñake ..
bhakāraṃ kaṭinābhisthaṃ rgokāraṃ jānuparvasu .. 1.17.80 ..
1.17.d:
णकारं दक्षिणे कुक्षौ यकारं वामसंज्ञके ॥
भकारं कटिनाभिस्थं र्गोकारं जानुपर्वसु ॥ 1.17.80 ॥
1.17.m: the syllable 'ṇa' in the right side of the belly, and the syllable 'ya' in that known as the left; / the syllable 'bha' situated at the waist and navel, and the syllable 'rgo' in the joints of the knees;

1.17.s:
dekāraṃ jaṃghayornyasya vakāraṃ pādapadmayoḥ ..
syakāramaṃguṣṭhayornyasya dhīkāraṃ corasi nyaset .. 81 ..
1.17.d:
देकारं जंघयोर्न्यस्य वकारं पादपद्मयोः ॥
स्यकारमंगुष्ठयोर्न्यस्य धीकारं चोरसि न्यसेत् ॥ 81 ॥
1.17.m: having placed the syllable 'de' on the two shanks, and the syllable 'va' on the two lotus-feet; / having placed the syllable 'sya' on the two thumbs, he should place the syllable 'dhī' on the chest;

1.17.s:
makāraṃ jānudeśe tu hikāraṃ guhyamāśritam ..
dhikāraṃ hṛdaye nyasya yokāraṃ cauṣṭhayo rnyaset .. 82 ..
1.17.d:
मकारं जानुदेशे तु हिकारं गुह्यमाश्रितम् ॥
धिकारं हृदये न्यस्य योकारं चौष्ठयो र्न्यसेत् ॥ 82 ॥
1.17.m: the syllable 'ma' in the region of the knees, and the syllable 'hi' resting on the private parts; / having placed the syllable 'dhi' on the heart, he should place the syllable 'yo' on the lips;

1.17.s:
nakāraṃ nāsikāgre tu prakāraṃ netramāśritam ..
cokāraṃ tu bhuvormadhye dakāraṃ prāṇamāśritam .. 83 ..
1.17.d:
नकारं नासिकाग्रे तु प्रकारं नेत्रमाश्रितम् ॥
चोकारं तु भुवोर्मध्ये दकारं प्राणमाश्रितम् ॥ 83 ॥
1.17.m: the syllable 'na' on the tip of the nose, and the syllable 'pra' resting on the eyes; / the syllable 'co' between the eyebrows, and the syllable 'da' resting on the breath;

1.17.s:
yākāraṃ vinyasenmūrdhni takāraṃ keśamāśritam ..
nyāsaṃ kṛtvātmano dehe deve kuryāttathā nṛpa ..
sarvopacārasaṃpannaṃ kṛtvā samyaṅ nirīkṣayet .. 84 ..
1.17.d:
याकारं विन्यसेन्मूर्ध्नि तकारं केशमाश्रितम् ॥
न्यासं कृत्वात्मनो देहे देवे कुर्यात्तथा नृप ॥
सर्वोपचारसंपन्नं कृत्वा सम्यङ् निरीक्षयेत् ॥ 84 ॥
1.17.m: he should place the syllable 'yā' on the crown of the head, and the syllable 'ta' resting on the hair. / Having performed the placement of mantras on his own body, he should likewise do so on the god, O king; / having rendered it complete with all rites of attendance, he should inspect it properly.

1.17.s:
kuṃkumāgurukarpūra candanena vimiśritam ..
gandhatoyamupaskṛtya gāyatryā praṇavena ca ..
prokṣayetsarvadravyāṇi paścādarcanamācaret .. 85 ..
1.17.d:
कुंकुमागुरुकर्पूर चन्दनेन विमिश्रितम् ॥
गन्धतोयमुपस्कृत्य गायत्र्या प्रणवेन च ॥
प्रोक्षयेत्सर्वद्रव्याणि पश्चादर्चनमाचरेत् ॥ 85 ॥
1.17.m: Having prepared scented water mixed with saffron, agallochum, camphor, / and sandalwood, with the Gāyatrī and the Praṇava / he should sprinkle all the substances, and afterwards perform the worship.

1.17.s:
cakragranthiṣu sarvāsu praṇavaṃ viniveśayet ..
bhūyaḥ plutaṃ samuccārya praṇavaṃ sarvatomukham .. 86 ..
1.17.d:
चक्रग्रन्थिषु सर्वासु प्रणवं विनिवेशयेत् ॥
भूयः प्लुतं समुच्चार्य प्रणवं सर्वतोमुखम् ॥ 86 ॥
1.17.m: He should deposit the Praṇava at all the junctures of the wheel; / having again uttered the protractedly accented Praṇava facing in all directions,

1.17.s:
vinyasetpadmamadhye tu pīṭhaniṣpattihetave ..
āsane pṛthivī jñeyā sarvasattvadharā matā .. 87 ..
1.17.d:
विन्यसेत्पद्ममध्ये तु पीठनिष्पत्तिहेतवे ॥
आसने पृथिवी ज्ञेया सर्वसत्त्वधरा मता ॥ 87 ॥
1.17.m: he should deposit it in the centre of the lotus to establish the seat. / The earth is to be understood in the seat, considered as supporting all beings.

1.17.s:
hrasvoṃkāre matā sā tu dīrghoṃkāre tu devarāṭ ..
plutastu vyāpayedbhāvaṃ mokṣadaṃ cāmṛtātmakam .. 88 ..
1.17.d:
ह्रस्वोंकारे मता सा तु दीर्घोंकारे तु देवराट् ॥
प्लुतस्तु व्यापयेद्भावं मोक्षदं चामृतात्मकम् ॥ 88 ॥
1.17.m: She is considered to be in the short Oṃkāra, while the king of gods is in the long Oṃkāra; / and the protractedly accented [Oṃkāra] pervades the state that grants liberation and consists of nectar.

1.17.s:
yatnastho na nivarteta yogī prāṇaparāyaṇaḥ ..
āvāhanaṃ tataḥ kuryādakṣareṇa pareṇa tu .. 89 ..
1.17.d:
यत्नस्थो न निवर्तेत योगी प्राणपरायणः ॥
आवाहनं ततः कुर्यादक्षरेण परेण तु ॥ 89 ॥
1.17.m: Standing steadfast in exertion, the yogin devoted to the vital breaths should not turn back. / Then he should perform the invocation with the supreme syllable.

1.17.s:
āvāhya tejorūpaṃ tu nyasenmantravarāṃstataḥ ..
tato vibhāvayeddevaṃ padmasthaṃ caturānanam..1.17.90..
1.17.d:
आवाह्य तेजोरूपं तु न्यसेन्मन्त्रवरांस्ततः ॥
ततो विभावयेद्देवं पद्मस्थं चतुराननम्॥1.17.90॥
1.17.m: Having invoked him in the form of splendour, he should then deposit the excellent mantras; / then he should meditate upon the four-faced god seated upon the lotus,

1.17.s:
sraṣṭāraṃ sarvajagatāṃ viṣṇurudravidhānagam..
saṃbhāvya gandhapuṣpādi saṃbhārānkramātsarvānprakalpayet..
gāyatrīmuccaranmantraṃ sarvakarmāṇi kārayet..92..
1.17.d:
स्रष्टारं सर्वजगतां विष्णुरुद्रविधानगम्॥
संभाव्य गन्धपुष्पादि संभारान्क्रमात्सर्वान्प्रकल्पयेत्॥
गायत्रीमुच्चरन्मन्त्रं सर्वकर्माणि कारयेत्॥92॥
1.17.m: the creator of all worlds, who attends to the ordainment of Viṣṇu and Rudra. / Having meditated on him, he should arrange all the requisites in order, such as scents and flowers; / uttering the Gāyatrī mantra, he should cause all the rites to be performed.

1.17.s:
puṣpaṃ dhūpaṃ tathā dīpaṃ naivedyaṃ sumanoharam..
khaṃḍalaḍḍukaśrīveṣṭakāsārāśokavartikāḥ..93..
1.17.d:
पुष्पं धूपं तथा दीपं नैवेद्यं सुमनोहरम्॥
खंडलड्डुकश्रीवेष्टकासाराशोकवर्तिकाः॥93॥
1.17.m: Flowers, incense, likewise a lamp, and very delightful food offerings: / sugar candy, laḍḍus, śrīveṣṭa pastries, kāsāra, aśokavartikās,

1.17.s:
svastikollopikādugdhatilāveṣṭatilāḍhikāḥ..
phalāni caiva pakvāni lagnakhaṇḍaguḍāni ca..94..
1.17.d:
स्वस्तिकोल्लोपिकादुग्धतिलावेष्टतिलाढिकाः॥
फलानि चैव पक्वानि लग्नखण्डगुडानि च॥94॥
1.17.m: svastika pastries, ullopikās, milk, tilāveṣṭas, pastries rich in sesame, / and ripe fruits, along with lumps of crystallized sugar and jaggery.

1.17.s:
anyāṃśca vividhāndadyātpūpāni vividhāni ca..
evamādīni sarvāṇi dāpayecachaktito nṛpa..95..
1.17.d:
अन्यांश्च विविधान्दद्यात्पूपानि विविधानि च॥
एवमादीनि सर्वाणि दापयेचछक्तितो नृप॥95॥
1.17.m: He should present other various cakes and different kinds of delicacies; / O king, he should cause all these and more to be offered according to his means.

1.17.s:
mūlamantreṇa devasya tato dehaṃ vibhāvayet ..
pūjayeccāpi vidhinā yena taṃ te bravīmyaham .. 96 ..
1.17.d:
मूलमन्त्रेण देवस्य ततो देहं विभावयेत् ॥
पूजयेच्चापि विधिना येन तं ते ब्रवीम्यहम् ॥ 96 ॥
1.17.m: Then with the root mantra he should meditate upon the body of the god, / and he should also worship him according to rule; I shall declare that to you.

1.17.s:
prāṇāyāmatrayaṃ kṛtvā dehasaṃśodhanāya vai ..
āvāhayettatonantaṃ dhārayantaṃ vacaḥ sadā .. 97 ..
1.17.d:
प्राणायामत्रयं कृत्वा देहसंशोधनाय वै ॥
आवाहयेत्ततोनन्तं धारयन्तं वचः सदा ॥ 97 ॥
1.17.m: Having performed three breath controls for the purification of the body, / he should then invoke Ananta, who ever maintains the word;

1.17.s:
dhyātvānantaṃ tato rudraṃ padmakiṃjalkamadhyagam ..
dhyāyedviṣṇuṃ tato devaṃ nyasetpadmodarodbhavam .. 98 ..
1.17.d:
ध्यात्वानन्तं ततो रुद्रं पद्मकिंजल्कमध्यगम् ॥
ध्यायेद्विष्णुं ततो देवं न्यसेत्पद्मोदरोद्भवम् ॥ 98 ॥
1.17.m: having meditated on Ananta, then on Rudra situated in the middle of the filaments of the lotus, / he should then meditate on the god Viṣṇu, and should place the one born from the interior of the lotus.

1.17.s:
evaṃ tridevatārūḍhaṃ padmamadhyeṃbujodbhavam ..
pūjayenmūlamantreṇa padmodarabhavaṃ nṛpa .. 99 ..
1.17.d:
एवं त्रिदेवतारूढं पद्ममध्येंबुजोद्भवम् ॥
पूजयेन्मूलमन्त्रेण पद्मोदरभवं नृप ॥ 99 ॥
1.17.m: Thus, upon the Lotus-born mounted upon the three deities in the middle of the lotus, / born from the interior of the lotus, he should bestow worship with the root mantra, O king.

1.17.s:
ṛgvedaṃ tu yajurvedaṃ sāmavedaṃ ca pūjayet ..
jñānavairāgyamaiśvaryaṃ dharmaṃ saṃpūjayedbudhaḥ .. 1.17.100 ..
1.17.d:
ऋग्वेदं तु यजुर्वेदं सामवेदं च पूजयेत् ॥
ज्ञानवैराग्यमैश्वर्यं धर्मं संपूजयेद्बुधः ॥ 1.17.100 ॥
1.17.m: The wise man should worship the Ṛgveda, the Yajurveda, and the Sāmaveda; / he should thoroughly worship wisdom, dispassion, sovereignty, and righteousness,

1.17.s:
īśānādikramādrājanvidiśāsu samaṃtataḥ ..
śikṣā kalpo vyākaraṇaṃ niruktaṃ chanda eva ca .. 101 ..
1.17.d:
ईशानादिक्रमाद्राजन्विदिशासु समंततः ॥
शिक्षा कल्पो व्याकरणं निरुक्तं छन्द एव च ॥ 101 ॥
1.17.m: in the intermediate directions all around in order beginning with the north-east, O king: / phonetics, ritual procedure, grammar, etymology, and metrics.

1.17.s:
jyotiṣaṃ ca mahābāho upavedāśca kṛtsnaśaḥ ..
itihāsapurāṇāni yathāyogyaṃ yathākramam .. 102 ..
1.17.d:
ज्योतिषं च महाबाहो उपवेदाश्च कृत्स्नशः ॥
इतिहासपुराणानि यथायोग्यं यथाक्रमम् ॥ 102 ॥
1.17.m: And astronomy, O mighty-armed one, and all the Upavedas in their entirety, / the Itihāsas and the Purāṇas, properly and in due order.

1.17.s:
śikṣā kalpo vyākaraṇaṃ devasya purataḥ sadā ..
kalpādayastataścānye diśāsu vidiśāsu ca..103..
1.17.d:
शिक्षा कल्पो व्याकरणं देवस्य पुरतः सदा ॥
कल्पादयस्ततश्चान्ये दिशासु विदिशासु च॥103॥
1.17.m: Phonetics, ritual, and grammar should always be placed in front of the god; / then ritual and the others, in the cardinal directions and intermediate directions.

1.17.s:
mahāvyāhṛtayaḥ sarvāḥ praṇavena samanvitāḥ..
pūrvādikramayogena pūjayedvidhinā nṛpa.. 104..
1.17.d:
महाव्याहृतयः सर्वाः प्रणवेन समन्विताः॥
पूर्वादिक्रमयोगेन पूजयेद्विधिना नृप॥ 104॥
1.17.m: All the great vyāhṛtis joined with the praṇava / one should worship according to the rite in order starting from the east, O king.

1.17.s:
śaktayo brahmaṇastvetā lokarūpā vyavasthitāḥ..
pūjanīyāḥ prayatnena maṃtrarūpāḥ sthitāḥ svayam..105..
1.17.d:
शक्तयो ब्रह्मणस्त्वेता लोकरूपा व्यवस्थिताः॥
पूजनीयाः प्रयत्नेन मंत्ररूपाः स्थिताः स्वयम्॥105॥
1.17.m: These are indeed the powers of Brahmā, established in the form of the worlds; / they should be worshipped with diligence, standing by themselves in the form of mantras.

1.17.s:
arakāṃtarasaṃsthāṃśca ṣaṭ samudrānsamarcayet ..
nakṣatrāṇi grahāścaiva rāśayaśca viśeṣataḥ . .
pūjyāḥ sarve yathānyāyaṃ surāgreṣu vyavasthitāḥ . . 106 ..
1.17.d:
अरकांतरसंस्थांश्च षट् समुद्रान्समर्चयेत् ॥
नक्षत्राणि ग्रहाश्चैव राशयश्च विशेषतः ॥
पूज्याः सर्वे यथान्यायं सुराग्रेषु व्यवस्थिताः ॥ 106 ॥
1.17.m: And one should worship the six oceans situated in the spaces between the spokes, / especially the constellations, the planets, and the zodiac signs. / All should be worshipped properly, positioned in front of the gods.

1.17.s:
nāgāśca garuḍaścaiva pūjanīyastathāgrataḥ ..
devatā ṛṣayaścaiva sahitāḥ kulaparvatāḥ ..
tattejonilayāḥ sarve pūjanīyāḥ prayatnataḥ .. 107 ..
1.17.d:
नागाश्च गरुडश्चैव पूजनीयस्तथाग्रतः ॥
देवता ऋषयश्चैव सहिताः कुलपर्वताः ॥
तत्तेजोनिलयाः सर्वे पूजनीयाः प्रयत्नतः ॥ 107 ॥
1.17.m: And the serpents and Garuḍa must likewise be worshipped in front; / the deities, the sages together with the principal mountain ranges— / all abiding in his brilliance—must be worshipped with diligence.

1.17.s:
ācamya vidhivatpūrvaṃ maṃtrapūtena vāriṇā ..
hṛdayādīnnyasedaṃgānhṛdayādiṣu kṛtsnaśaḥ . . 108 . .
1.17.d:
आचम्य विधिवत्पूर्वं मंत्रपूतेन वारिणा ॥
हृदयादीन्न्यसेदंगान्हृदयादिषु कृत्स्नशः ॥ 108 ॥
1.17.m: Having first sipped water according to rule with mantra-purified water, / one should completely install the limbs, such as the heart, on the heart and other [parts of the body].

1.17.s:
śikhā netraṃ tathā carma astraṃ ca bharatarṣabha . .
maheṃdrādidiśaścaitāḥ pūjayedvidhivannṛpa . . 109 . .
1.17.d:
शिखा नेत्रं तथा चर्म अस्त्रं च भरतर्षभ ॥
महेंद्रादिदिशश्चैताः पूजयेद्विधिवन्नृप ॥ 109 ॥
1.17.m: The tuft, the eye, and likewise the armor and weapon, O bull of the Bharatas; / and one should worship these directions of Mahendra and the rest according to rule, O king.

1.17.s:
hṛdayaṃ purataḥ pūjyaṃ śiro devasya pṛṣṭhataḥ ..
pūrvaṃ saṃpūjayeddevaṃ mūlamaṃtreṇa kṛtsnaśaḥ . . 1.17.110 ..
1.17.d:
हृदयं पुरतः पूज्यं शिरो देवस्य पृष्ठतः ॥
पूर्वं संपूजयेद्देवं मूलमंत्रेण कृत्स्नशः ॥ 1.17.110 ॥
1.17.m: The heart should be worshipped in front, the head at the back of the god; / one should first worship the god completely with the root mantra.

1.17.s:
visarjayeddarśayitvā mudrāṃ tu bharatarṣabha . .
aṃkuśaṃ naraśārdūla hyāhvāne kaṃjamādiśet .. 111 . .
1.17.d:
विसर्जयेद्दर्शयित्वा मुद्रां तु भरतर्षभ ॥
अंकुशं नरशार्दूल ह्याह्वाने कंजमादिशेत् ॥ 111 ॥
1.17.m: Having displayed the mudrā, O bull of the Bharatas, he should perform the dismissal; / O tiger among men, he should indicate the goad and the lotus at the invocation.

1.17.s:
yastvevaṃ pūjayeddevaṃ pratipannityameva ca . .
upoṣya paṃcadaśyāṃ tu sa yāti paramaṃ padam .. 112 ..
1.17.d:
यस्त्वेवं पूजयेद्देवं प्रतिपन्नित्यमेव च ॥
उपोष्य पंचदश्यां तु स याति परमं पदम् ॥ 112 ॥
1.17.m: Whoever thus worships the god constantly on the pratipad, / having fasted on the fifteenth [day], he goes to the supreme abode.

1.17.s:
.. sumaṃtu ruvāca . . . .
āpo hiṣṭheti maṃtro'yaṃ hṛdayaṃ parikīrtitam . .
ṛtaṃ satyaṃ śikhā proktā udutyaṃ netramādiśet . . 113 ..
1.17.d:
॥ सुमंतु रुवाच ॥ ॥
आपो हिष्ठेति मंत्रोऽयं हृदयं परिकीर्तितम् ॥
ऋतं सत्यं शिखा प्रोक्ता उदुत्यं नेत्रमादिशेत् ॥ 113 ॥
1.17.m: Sumantu said: / The mantra 'āpo hi ṣṭha' is proclaimed as the heart; / 'ṛtaṃ satyam' is taught as the tuft; 'ud utyam' one should assign as the eye.

1.17.s:
citraṃ devānāṃ mastamiti sarvalokeṣu viśrutam . .
varmaṇā te cchādayāmi kavacaṃ samudāhṛtam . . 114 . .
1.17.d:
चित्रं देवानां मस्तमिति सर्वलोकेषु विश्रुतम् ॥
वर्मणा ते च्छादयामि कवचं समुदाहृतम् ॥ 114 ॥
1.17.m: 'citraṃ devānām' is renowned in all the worlds as the head; / 'varmaṇā te chādayāmi' is declared to be the armor.

1.17.s:
bhūrbhuvaḥ svariti tathā śirase parikīrtitam ..
gāyatrīmūlataṃtrastu sādhakaḥ sarvakarmaṇām . . 11 5. .
1.17.d:
भूर्भुवः स्वरिति तथा शिरसे परिकीर्तितम् ॥
गायत्रीमूलतंत्रस्तु साधकः सर्वकर्मणाम् ॥ 11 5॥
1.17.m: Likewise, 'bhūr bhuvaḥ svaḥ' is proclaimed for the head; / the root manual is the Gāyatrī, accomplishing all rituals.

1.17.s:
gāyatryā pūjayeddevamoṃkāreṇābhimaṃtritam. .
praṇavenāparānsarvānṛgvedādīnprapūjayet . . 116 . .
1.17.d:
गायत्र्या पूजयेद्देवमोंकारेणाभिमंत्रितम्॥
प्रणवेनापरान्सर्वानृग्वेदादीन्प्रपूजयेत् ॥ 116 ॥
1.17.m: One should worship the god with the Gāyatrī consecrated by the sound oṃ; / one should worship all the others, the Ṛgveda and the rest, with the praṇava.

1.17.s:
āhvāne pūjane vīra visarge brahmaṇastathā . .
gāyatrī paramo maṃtro vedamātā vibhāvinī . 117 ..
1.17.d:
आह्वाने पूजने वीर विसर्गे ब्रह्मणस्तथा ॥
गायत्री परमो मंत्रो वेदमाता विभाविनी । 117 ॥
1.17.m: In the invocation, in the worship, and likewise in the dismissal of Brahmā, O hero, / the Gāyatrī is the supreme mantra, the radiant mother of the Vedas.

1.17.s:
gāyatryakṣaratattvaistu pūjayedyastu devatām . .
sa gacchedbrahmaṇaḥ sthānaṃ durlabhaṃ yaddurā sadam . . 118 . . ..
iti śrībhaviṣye mahāpurāṇe śatārddhasāhasryāṃ saṃhitāyāṃ brāhme parvaṇi pratipatkalpe brahmaṇo'rcanavidhivarṇanaṃ nāma saptadaśo'dhyāyaḥ . . 17 . .
pratipatkalpasamāptivarṇanam
1.17.d:
गायत्र्यक्षरतत्त्वैस्तु पूजयेद्यस्तु देवताम् ॥
स गच्छेद्ब्रह्मणः स्थानं दुर्लभं यद्दुरा सदम् ॥ 118 ॥ ॥
इति श्रीभविष्ये महापुराणे शतार्द्धसाहस्र्यां संहितायां ब्राह्मे पर्वणि प्रतिपत्कल्पे ब्रह्मणोऽर्चनविधिवर्णनं नाम सप्तदशोऽध्यायः ॥ 17 ॥
प्रतिपत्कल्पसमाप्तिवर्णनम्
1.17.m:
Whoever worships the deity with the syllable-principles of the Gāyatrī, / he goes to the realm of Brahmā, which is difficult to attain and hard to reach.
Thus ends the seventeenth chapter, titled 'Description of the Ritual for Worshipping Brahmā in the Pratipatkalpa', in the Brāhmaparvan of the glorious Bhaviṣya Mahāpurāṇa consisting of fifty thousand verses.
Description of the Completion of the Pratipatkalpa

1.18.s:
sumanturuvāca
paurṇamāsyupavāsaṃ tu kṛtvā bhaktyā narādhipa .
anena vidhinā yastu viriñciṃ pūjayennaraḥ . . 1
1.18.d:
सुमन्तुरुवाच
पौर्णमास्युपवासं तु कृत्वा भक्त्या नराधिप ।
अनेन विधिना यस्तु विरिञ्चिं पूजयेन्नरः ॥ 1
1.18.m: Sumantu said: / Having fasted on the full moon day with devotion, O lord of men, / the man who worships Viriñci according to this rite,

1.18.s:
pratipadyāṃ mahābāho sa gacchedbrahmaṇaḥ padam .
ṛgbhirviśeṣato 1 devī viriñcervāstudevatāḥ . . 2
1.18.d:
प्रतिपद्यां महाबाहो स गच्छेद्ब्रह्मणः पदम् ।
ऋग्भिर्विशेषतो 1 देवी विरिञ्चेर्वास्तुदेवताः ॥ 2
1.18.m: on the pratipad, O mighty-armed one, goes to the abode of Brahmā; / especially [worshipping] with verses from the Ṛgveda the goddess and the household deities of Viriñci.

1.18.s:
kārttike māsi devasya rathayātrā prakīrtitā .
yāṃ kṛtvā mānavo bhaktyā yāti brahmasalokatām . . 3
1.18.d:
कार्त्तिके मासि देवस्य रथयात्रा प्रकीर्तिता ।
यां कृत्वा मानवो भक्त्या याति ब्रह्मसलोकताम् ॥ 3
1.18.m: In the month of Kārttika, the chariot procession of the god is proclaimed, / having performed which with devotion, a mortal attains dwelling in the world of Brahmā.

1.18.s:
kārtike māsi rājendra paurṇamāsyāṃ caturmukham .
mārgeṇa carmaṇā sārdhaṃ sāvitryā ca parantapa . . 4
1.18.d:
कार्तिके मासि राजेन्द्र पौर्णमास्यां चतुर्मुखम् ।
मार्गेण चर्मणा सार्धं सावित्र्या च परन्तप ॥ 4
1.18.m: In the month of Kārtika on the full moon day, O king of kings, scorcher of foes, / [taking] the four-faced [god] along with the path, the shield, and Sāvitrī,

1.18.s:
bhrāmayennagaraṃ sarvaṃ nānāvādyaiḥ samanvitam .
sthāpayed bhrāmayitvā tu salokaṃ nagaraṃ nṛpa . . 5
1.18.d:
भ्रामयेन्नगरं सर्वं नानावाद्यैः समन्वितम् ।
स्थापयेद् भ्रामयित्वा तु सलोकं नगरं नृप ॥ 5
1.18.m: one should take [him] around the entire city, accompanied by diverse musical instruments; / having taken [him] around the city along with its people, one should reinstall [him], O king.

1.18.s:
brāhmaṇaṃ bhojayityāgre śāṃḍileyaṃ prapūjya ca .
āropayedrathe devaṃ puṇyavāditranisvanaiḥ . . 6
1.18.d:
ब्राह्मणं भोजयित्याग्रे शांडिलेयं प्रपूज्य च ।
आरोपयेद्रथे देवं पुण्यवादित्रनिस्वनैः ॥ 6
1.18.m: Having first fed a brāhmaṇa and worshipped Śāṇḍileya, / one should place the god on the chariot amidst auspicious instrumental sounds.

1.18.s:
rathāgre śāṃḍilīputraṃ pūjayitvā vidhānataḥ .
brāhmaṇānvācayitvā ca kṛtvā puṇyāhamaṃgalam . . 7
1.18.d:
रथाग्रे शांडिलीपुत्रं पूजयित्वा विधानतः ।
ब्राह्मणान्वाचयित्वा च कृत्वा पुण्याहमंगलम् ॥ 7
1.18.m: Having worshipped the son of Śāṇḍilī in front of the chariot according to the rite, / having caused brāhmaṇas to recite, and having performed the auspicious declaration of a holy day,

1.18.s:
devamāropayitvā tu rathe kuryātprajāgaram .
nānāvidhaiḥ prekṣaṇakairbrahmaghoṣaiśca puṣkalaiḥ . . 8 rathopari ṭippaṇī
kṛtvā prajāgaraṃ hyevaṃ prabhāte brāhmaṇaṃ nṛpa .
bhojayitvā yathāśaktyā bhakṣyabhojyairanekaśaḥ . . 9
1.18.d:
देवमारोपयित्वा तु रथे कुर्यात्प्रजागरम् ।
नानाविधैः प्रेक्षणकैर्ब्रह्मघोषैश्च पुष्कलैः ॥ 8 रथोपरि टिप्पणी
कृत्वा प्रजागरं ह्येवं प्रभाते ब्राह्मणं नृप ।
भोजयित्वा यथाशक्त्या भक्ष्यभोज्यैरनेकशः ॥ 9
1.18.m: having placed the god on the chariot, one should keep a night vigil / with various spectacles and copious chants of the Veda. / Having thus kept a night vigil, in the morning, O king, / having fed a brāhmaṇa to the best of one's ability with numerous pastries and foods,

1.18.s:
pūjayitvā janaṃ2 vīra vajreṇa vidhivannṛpa .
bījena ca mahābāho payasā pāyasena ca . . 1.18.10
1.18.d:
पूजयित्वा जनं2 वीर वज्रेण विधिवन्नृप ।
बीजेन च महाबाहो पयसा पायसेन च ॥ 1.18.10
1.18.m: having worshipped the people, O hero, with a thunderbolt according to rule, O king, / and with seed, O mighty-armed one, with milk and rice boiled in milk,

1.18.s:
brāhmaṇānvācayitvā ca cchāṃdena vidhinā nṛpa .
kṛtvā puṇyāhaśabdaṃ ca rathaṃ ca bhrāmayetpure . . 11
1.18.d:
ब्राह्मणान्वाचयित्वा च च्छांदेन विधिना नृप ।
कृत्वा पुण्याहशब्दं च रथं च भ्रामयेत्पुरे ॥ 11
1.18.m: and having caused brāhmaṇas to recite according to Vedic rule, O king, / and having made the utterance of an auspicious day, one should take the chariot around the city.

1.18.s:
caturvedavidairviprairbhrāmayedbrahmaṇo ratham .
bahvṛcātharvaṇoccāraiśchandogādhvaryubhistathā . . 12
1.18.d:
चतुर्वेदविदैर्विप्रैर्भ्रामयेद्ब्रह्मणो रथम् ।
बह्वृचाथर्वणोच्चारैश्छन्दोगाध्वर्युभिस्तथा ॥ 12
1.18.m: One should have the chariot of Brahmā driven by brāhmaṇas learned in the four Vedas, / with the recitations of Ṛgvedins and Atharvavedins, and by Sāmavedins and Yajurvedins.

1.18.s:
bhrāmayeddevadevasya surajyeṣṭhasya taṃ ratham .
pradakṣiṇaṃ puraṃ sarvaṃ mārgeṇa susamena tu . . 13
1.18.d:
भ्रामयेद्देवदेवस्य सुरज्येष्ठस्य तं रथम् ।
प्रदक्षिणं पुरं सर्वं मार्गेण सुसमेन तु ॥ 13
1.18.m: One should drive that chariot of the god of gods, the eldest of the deities, / clockwise around the entire city along an even road.

1.18.s:
na voḍhavyo ratho vīra śūdreṇa śubhamicchatā .
nāruheta rathaṃ prājño muktvaikaṃ bhojakaṃ nṛpa . . 14
1.18.d:
न वोढव्यो रथो वीर शूद्रेण शुभमिच्छता ।
नारुहेत रथं प्राज्ञो मुक्त्वैकं भोजकं नृप ॥ 14
1.18.m: The chariot should not be drawn by a śūdra desiring well-being, O hero; / a wise man should not mount the chariot, O king, except for a single Bhojaka.

1.18.s:
brahmaṇo dakṣiṇe pārśve sāvitrīṃ sthāpayennṛpa .
bhojako vāmapārśve tu purataḥ kañjajaṃ nyaset . . 15
1.18.d:
ब्रह्मणो दक्षिणे पार्श्वे सावित्रीं स्थापयेन्नृप ।
भोजको वामपार्श्वे तु पुरतः कञ्जजं न्यसेत् ॥ 15
1.18.m: On the right side of Brahmā one should place Sāvitrī, O king; / the Bhojaka on the left side, and in front one should place the lotus-born [god].

1.18.s:
evaṃ tūryaninādaistu śaṃkhaśabdaiśca puṣkalaiḥ .
bhrāmayitvā rathaṃ rājanpuraṃ sarvaṃ pradakṣiṇam . .
svasthāne sthāpayedbhūyaḥ kṛtvā nīrājanaṃ budhaḥ . . 16
1.18.d:
एवं तूर्यनिनादैस्तु शंखशब्दैश्च पुष्कलैः ।
भ्रामयित्वा रथं राजन्पुरं सर्वं प्रदक्षिणम् ॥
स्वस्थाने स्थापयेद्भूयः कृत्वा नीराजनं बुधः ॥ 16
1.18.m: Having thus taken the chariot clockwise around the whole city, O king, / with blaring trumpets and copious conch-sounds, / the wise man should reinstall [it] in its own place after performing the wave-offering.

1.18.s:
ya evaṃ kurute yātrāṃ bhaktyā yaścāpi paśyati .
rathaṃ cākarṣate yastu sa gacchedbrahmaṇaḥ padam . . 17
1.18.d:
य एवं कुरुते यात्रां भक्त्या यश्चापि पश्यति ।
रथं चाकर्षते यस्तु स गच्छेद्ब्रह्मणः पदम् ॥ 17
1.18.m: He who thus conducts the procession, or who views it with devotion, / and he who pulls the chariot, goes to the abode of Brahmā.

1.18.s:
kārtike māsyamāvāsyāṃ yastu dīpapradīpanam .
śālāyāṃ brahmaṇaḥ kuryātsa gacchedbrahmaṇaḥ padam . . 18
1.18.d:
कार्तिके मास्यमावास्यां यस्तु दीपप्रदीपनम् ।
शालायां ब्रह्मणः कुर्यात्स गच्छेद्ब्रह्मणः पदम् ॥ 18
1.18.m: In the month of Kārtika on the new moon day, whoever kindles lamps / in the hall of Brahmā, goes to the abode of Brahmā.

1.18.s:
pratipadi brāhmaṇāṃścāpi guḍamiśraiḥ pradīpakaiḥ .
vāsobhirahataiścāpi sa gacchedbrahmaṇaḥ padam . . 19
1.18.d:
प्रतिपदि ब्राह्मणांश्चापि गुडमिश्रैः प्रदीपकैः ।
वासोभिरहतैश्चापि स गच्छेद्ब्रह्मणः पदम् ॥ 19
1.18.m: On the pratipad, [whoever honors] brāhmaṇas with lamps mixed with jaggery / and with unwashed garments, he goes to the abode of Brahmā.

1.18.s:
gaṃdhaipuṣpairnavairvastrairātmānaṃ 1 pūjayecca yaḥ .
tasyāṃ pratipadāyāṃ tu sa gacchedbrahmaṇaḥ padam . . 1.18.20
1.18.d:
गंधैपुष्पैर्नवैर्वस्त्रैरात्मानं 1 पूजयेच्च यः ।
तस्यां प्रतिपदायां तु स गच्छेद्ब्रह्मणः पदम् ॥ 1.18.20
1.18.m: And he who honors himself with perfumes, flowers, and new garments / on that pratipad, goes to the abode of Brahmā.

1.18.s:
mahāpuṇyā tithiriyaṃ balirājyapravartinī .
brahmaṇaḥ supriyā nityaṃ bāleyā parikīrtitā . . 21
1.18.d:
महापुण्या तिथिरियं बलिराज्यप्रवर्तिनी ।
ब्रह्मणः सुप्रिया नित्यं बालेया परिकीर्तिता ॥ 21
1.18.m: This lunar day is highly auspicious, inaugurating the reign of Bali; / always dear to Brahmā, it is renowned as Bāleyā.

1.18.s:
brāhmaṇānpūjayitvāsyāmātmānaṃ ca viśeṣataḥ .
sa yāti paramaṃ sthānaṃ viṣṇoramitatejasaḥ . . 22
1.18.d:
ब्राह्मणान्पूजयित्वास्यामात्मानं च विशेषतः ।
स याति परमं स्थानं विष्णोरमिततेजसः ॥ 22
1.18.m: Having worshipped brāhmaṇas on this [day] and especially oneself, / one goes to the supreme abode of Viṣṇu of immeasurable splendor.

1.18.s:
caitre māsi mahābāho puṇyā pratipadā parā .
tasyāṃ yaḥ śvapacaṃ spṛṣṭvā snānaṃ kuryānnarottama . 23
1.18.d:
चैत्रे मासि महाबाहो पुण्या प्रतिपदा परा ।
तस्यां यः श्वपचं स्पृष्ट्वा स्नानं कुर्यान्नरोत्तम । 23
1.18.m: In the month of Caitra, O mighty-armed one, the pratipad is supreme and auspicious; / on that day, whoever bathes after touching an outcaste, O best of men,

1.18.s:
na tasya duritaṃ kiñcinnādhayo vyādhayo nṛpa .
bhavanti kuruśārdūla tasmātsnānaṃ pravartayet . . 24
1.18.d:
न तस्य दुरितं किञ्चिन्नाधयो व्याधयो नृप ।
भवन्ति कुरुशार्दूल तस्मात्स्नानं प्रवर्तयेत् ॥ 24
1.18.m: to him no sin, nor mental agonies or bodily diseases occur, O king, / O tiger of the Kurus; therefore, one should perform that bath.

1.18.s:
divyaṃ nīrājanaṃ taddhi sarvarogavināśanam .
gomahiṣyādi yatkiṃcittatsarvaṃ bhūṣayennṛpa . . 25
1.18.d:
दिव्यं नीराजनं तद्धि सर्वरोगविनाशनम् ।
गोमहिष्यादि यत्किंचित्तत्सर्वं भूषयेन्नृप ॥ 25
1.18.m:
For that is a divine waving of lights that destroys all diseases.
O king, one should adorn whatever [cattle there are], such as cows and buffaloes.

1.18.s:
tailaśastrādibhirvastrastoraṇādhastato nayet .
brāhmaṇānāṃ tathā bhojyaṃ kuryātkurukulodvaha . . 26
1.18.d:
तैलशस्त्रादिभिर्वस्त्रस्तोरणाधस्ततो नयेत् ।
ब्राह्मणानां तथा भोज्यं कुर्यात्कुरुकुलोद्वह ॥ 26
1.18.m:
Then, with oil, weapons, garments, and other things, one should lead them beneath an archway.
Likewise, O upholder of the Kuru lineage, one should provide food for brāhmaṇas.

1.18.s:
tisro hyetāḥ parāḥ proktāstithayaḥ kurunandana .
kārttikeśvayuje māsi caitre māse ca bhārata . . 27
1.18.d:
तिस्रो ह्येताः पराः प्रोक्तास्तिथयः कुरुनन्दन ।
कार्त्तिकेश्वयुजे मासि चैत्रे मासे च भारत ॥ 27
1.18.m:
For these three lunar days are proclaimed as supreme, O joy of the Kurus,
in the months of Kārttika, Āśvayuja, and Caitra, O Bhārata.

1.18.s:
snānaṃ dānaṃ śataguṇaṃ kārttike yā tithirnṛpa .
balirājyāptisukhadā pāṃśulāśubhanāśinī . . 28
śaryātyākhyāne puṣpadvitīyā varṇanam
1.18.d:
स्नानं दानं शतगुणं कार्त्तिके या तिथिर्नृप ।
बलिराज्याप्तिसुखदा पांशुलाशुभनाशिनी ॥ 28
शर्यात्याख्याने पुष्पद्वितीया वर्णनम्

1.19.s:
sumanturuvāca
dvitīyāyāṃ tu rājendra aśvinau somapītinau .
cyavanena kṛtau yajñe miṣato maghavasya1 ca . . 1
1.19.d:
सुमन्तुरुवाच
द्वितीयायां तु राजेन्द्र अश्विनौ सोमपीतिनौ ।
च्यवनेन कृतौ यज्ञे मिषतो मघवस्य1 च ॥ 1
1.19.m:
Sumantu said:
On the second lunar day, O king of kings, the two Aśvins were made drinkers of soma
by Cyavana at the sacrifice, before the very eyes of Maghavan.

1.19.s:
śatānīka uvāca
kathamindrasya miṣataḥ kṛtau tau somapītinau .
cyavanena hi devānāṃ paśyatāṃ tadvadasva me . . 2
1.19.d:
शतानीक उवाच
कथमिन्द्रस्य मिषतः कृतौ तौ सोमपीतिनौ ।
च्यवनेन हि देवानां पश्यतां तद्वदस्व मे ॥ 2
1.19.m:
Śatānīka said:
How were the two made drinkers of soma before the very eyes of Indra
by Cyavana while the gods were looking on? Tell me that.

1.19.s:
aho mahattapastasya cyavanasya mahātmanaḥ .
yadindrasya balādeva devatvaṃ prāpitāvubhau . . 3
1.19.d:
अहो महत्तपस्तस्य च्यवनस्य महात्मनः ।
यदिन्द्रस्य बलादेव देवत्वं प्रापितावुभौ ॥ 3
1.19.m:
Ah, great was the ascetic power of that noble-minded Cyavana,
since by force against Indra both were raised to godhood!

1.19.s:
sumanturuvāca
purātanayuge sandhau paścime'tha narādhipa .
cyavano yogamāsthāya gaṃgākūle'vasacciram . . 4
1.19.d:
सुमन्तुरुवाच
पुरातनयुगे सन्धौ पश्चिमेऽथ नराधिप ।
च्यवनो योगमास्थाय गंगाकूलेऽवसच्चिरम् ॥ 4
1.19.m:
Sumantu said:
In an ancient age, at the twilight of the last [quarter], O ruler of men,
Cyavana, engaging in yoga, dwelt on the bank of the Gaṅgā for a long time.

1.19.s:
tatra śaryātirāyātaḥ snātumantaḥ1 puraiḥ saha .
snātvābhyarcya2 pitṝndevāngamanāyopacakrame . . 5
1.19.d:
तत्र शर्यातिरायातः स्नातुमन्तः1 पुरैः सह ।
स्नात्वाभ्यर्च्य2 पितॄन्देवान्गमनायोपचक्रमे ॥ 5
1.19.m:
Śaryāti arrived there to bathe along with his inner apartments.
Having bathed and worshipped the ancestors and the gods, he prepared to depart.

1.19.s:
tatra mūḍhaṃ janapadamapaśyatpathi ceṣṭanam .
viṇmūtrotsargasaṃruddhaṃ jyotirākṣiptaniṣkriyam . .
bhramantaṃ tatratatraiva samīkṣya sa balaṃ nṛpaḥ . . 6
1.19.d:
तत्र मूढं जनपदमपश्यत्पथि चेष्टनम् ।
विण्मूत्रोत्सर्गसंरुद्धं ज्योतिराक्षिप्तनिष्क्रियम् ॥
भ्रमन्तं तत्रतत्रैव समीक्ष्य स बलं नृपः ॥ 6
1.19.m:
There he saw his people bewildered, writhing upon the road,
blocked from discharging feces and urine, their light cast down, stripped of movement.
Seeing his army wandering about right there, the king,

1.19.s:
uvāca3 durmanā rājā amātyānsvānpurogamān .
cyavanasyāśramo'yaṃ hi nāparāddhaṃ tu kenacit . . 7
1.19.d:
उवाच3 दुर्मना राजा अमात्यान्स्वान्पुरोगमान् ।
च्यवनस्याश्रमोऽयं हि नापराद्धं तु केनचित् ॥ 7
1.19.m:
the king, dejected in mind, said to his ministers who preceded him:
'This is indeed the hermitage of Cyavana; has no offense been committed by anyone?'

1.19.s:
na covāca yadā kaścittasya rājñastu pṛcchataḥ .
tadā sutā sukanyāsya provāca pitaraṃ vacaḥ . . 8
1.19.d:
न चोवाच यदा कश्चित्तस्य राज्ञस्तु पृच्छतः ।
तदा सुता सुकन्यास्य प्रोवाच पितरं वचः ॥ 8
1.19.m:
And when no one spoke as that king questioned them,
then his daughter Sukanyā spoke these words to her father:

1.19.s:
mayā dṛṣṭaṃ tu yattāta sakhibhiḥ saha kautukam .
tatte vacmi nibodha tvaṃ śṛṇu tāta mahādbhutam . . 9
1.19.d:
मया दृष्टं तु यत्तात सखिभिः सह कौतुकम् ।
तत्ते वच्मि निबोध त्वं शृणु तात महाद्भुतम् ॥ 9
1.19.m:
'What was seen as a curiosity by me and my companions, O father,
that I will tell you; listen, understand, O father, a great wonder!

1.19.s:
śiñjitārāvabahulāḥ kāñcīnūpuramekhalāḥ .
gāyantyo vilapantyaśca kīḍantyaścātra kānane . . 1.19.10
1.19.d:
शिञ्जितारावबहुलाः काञ्चीनूपुरमेखलाः ।
गायन्त्यो विलपन्त्यश्च कीडन्त्यश्चात्र कानने ॥ 1.19.10
1.19.m:
[We were] resounding with jingling sounds from girdles, anklets, and waistbands,
singing, crying out, and playing in this forest.

1.19.s:
kokiladhvanimaśrauṣaṃ vyaktāvyaktākṣaraṃ kṛśam .
sukanye hyehihyehīti valmīkādvacamudgiran . . 11
1.19.d:
कोकिलध्वनिमश्रौषं व्यक्ताव्यक्ताक्षरं कृशम् ।
सुकन्ये ह्येहिह्येहीति वल्मीकाद्वचमुद्गिरन् ॥ 11
1.19.m:
I heard a sound like a cuckoo, faint, with distinct and indistinct syllables,
uttering the words: "Sukanyā, come, come!" from an anthill.

1.19.s:
tatra gatvādbhutaṃ tāta paśyāmaḥ kila pāvakau .
dīpāvivācalaśikhau bhūyaḥ kanyā uvāca ha . . 12
1.19.d:
तत्र गत्वाद्भुतं तात पश्यामः किल पावकौ ।
दीपाविवाचलशिखौ भूयः कन्या उवाच ह ॥ 12
1.19.m:
Having gone there, O father, we truly saw a wonder: two fires,
like lamps with motionless flames.' Again the maiden spoke:

1.19.s:
mayā ca kautukāttāta kimetadityabuddhitaḥ .
sūditau darbhasūcyagraistattejaḥ samupāramat . . 13
1.19.d:
मया च कौतुकात्तात किमेतदित्यबुद्धितः ।
सूदितौ दर्भसूच्यग्रैस्तत्तेजः समुपारमत् ॥ 13
1.19.m:
'And out of curiosity, O father, not understanding what it was,
they were pierced with the points of darbha needles, and that luster ceased.'

1.19.s:
tacchrutvā nṛpatistrastastūrṇaṃ tadvanamāgamat .
yatrāste bhārgavaḥ kaṣṭaṃ valmīkāntargato muniḥ . . 14
1.19.d:
तच्छ्रुत्वा नृपतिस्त्रस्तस्तूर्णं तद्वनमागमत् ।
यत्रास्ते भार्गवः कष्टं वल्मीकान्तर्गतो मुनिः ॥ 14
1.19.m:
Hearing that, the terrified king quickly went to that forest
where the sage, the descendant of Bhṛgu, sat in distress inside the anthill.

1.19.s:
gatvā sa tatra provāca praṇipatya dvijottamam .
aparāddhaṃ mayā 1 deva tatkṣamasva namo'stu te . . 15
1.19.d:
गत्वा स तत्र प्रोवाच प्रणिपत्य द्विजोत्तमम् ।
अपराद्धं मया 1 देव तत्क्षमस्व नमोऽस्तु ते ॥ 15
1.19.m:
Going there and bowing down to that best of the twice-born, he said:
'An offense has been committed by me, O lord; forgive it, reverence to you!'

1.19.s:
sa taṃ provāca nṛpatiṃ mayā jñātaṃ narādhipa .
sukanyāṃ me prayacchasva niveśārthī2 hyahaṃ nṛpa . .
anukramansukanyāṃ tu dattvā rājansukhī bhava . . 16
1.19.d:
स तं प्रोवाच नृपतिं मया ज्ञातं नराधिप ।
सुकन्यां मे प्रयच्छस्व निवेशार्थी2 ह्यहं नृप ॥
अनुक्रमन्सुकन्यां तु दत्त्वा राजन्सुखी भव ॥ 16
1.19.m:
He said to that king: 'It has been understood by me, O ruler of men.
Give me Sukanyā, for I desire marriage, O king.
In accordance with duty, having given Sukanyā, O king, be happy.'

1.19.s:
ityuktaḥ pradadau rājā sukanyāmavicārayan .
tataḥ svapuramāgamya avasatsuciraṃ sukhī . . 17
1.19.d:
इत्युक्तः प्रददौ राजा सुकन्यामविचारयन् ।
ततः स्वपुरमागम्य अवसत्सुचिरं सुखी ॥ 17
1.19.m:
Thus addressed, the king gave Sukanyā without deliberating.
Then, having returned to his own city, he lived happy for a very long time.

1.19.s:
sukanyāpi patiṃ labdhvā suprītārādhayattadā .
rājyaśriyaṃ parityajya valkalājinadhāriṇī . . 18
1.19.d:
सुकन्यापि पतिं लब्ध्वा सुप्रीताराधयत्तदा ।
राज्यश्रियं परित्यज्य वल्कलाजिनधारिणी ॥ 18
1.19.m:
Sukanyā too, having obtained a husband, served him with great joy then,
abandoning royal splendour and wearing bark and animal skins.

1.19.s:
gate bahutithe kāle vasante samupasthite .
tapodyotitasarvāṅgīṃ rūpodāryaguṇānvitām . .
snātāṃ svabhāryāṃ cyavana uvāca madhurākṣaram . . 19
1.19.d:
गते बहुतिथे काले वसन्ते समुपस्थिते ।
तपोद्योतितसर्वाङ्गीं रूपोदार्यगुणान्विताम् ॥
स्नातां स्वभार्यां च्यवन उवाच मधुराक्षरम् ॥ 19
1.19.m:
When a long time had passed and spring had arrived,
Cyavana spoke sweet words to his own wife who had bathed,
her limbs illuminated by asceticism, endowed with beauty, dignity, and virtues:

1.19.s:
ehyehi bhadre bhadraṃ te śayanīyaṃ samāśraya .
apatyaṃ janayasyādya kuladvayavivardhanam . . 1.19.20
1.19.d:
एह्येहि भद्रे भद्रं ते शयनीयं समाश्रय ।
अपत्यं जनयस्याद्य कुलद्वयविवर्धनम् ॥ 1.19.20
1.19.m:
'Come, come, auspicious one, may good betide you; take to the bed.
Bear an offspring today to increase both families.'

1.19.s:
evamuktā tu sā kanyā prāñjaliḥ patimabravīt .
3nārhasyadya sukalyāṇa saṅgamaṃ sthaṇḍile'same . . 21
1.19.d:
एवमुक्ता तु सा कन्या प्राञ्जलिः पतिमब्रवीत् ।
3नार्हस्यद्य सुकल्याण सङ्गमं स्थण्डिलेऽसमे ॥ 21
1.19.m:
Addressed thus, the maiden, with folded hands, said to her husband:
'You ought not, O most blessed one, to have union today on an uneven patch of ground.

1.19.s:
mama priyaṃ kuruṣvādya tato māmāhvayasva ca .
pitṛgehe yathātiṣṭhaṃ śayanīye susaṃskṛte . . 22
1.19.d:
मम प्रियं कुरुष्वाद्य ततो मामाह्वयस्व च ।
पितृगेहे यथातिष्ठं शयनीये सुसंस्कृते ॥ 22
1.19.m:
Do what pleases me today, and then summon me,
just as I remained in my father’s house on a well-prepared bed,

1.19.s:
bahugairikavarṇādyaiḥ śvetapītāruṇākule .
vastrālaṅkāragandhādyaistathā tvamapi tatkuru . . 23
1.19.d:
बहुगैरिकवर्णाद्यैः श्वेतपीतारुणाकुले ।
वस्त्रालङ्कारगन्धाद्यैस्तथा त्वमपि तत्कुरु ॥ 23
1.19.m:
filled with white, yellow, and red colors from abundant red ochre and the like,
and with garments, ornaments, perfumes, and other things—do you also make it so!

1.19.s:
ātmānaṃ vayasopetaṃ rūpavantaṃ suvarcasam .
vastrālaṅkāragandhāḍhyaṃ paśyeyaṃ yena sādaram . . 24
1.19.d:
आत्मानं वयसोपेतं रूपवन्तं सुवर्चसम् ।
वस्त्रालङ्कारगन्धाढ्यं पश्येयं येन सादरम् ॥ 24
1.19.m:
May I see you endowed with youth, handsome, radiant,
rich in garments, ornaments, and perfumes, so that [I may look upon you] with affection.'

1.19.s:
sukanyāyā vacaḥ śrutvā cyavanaḥ prāha durmanāḥ .
na me'sti vittaṃ kalyāṇi pituste'sti yathā vane . . 25
1.19.d:
सुकन्याया वचः श्रुत्वा च्यवनः प्राह दुर्मनाः ।
न मेऽस्ति वित्तं कल्याणि पितुस्तेऽस्ति यथा वने ॥ 25
1.19.m:
Hearing Sukanyā’s words, Cyavana, troubled in mind, said:
'I have no wealth, auspicious one, such as your father has in the forest.

1.19.s:
sa kathaṃ bhūṣayāmyadya surūpaśca kathaṃ vada .
provāca sā patiṃ bhūyaḥ prahasantī kṛtāñjaliḥ . .
vittaṃ dadāvailavilo rūpaṃ vairocano'dadat . . 26
1.19.d:
स कथं भूषयाम्यद्य सुरूपश्च कथं वद ।
प्रोवाच सा पतिं भूयः प्रहसन्ती कृताञ्जलिः ॥
वित्तं ददावैलविलो रूपं वैरोचनोऽददत् ॥ 26
1.19.m:
How then can I adorn myself today, and how can I become handsome? Tell me.'
Laughing, with hands joined in reverent greeting, she spoke again to her husband:
'The son of Ilavilā gave wealth; the son of Virocana gave beauty.'

1.19.s:
cyavanaḥ prāha bhāryāṃ tāṃ na kariṣye tapovyayam .
evamuktvā tapaścograṃ tatāpa suciraṃ tadā . . 27
1.19.d:
च्यवनः प्राह भार्यां तां न करिष्ये तपोव्ययम् ।
एवमुक्त्वा तपश्चोग्रं तताप सुचिरं तदा ॥ 27
1.19.m:
Cyavana said to his wife: 'I will not waste my asceticism.'
Having spoken thus, he then performed fierce asceticism for a very long time.

1.19.s:
atha tatrāgatau vīrāvaśvinau kālaparyayāt .
dṛṣṭavantau sukanyāṃ tau dīptyā vai devatāmiva . . 28
1.19.d:
अथ तत्रागतौ वीरावश्विनौ कालपर्ययात् ।
दृष्टवन्तौ सुकन्यां तौ दीप्त्या वै देवतामिव ॥ 28
1.19.m:
Then in the course of time, the two heroic Aśvins arrived there.
They saw Sukanyā, like a deity in splendour.

1.19.s:
upagamyocatustāṃ tau kā tvaṃ sundari rūpiṇī .
kimarthamiha ekā tvaṃ tiṣṭhase kastavāśrayaḥ . . 29
1.19.d:
उपगम्योचतुस्तां तौ का त्वं सुन्दरि रूपिणी ।
किमर्थमिह एका त्वं तिष्ठसे कस्तवाश्रयः ॥ 29
1.19.m:
Approaching her, the two said: 'Who are you, beautiful, shapely woman?
For what reason do you stand here alone? Who is your protector?'

1.19.s:
sā tāvuvāca tanvaṅgī śaryātiduhitā hyaham .
bhartā ca cyavano mahyaṃ kau ca vāṃ me tathocyatām . . 1.19.30
1.19.d:
सा तावुवाच तन्वङ्गी शर्यातिदुहिता ह्यहम् ।
भर्ता च च्यवनो मह्यं कौ च वां मे तथोच्यताम् ॥ 1.19.30
1.19.m:
The slender-limbed woman said to them: 'I am indeed the daughter of Śaryāti,
and Cyavana is my husband. And who are you two? Let that be told to me.'

1.19.s:
ūcatuścāśvinau devāvāvāṃ viddhi nṛpātmaje .
kiṃ kariṣyasi tena tvaṃ jīrṇena ca kṛśena ca . .
āvayorvṛṇu bhartāramekameva yamicchasi . . 31
1.19.d:
ऊचतुश्चाश्विनौ देवावावां विद्धि नृपात्मजे ।
किं करिष्यसि तेन त्वं जीर्णेन च कृशेन च ॥
आवयोर्वृणु भर्तारमेकमेव यमिच्छसि ॥ 31
1.19.m:
The two divine Aśvins said: 'Know us, O king’s daughter.
What will you do with him, who is aged and emaciated?
Choose one of us two as your husband, whichever you desire.'

1.19.s:
sā tvabravīcca mā maivaṃ vaktumarhau divaukasau .
bhartāramanuraktāṅgī yathā svāhā vibhāvasoḥ . . 32
1.19.d:
सा त्वब्रवीच्च मा मैवं वक्तुमर्हौ दिवौकसौ ।
भर्तारमनुरक्ताङ्गी यथा स्वाहा विभावसोः ॥ 32
1.19.m:
She, however, said: 'You two dwellers in heaven ought not to speak thus.
I am devoted in body to my husband, just as Svāhā is to Fire.'

1.19.s:
aśvināvūcatuḥ
āyātu ca viśatvadya cyavano vaiṣṇavījalam .
tato nau madhyagaṃ hyekaṃ vṛṇīṣvānyaṃ yamicchati . . 33
tāvabrūtāṃ sukanyāṃ tu gatvā pṛccha svakaṃ patim .
taṃ ca pṛṣṭvā punaścātrāgaccha nau sannidhau punaḥ . . 34.
āvāmatraiva tiṣṭhāvo yāvadāgamanaṃ tava .
sā gatvā prāha bhartāramaśvināvevasūcatuḥ 1 . . 35
1.19.d:
अश्विनावूचतुः
आयातु च विशत्वद्य च्यवनो वैष्णवीजलम् ।
ततो नौ मध्यगं ह्येकं वृणीष्वान्यं यमिच्छति ॥ 33
तावब्रूतां सुकन्यां तु गत्वा पृच्छ स्वकं पतिम् ।
तं च पृष्ट्वा पुनश्चात्रागच्छ नौ सन्निधौ पुनः ॥ 34.
आवामत्रैव तिष्ठावो यावदागमनं तव ।
सा गत्वा प्राह भर्तारमश्विनावेवसूचतुः 1 ॥ 35
1.19.m:
The two Aśvins said:
'Let Cyavana come and enter the Vaiṣṇavī waters today.
Then choose one between us, or another, whichever [he] wishes.'
The two said to Sukanyā: 'Go and ask your own husband.
Having asked him, come here once more into our presence.
We two shall remain right here until your return.'
She, having gone, told her husband just what the two Aśvins had said:

1.19.s:
rūpavantaṃ ca bhartāraṃ kariṣyāvo yamicchasi .
atha madhyagataṃ hyekaṃ bhartṛtvena variṣyasi . . 36
1.19.d:
रूपवन्तं च भर्तारं करिष्यावो यमिच्छसि ।
अथ मध्यगतं ह्येकं भर्तृत्वेन वरिष्यसि ॥ 36
1.19.m:
'"We two shall make your husband handsome, as you desire.
Then you will choose one of us standing between as your husband."'

1.19.s:
evamastviti tāṃ prāha bhāryāṃ cyavanastvaran .
sā taṃ gṛhya jagāmāśu yatra tau bhiṣajāvubhau . . 37
1.19.d:
एवमस्त्विति तां प्राह भार्यां च्यवनस्त्वरन् ।
सा तं गृह्य जगामाशु यत्र तौ भिषजावुभौ ॥ 37
1.19.m:
'So be it,' Cyavana said in haste to that wife.
Taking him, she went swiftly to where both physicians were.

1.19.s:
sā tāvuvāca cyavano yathoktaṃ bhavatorvacaḥ .
kurutaṃ hyaśvinau kṣipraṃ sukanyā cepsitaṃ2 vṛṇot . . 38
1.19.d:
सा तावुवाच च्यवनो यथोक्तं भवतोर्वचः ।
कुरुतं ह्यश्विनौ क्षिप्रं सुकन्या चेप्सितं2 वृणोत् ॥ 38
1.19.m: She said to the two of them: 'Cyavana has accepted the word of you two, as spoken. / Do it quickly, O Aśvins, and let Sukanyā choose the desired one.'

1.19.s:
tau taṃ saṅgṛhya gaṅgāyāṃ praviṣṭau muninā saha .
muhūrtāttu samuttiṣṭhanrūpataśca śriyā vṛtāḥ . . 39
1.19.d:
तौ तं सङ्गृह्य गङ्गायां प्रविष्टौ मुनिना सह ।
मुहूर्तात्तु समुत्तिष्ठन्रूपतश्च श्रिया वृताः ॥ 39
1.19.m: Taking him, the two plunged into the Gaṅgā together with the sage; / after an instant, they emerged, endowed with beauty and radiant splendor.

1.19.s:
śobhante sma mahābāhau kamudbhidya tapoyutāḥ .
kalpādau kalaśe yadvatkañjākṣa vyoma vedhasaḥ . .
udakādutthitāstasmātsarve te samarūpakāḥ ..1.19.40
1.19.d:
शोभन्ते स्म महाबाहौ कमुद्भिद्य तपोयुताः ।
कल्पादौ कलशे यद्वत्कञ्जाक्ष व्योम वेधसः ॥
उदकादुत्थितास्तस्मात्सर्वे ते समरूपकाः ॥1.19.40
1.19.m: Those ascetic ones shone, O mighty-armed one, breaking out of the water, / just as at the beginning of the kalpa the lotus-eyed Brahma's sky [burst forth] from the jar. / Rising up from that water, they were all of identical form.

1.19.s:
sukanyā tu tato dṛṣṭvā bharttāraṃ devarūpiṇam .
harṣeṇa mahatāviṣṭā na ca taṃ veda bhārata ..41
1.19.d:
सुकन्या तु ततो दृष्ट्वा भर्त्तारं देवरूपिणम् ।
हर्षेण महताविष्टा न च तं वेद भारत ॥41
1.19.m: Then Sukanyā, seeing her husband possessing the form of a god, / was filled with immense joy, but could not distinguish him, O descendant of Bharata.

1.19.s:
samakāyāḥ samavayaḥ samarūpāḥ samaśriyaḥ .
vastrālaṅkārasadṛśāndṛṣṭvā cintāṃ gatā ciram ..42
1.19.d:
समकायाः समवयः समरूपाः समश्रियः ।
वस्त्रालङ्कारसदृशान्दृष्ट्वा चिन्तां गता चिरम् ॥42
1.19.m: With identical bodies, identical age, identical form, identical glory, / and identical garments and ornaments—seeing them, she fell into prolonged contemplation.

1.19.s:
sā cintayitvā suciraṃ vaidyadevāvuvāca ha .
bībhatso'pi mayā bhartā parityakto na karhicit ..43
1.19.d:
सा चिन्तयित्वा सुचिरं वैद्यदेवावुवाच ह ।
बीभत्सोऽपि मया भर्ता परित्यक्तो न कर्हिचित् ॥43
1.19.m: Having reflected for a long time, she said to the two divine physicians: / 'Though repulsive, my husband was never abandoned by me.

1.19.s:
bhavadbhirātmasaṃdṛśaṃ kathaṃ1 tyaktvā vṛṇe param .
tasmāttameva bhartāraṃ prayacchadhvaṃ divaukasaḥ ..44
1.19.d:
भवद्भिरात्मसंदृशं कथं1 त्यक्त्वा वृणे परम् ।
तस्मात्तमेव भर्तारं प्रयच्छध्वं दिवौकसः ॥44
1.19.m: Leaving aside the one like yourselves, how could I choose another? / Therefore, grant that very husband to me, O gods!'

1.19.s:
tayā sabahumānaṃ tau prāñjalyā prārthitau tadā .
devacihnāni svānyeva dhārayantau supūjitau ..45
1.19.d:
तया सबहुमानं तौ प्राञ्जल्या प्रार्थितौ तदा ।
देवचिह्नानि स्वान्येव धारयन्तौ सुपूजितौ ॥45
1.19.m: She besought the two with great reverence, her hands joined in supplication. / Then, properly worshipped, they displayed their divine signs.

1.19.s:
sukanyā nipuṇaṃ tau tu sunirīkṣya ca vihvalā .
na rajo na nimeṣo vai na spṛśete dharāṃ pade ..46
1.19.d:
सुकन्या निपुणं तौ तु सुनिरीक्ष्य च विह्वला ।
न रजो न निमेषो वै न स्पृशेते धरां पदे ॥46
1.19.m: Sukanyā scrutinized them carefully; being agitated, [she saw that] / their feet had no dust, no blinking of the eyes, and did not touch the ground.

1.19.s:
ayaṃ ca sarajā mlāno bhūmimāśritya tiṣṭhati .
nimeṣaṃ caiva tasyaivaṃ jñātvā vai cyavano vṛtaḥ ..47
1.19.d:
अयं च सरजा म्लानो भूमिमाश्रित्य तिष्ठति ।
निमेषं चैव तस्यैवं ज्ञात्वा वै च्यवनो वृतः ॥47
1.19.m: 'This one has dust, looks weary, and stands touching the ground, / and he blinks'—knowing this thus, she chose Cyavana.

1.19.s:
cyavane vṛte sukanyayā puṣpavṛṣṭiḥ papāta ha .
devadundubhayaścaiva prāvādyanta anekaśaḥ ..48
1.19.d:
च्यवने वृते सुकन्यया पुष्पवृष्टिः पपात ह ।
देवदुन्दुभयश्चैव प्रावाद्यन्त अनेकशः ॥48
1.19.m: When Cyavana was chosen by Sukanyā, a shower of flowers fell, / and celestial drums sounded in great numbers.

1.19.s:
tatastu cyavanastuṣṭo divyarūpadharastadā .
uvāca tau tu suprīta aśvinau kiṃ karomi vām ..49
1.19.d:
ततस्तु च्यवनस्तुष्टो दिव्यरूपधरस्तदा ।
उवाच तौ तु सुप्रीत अश्विनौ किं करोमि वाम् ॥49
1.19.m: Then Cyavana, delighted and bearing a celestial form, / highly pleased, spoke to the two Aśvins: 'What shall I do for you?

1.19.s:
bhāryā dattā kṛtaṃ rūpaṃ devānāmapi durlabham .
upakāraṃ variṣṭhaṃ yo na karotyupakāriṇaḥ ..1.19.50
1.19.d:
भार्या दत्ता कृतं रूपं देवानामपि दुर्लभम् ।
उपकारं वरिष्ठं यो न करोत्युपकारिणः ॥1.19.50
1.19.m: A wife has been granted, and a form hard even for the gods to attain has been bestowed. / Whoever does not render the highest service to a benefactor

1.19.s:
ekaviṃśatsa gacchecca narakāṇi krameṇa vai .
tasmādahaṃ variṣṭhaṃ vai kariṣye'hamamānuṣam . . 51
1.19.d:
एकविंशत्स गच्छेच्च नरकाणि क्रमेण वै ।
तस्मादहं वरिष्ठं वै करिष्येऽहममानुषम् ॥ 51
1.19.m: would go to twenty-one hells one after another. / Therefore, I shall perform an extraordinary, superhuman

1.19.s:
upakāraṃ bhavadbhyāṃ tu prītaḥ kuryāṃ suniścitam .
yajñabhāgaphalaṃ dadyāṃ yaddeveṣvapi durlabham . . 52
1.19.d:
उपकारं भवद्भ्यां तु प्रीतः कुर्यां सुनिश्चितम् ।
यज्ञभागफलं दद्यां यद्देवेष्वपि दुर्लभम् ॥ 52
1.19.m: service for you both, being pleased, most assuredly: / I shall give you a share of the sacrifice and its fruit, which is rare even among the gods.'

1.19.s:
evamuktvā tu deveśau visasarja mahāmuniḥ .
ājagāmāśramaṃ puṇyaṃ sahabhāryo mudānvitaḥ . . 53
1.19.d:
एवमुक्त्वा तु देवेशौ विससर्ज महामुनिः ।
आजगामाश्रमं पुण्यं सहभार्यो मुदान्वितः ॥ 53
1.19.m: Having spoken thus, the great sage dismissed the two lords of gods, / and returned to his holy hermitage with his wife, full of joy.

1.19.s:
atha śuśrāva śaryātiścyavanaṃ devarūpiṇam .
jagāma ca mahātejā draṣṭuṃ munivaraṃ vaśī . . 54
1.19.d:
अथ शुश्राव शर्यातिश्च्यवनं देवरूपिणम् ।
जगाम च महातेजा द्रष्टुं मुनिवरं वशी ॥ 54
1.19.m: Then Śaryāti heard that Cyavana possessed the form of a god, / and the self-controlled, glorious king went to see the best of sages.

1.19.s:
taṃ dṛṣṭvā praṇipatyādau pratipūjya yathārhataḥ .
sukanyāṃ tu tato dṛṣṭvā praṇipatyābhinandya ca . . 55
1.19.d:
तं दृष्ट्वा प्रणिपत्यादौ प्रतिपूज्य यथार्हतः ।
सुकन्यां तु ततो दृष्ट्वा प्रणिपत्याभिनन्द्य च ॥ 55
1.19.m: Seeing him, he first bowed down and honored him fittingly; / then seeing Sukanyā, he bowed to her and welcomed her.

1.19.s:
sasvaje mūrdhni āghrāya tatotsaṅgaṃ 1 samānayat .
sā tasyāḥ sasvaje premṇā ānandāśrupariplutā . .
saṃsthāpya tāṃ mudā yukto nṛpatiḥ saha bhāryayā . . 56
1.19.d:
सस्वजे मूर्ध्नि आघ्राय ततोत्सङ्गं 1 समानयत् ।
सा तस्याः सस्वजे प्रेम्णा आनन्दाश्रुपरिप्लुता ॥
संस्थाप्य तां मुदा युक्तो नृपतिः सह भार्यया ॥ 56
1.19.m: He smelled her crown and embraced her, then took her onto his lap. / She embraced him with affection, overflowing with tears of joy. / Having seated her, the delighted king, together with his wife,

1.19.s:
bhūyo'bravītsusaṃtuṣṭaṃ cyavanastaṃ narādhipam .
saṃbhāraṃ kuru yajñārthaṃ yājayiṣye narādhipa . . 57
1.19.d:
भूयोऽब्रवीत्सुसंतुष्टं च्यवनस्तं नराधिपम् ।
संभारं कुरु यज्ञार्थं याजयिष्ये नराधिप ॥ 57
1.19.m: said to him: Cyavana, very satisfied, spoke further to that king of men: / 'Make preparations for a sacrifice; I shall officiate as your priest, O king.'

1.19.s:
evamuktaḥ sa nṛpatiḥ praṇipatya mahāmunim .
jagāma svapuraṃ hṛṣṭo yajñārthaṃ yatnamācarat . . 58
1.19.d:
एवमुक्तः स नृपतिः प्रणिपत्य महामुनिम् ।
जगाम स्वपुरं हृष्टो यज्ञार्थं यत्नमाचरत् ॥ 58
1.19.m: Thus addressed, the king bowed down to the great sage, / and went to his own city rejoiced, making efforts for the sacrifice.

1.19.s:
sapreṣyānpreṣayankṣipraṃ yajñārthe dravyamāharat .
maṃtripurohitācāryānānayāmāsa satvaram . . 59
1.19.d:
सप्रेष्यान्प्रेषयन्क्षिप्रं यज्ञार्थे द्रव्यमाहरत् ।
मंत्रिपुरोहिताचार्यानानयामास सत्वरम् ॥ 59
1.19.m: Sending messengers swiftly, he procured the materials for the sacrifice; / he promptly summoned ministers, family priests, and preceptors.

1.19.s:
samānīteṣu sarveṣu teṣu dravyeṣu bhārata .
ājagāma viśuddhātmā cyavanaḥ saha bhāryayā . . 1.19.60
1.19.d:
समानीतेषु सर्वेषु तेषु द्रव्येषु भारत ।
आजगाम विशुद्धात्मा च्यवनः सह भार्यया ॥ 1.19.60
1.19.m: When all those materials had been assembled, O descendant of Bharata, / the pure-minded Cyavana arrived together with his wife.

1.19.s:
sampūjitaśca śuśrāva mahāntaṃ tyāgamaujasam .
anyaiśca bahubhiḥ sārddhamatryaṅgirasabhārgavaiḥ . . 61
1.19.d:
सम्पूजितश्च शुश्राव महान्तं त्यागमौजसम् ।
अन्यैश्च बहुभिः सार्द्धमत्र्यङ्गिरसभार्गवैः ॥ 61
1.19.m: Revered, he heard of the great, splendid generosity [of the king], / along with many other [sages]—Atri, Aṅgiras, and Bhārgavas.

1.19.s:
pravartite mahāyajñe yajamāne nṛpottame .
ṛtviktvakarmanirate hūyamāne hutāśane . .
āhūtāḥ svāgatāḥ sarve bhāgārthaṃ tridivālayāḥ . . 62
1.19.d:
प्रवर्तिते महायज्ञे यजमाने नृपोत्तमे ।
ऋत्विक्त्वकर्मनिरते हूयमाने हुताशने ॥
आहूताः स्वागताः सर्वे भागार्थं त्रिदिवालयाः ॥ 62
1.19.m: When the great sacrifice commenced with the best of kings acting as the patron, / with [priests] engaged in the duties of officiating priests, and the sacrificial fire being fed with oblations, / all the dwellers of heaven were invoked and welcomed to receive their share.

1.19.s:
yajñabhāge pravṛtte tu śāstroktena vidhānataḥ .
āgatāvaśvinau tatra āhūto cyavanena tu . . 63
1.19.d:
यज्ञभागे प्रवृत्ते तु शास्त्रोक्तेन विधानतः ।
आगतावश्विनौ तत्र आहूतो च्यवनेन तु ॥ 63
1.19.m: When the offering of the sacrificial share was underway according to the scriptural rules, / the two Aśvins arrived there, having been summoned by Cyavana.

1.19.s:
āhvāne kriyamāṇe tu aśvibhyāṃ tu tadā nṛpa .
provācendro'tha cyavanaṃ naitau bhāgānvitau kuru . .
devānāṃ bhiṣajāvetau na bhāgārhau na daivatau . . 64
1.19.d:
आह्वाने क्रियमाणे तु अश्विभ्यां तु तदा नृप ।
प्रोवाचेन्द्रोऽथ च्यवनं नैतौ भागान्वितौ कुरु ॥
देवानां भिषजावेतौ न भागार्हौ न दैवतौ ॥ 64
1.19.m: While the invocation was being made for the two Aśvins, O king, / Indra then said to Cyavana: 'Do not make these two recipients of a share! / These two are mere physicians of the gods, unworthy of a sacrificial share and not true deities.'

1.19.s:
cyavanastviṃdramāhedaṃ devau hyetāvubhāvapi .
mamopakāriṇāvetau dadmi bhāgaṃ na saṃśayaḥ . . 65
1.19.d:
च्यवनस्त्विंद्रमाहेदं देवौ ह्येतावुभावपि ।
ममोपकारिणावेतौ दद्मि भागं न संशयः ॥ 65
1.19.m: Cyavana replied to Indra: 'These two are indeed gods. / They have been my benefactors; I shall give them a share without a doubt.'

1.19.s:
tato hyuvāca sakrodhaḥ sa śakraścyavanaṃ ruṣā .
viprarṣe prahariṣyāmi yadi bhāgaṃ prayacchasi . . 66
1.19.d:
ततो ह्युवाच सक्रोधः स शक्रश्च्यवनं रुषा ।
विप्रर्षे प्रहरिष्यामि यदि भागं प्रयच्छसि ॥ 66
1.19.m: Then Śakra, enraged, spoke furiously to Cyavana: / 'O Brahmin sage, I shall strike you if you grant them a share!'

1.19.s:
evamuktastu viprarṣirna covācāpi kiñcana .
bhāgau dadau ca so'śvibhyāṃ sruvamudyamya mantrataḥ . . 67
1.19.d:
एवमुक्तस्तु विप्रर्षिर्न चोवाचापि किञ्चन ।
भागौ ददौ च सोऽश्विभ्यां स्रुवमुद्यम्य मन्त्रतः ॥ 67
1.19.m: Though thus spoken to, the Brahmin sage said nothing in return; / he raised the sacrificial ladle with a mantra and offered the shares to the two Aśvins.

1.19.s:
atha udyamya bhiduraṃ moktukāmo divaspatiḥ .
stambhitaścyavanenātha savajraḥ sa narādhipa . . 68
1.19.d:
