अथ उद्यम्य भिदुरं मोक्तुकामो दिवस्पतिः ।
स्तम्भितश्च्यवनेनाथ सवज्रः स नराधिप ॥ 68
1.19.m: Then, having raised his thunderbolt, the lord of heaven wished to unleash it, / but with his thunderbolt he was paralyzed by Cyavana, O ruler of men.

1.19.s:
sa stambhayitvātvindraṃ tu bhāgaṃ dattvāśvinorvaśī .
samāpayāmāsa tadā yajñakarma yathārthavat . . 69
1.19.d:
स स्तम्भयित्वात्विन्द्रं तु भागं दत्त्वाश्विनोर्वशी ।
समापयामास तदा यज्ञकर्म यथार्थवत् ॥ 69
1.19.m: Having paralyzed Indra and given the share to the two Aśvins, the self-controlled one / then completed the sacrificial rite according to rule.

1.19.s:
kañjajo'thājagāmāśu āha ca cyavanaṃ tadā .
uttaṃbhyatāmayaṃ lekho bhāgaścāstvaśvinoriha ..1.19.70
1.19.d:
कञ्जजोऽथाजगामाशु आह च च्यवनं तदा ।
उत्तंभ्यतामयं लेखो भागश्चास्त्वश्विनोरिह ॥1.19.70
1.19.m: Then the lotus-born [Brahmā] arrived quickly and said to Cyavana: / 'Let this god be released from paralysis, and let the share here belong to the two Aśvins.'

1.19.s:
tathendrastamuvācedaṃ cyavanaṃ prītamānasaḥ .
jānāmi śaktiṃ tapasaścyavaneha tavottamām ..7 1
khyāpanārthaṃ hi tapasastava etatkṛtaṃ mayā .
adyaprabhṛti bhāgo'stu devatvaṃ cāśvinostathā ..72
1.19.d:
तथेन्द्रस्तमुवाचेदं च्यवनं प्रीतमानसः ।
जानामि शक्तिं तपसश्च्यवनेह तवोत्तमाम् ॥7 1
ख्यापनार्थं हि तपसस्तव एतत्कृतं मया ।
अद्यप्रभृति भागोऽस्तु देवत्वं चाश्विनोस्तथा ॥72
1.19.m: Then Indra, with a pleased mind, said this to Cyavana: / 'I know the superior power of your austerity here, O Cyavana! / This was done by me only to make known the power of your austerity. / From this day forth, let the sacrificial share and godhood belong to the two Aśvins.

1.19.s:
yastvimāṃ tapasaḥ khyātiṃ tvadīyāṃ vai paṭhiṣyati .
śṛṇuyādvāpi śuddhātmā tasya puṇyaphalaṃ śṛṇu ..73
1.19.d:
यस्त्विमां तपसः ख्यातिं त्वदीयां वै पठिष्यति ।
शृणुयाद्वापि शुद्धात्मा तस्य पुण्यफलं शृणु ॥73
1.19.m: Whoever, with a pure soul, recites or hears / this renown of your asceticism—hear the meritorious fruit thereof:

1.19.s:
virocanasado gatvā gatvā puṣpasadastathā .
kāle'tha vāmadevasya muñjakeśasadastathā ..
yauvanayuktaḥ sa krīḍāstiṣṭhatīti na saṃśayaḥ ..74
1.19.d:
विरोचनसदो गत्वा गत्वा पुष्पसदस्तथा ।
कालेऽथ वामदेवस्य मुञ्जकेशसदस्तथा ॥
यौवनयुक्तः स क्रीडास्तिष्ठतीति न संशयः ॥74
1.19.m: Having gone to the abode of Virocana, and having gone to the flower-abode, / and in due time to the abode of Vāmadeva and Muñjakeśa, / he dwells sporting, endowed with youth, without a doubt.'

1.19.s:
evamuktvā jagāmāśu devaḥ svabhavanaṃ vaśī .
cyavano'pi sabhāryo vai śayārtiścāśramaṃ gataḥ ..75
1.19.d:
एवमुक्त्वा जगामाशु देवः स्वभवनं वशी ।
च्यवनोऽपि सभार्यो वै शयार्तिश्चाश्रमं गतः ॥75
1.19.m: Having spoken thus, the self-controlled god went swiftly to his own abode; / Cyavana too, with his wife, and Śaryāti returned to the hermitage.

1.19.s:
athāpaśyadvimānābhaṃ bhavanaṃ devanirmitam .
śayyāsanavarairjuṣṭaṃ sarvakāmasamṛddhimat ..76
1.19.d:
अथापश्यद्विमानाभं भवनं देवनिर्मितम् ।
शय्यासनवरैर्जुष्टं सर्वकामसमृद्धिमत् ॥76
1.19.m: Then he saw a mansion resembling a celestial chariot, crafted by the gods, / furnished with excellent couches and seats, abundant with every desired object,

1.19.s:
1udyānavāpibhirjuṣṭaṃ devendreṇa samāhṛtam .
2gokhaṇḍasannibhaṃ reje gṛhaṃ tadbhuvi durlabham ..77
1.19.d:
1उद्यानवापिभिर्जुष्टं देवेन्द्रेण समाहृतम् ।
2गोखण्डसन्निभं रेजे गृहं तद्भुवि दुर्लभम् ॥77
1.19.m: provided with gardens and reservoirs, provided by the lord of the gods; / that house, shining like a paradise, was rare upon the earth.

1.19.s:
subhūṣaṇāni divyāni ratnavanti mahānti ca .
arajānsi ca vastrāṇi divyaprāvaraṇāni ca . .78
1.19.d:
सुभूषणानि दिव्यानि रत्नवन्ति महान्ति च ।
अरजान्सि च वस्त्राणि दिव्यप्रावरणानि च ॥78
1.19.m: Splendid divine ornaments, large and studded with jewels, / dust-free garments, and celestial coverings [were there].

1.19.s:
tatsarvamakhilaṃ saha patnyā mahāmuniḥ .
mudaṃ paramikāṃ lebhe śakraṃ ca praśaśaṃsa ha ..79
1.19.d:
तत्सर्वमखिलं सह पत्न्या महामुनिः ।
मुदं परमिकां लेभे शक्रं च प्रशशंस ह ॥79
1.19.m: Beholding all that in its entirety together with his wife, the great sage / attained supreme joy and praised Śakra.

1.19.s:
evamiṣṭā tithiriyaṃ dvitīyā aśvinornṛpa .
devatvaṃ yajñabhāgaṃ ca samprāptāviha bhārata ..1.19.80
1.19.d:
एवमिष्टा तिथिरियं द्वितीया अश्विनोर्नृप ।
देवत्वं यज्ञभागं च सम्प्राप्ताविह भारत ॥1.19.80
1.19.m: Thus this second lunar day is beloved of the Aśvins, O king; / here they attained godhood and their sacrificial share, O descendant of Bharata.

1.19.s:
upoṣyā vidhinā yena taṃ śṛṇuṣva narādhipa .
rūpaṃ surūpaṃ yo vāñcheddvitīyāyāṃ narādhipa . . 81
1.19.d:
उपोष्या विधिना येन तं शृणुष्व नराधिप ।
रूपं सुरूपं यो वाञ्छेद्द्वितीयायां नराधिप ॥ 81
1.19.m: Hear, O ruler of men, the rule by which it should be kept as a fast / by anyone who desires handsome beauty on the second lunar day, O ruler of men.

1.19.s:
kārtike śuklapakṣasya dvitīyāyāṃ narādhipa .
puṣpāhāro varṣamekaṃ bhavetsa niyatātmavān . . 82
1.19.d:
कार्तिके शुक्लपक्षस्य द्वितीयायां नराधिप ।
पुष्पाहारो वर्षमेकं भवेत्स नियतात्मवान् ॥ 82
1.19.m: On the second lunar day of the bright fortnight in Kārtika, O ruler of men, / self-controlled, one should eat only flowers for one year.

1.19.s:
kālaprāptāni yāni syurhaviṣyaṃ kusumāni tu .
bhuñjīyāttāni dattvā tu brāhmaṇebhyo narādhipa . . 83
1.19.d:
कालप्राप्तानि यानि स्युर्हविष्यं कुसुमानि तु ।
भुञ्जीयात्तानि दत्त्वा तु ब्राह्मणेभ्यो नराधिप ॥ 83
1.19.m: Whatever blossoms of the season may be fit for sacrificial food, / one should eat them after giving them to the brāhmaṇas, O ruler of men.

1.19.s:
sauvarṇaraupyapuṣpāṇi atha vā jalajāni 1 ca .
vratānte tasya santuṣṭau devau tribhuvane'śvinau . . 84
1.19.d:
सौवर्णरौप्यपुष्पाणि अथ वा जलजानि 1 च ।
व्रतान्ते तस्य सन्तुष्टौ देवौ त्रिभुवनेऽश्विनौ ॥ 84
1.19.m: At the conclusion of the votive observance, offering gold, silver, / or water-born flowers, the two Aśvins, gods in the three worlds, are pleased with him.

1.19.s:
dadatuḥ kāmagaṃ divyaṃ vimānamatitejasam .
suciraṃ divi nārībhirloke'sau ramate'śvinoḥ . . 85
1.19.d:
ददतुः कामगं दिव्यं विमानमतितेजसम् ।
सुचिरं दिवि नारीभिर्लोकेऽसौ रमतेऽश्विनोः ॥ 85
1.19.m: They grant him a divine celestial chariot that moves at will and shines with supreme splendour. / For a very long time in heaven, he rejoices with women in the world of the Aśvins.

1.19.s:
iha cāgatya kalpānte jāto vipraḥ puraskṛtaḥ .
vedavedāṃgaviduṣaḥ saptajanmāntarāṇyasau . . 86
1.19.d:
इह चागत्य कल्पान्ते जातो विप्रः पुरस्कृतः ।
वेदवेदांगविदुषः सप्तजन्मान्तराण्यसौ ॥ 86
1.19.m: And coming here at the end of the kalpa, he is born as an honoured brāhmaṇa, / learned in the Vedas and the Vedāṅgas for seven consecutive births.

1.19.s:
jāto jāto bhavedvidvānbrāhmaṇo'sau kṛte yuge .
dātā yajñapatirvāgmī ādhivyādhivivarjitaḥ . . 87
1.19.d:
जातो जातो भवेद्विद्वान्ब्राह्मणोऽसौ कृते युगे ।
दाता यज्ञपतिर्वाग्मी आधिव्याधिविवर्जितः ॥ 87
1.19.m: Born repeatedly in the Kṛta Yuga, he becomes a learned brāhmaṇa, / generous, master of sacrifices, eloquent, and free from mental agony and physical disease.

1.19.s:
putrapautraiḥ parivṛtaḥ saha pantyā'vasacciram .
madhyadeśe sunagare 2 dharmiṣṭho rājyabhāgbhavet . . 88
1.19.d:
पुत्रपौत्रैः परिवृतः सह पन्त्याऽवसच्चिरम् ।
मध्यदेशे सुनगरे 2 धर्मिष्ठो राज्यभाग्भवेत् ॥ 88
1.19.m: Surrounded by sons and grandsons, he dwells long with his wife. / In an excellent city of Madhyadeśa, righteous, he obtains a kingdom.

1.19.s:
ityeṣā kathitā tubhyaṃ dvitīyā puṣpasaṃjñitā .
phalasaṃjñā tathānyā syātsute vai muñjakeśini . . 89
1.19.d:
इत्येषा कथिता तुभ्यं द्वितीया पुष्पसंज्ञिता ।
फलसंज्ञा तथान्या स्यात्सुते वै मुञ्जकेशिनि ॥ 89
1.19.m: Thus has the second lunar day named Puṣpā been related to you; / likewise, another known as Phalā exists, O son, for Muñjakeśin.

1.19.s:
suṣṭhu puṇyā pāpaharā viṣṭaraśravasaḥ priyā .
aśūnyaśayanā loke prakhyātā kurunandana . . 1.19.90
1.19.d:
सुष्ठु पुण्या पापहरा विष्टरश्रवसः प्रिया ।
अशून्यशयना लोके प्रख्याता कुरुनन्दन ॥ 1.19.90
1.19.m: Exceedingly auspicious, destroying sin, dear to Viṣṇu, / it is renowned in the world as Aśūnyaśayanā, O delight of the Kurus.

1.19.s:
tāmupoṣya naro rājañchraddhābhaktipuraskṛtaḥ .
ṛddhiṃ vṛddhiṃ śriyaṃ vātha bhāryayā saha modate . . 91
aśūnyaśayanā nāmnyāḥ dvitīyātithermahattvam
1.19.d:
तामुपोष्य नरो राजञ्छ्रद्धाभक्तिपुरस्कृतः ।
ऋद्धिं वृद्धिं श्रियं वाथ भार्यया सह मोदते ॥ 91
अशून्यशयना नाम्न्याः द्वितीयातिथेर्महत्त्वम्
1.19.m:
Fasting on it, O king, endued with faith and devotion, / a man rejoices with his wife in prosperity, growth, and fortune.
The greatness of the second lunar day named Aśūnyaśayanā.

1.20.s:
śatānīka uvāca
brūhi me dvijaśārdūla dvitīyāṃ phalasaṃjñitām .
yāmupoṣya naro yoṣidviyogaṃ neha gacchati . . 1
1.20.d:
शतानीक उवाच
ब्रूहि मे द्विजशार्दूल द्वितीयां फलसंज्ञिताम् ।
यामुपोष्य नरो योषिद्वियोगं नेह गच्छति ॥ 1
1.20.m: Śatānīka said: / Tell me, O tiger among the twice-born, of the second lunar day named Phalā, / by fasting on which a man here does not suffer separation from a woman;

1.20.s:
patnyā naro muniśreṣṭha bhāryā ca patinā 1 saha .
tāmahaṃ śrotumicchāmi vidhavā strī na jāyate . .
upoṣitena yenārya patnyā ca sahito naraḥ . . 2
1.20.d:
पत्न्या नरो मुनिश्रेष्ठ भार्या च पतिना 1 सह ।
तामहं श्रोतुमिच्छामि विधवा स्त्री न जायते ॥
उपोषितेन येनार्य पत्न्या च सहितो नरः ॥ 2
1.20.m: A man from his wife, O best of sages, and a wife from her husband. / I desire to hear about that by which a woman does not become a widow, / [and] by fasting on which, O noble one, a man remains united with his wife.

1.20.s:
tanme brūhi dvijaśreṣṭha śreyo'rthaṃ narayoṣitām .
yena me kautukaṃ brahmañchrutvāpūrvaṃ prasarpati . . 3
1.20.d:
तन्मे ब्रूहि द्विजश्रेष्ठ श्रेयोऽर्थं नरयोषिताम् ।
येन मे कौतुकं ब्रह्मञ्छ्रुत्वापूर्वं प्रसर्पति ॥ 3
1.20.m: Tell that to me, O best of the twice-born, for the welfare of men and women, / whereby, having heard it anew, O brāhmaṇa, my curiosity is aroused.

1.20.s:
sumanturuvāca
aśūnyaśayanāṃ nāma dvitīyāṃ śṛṇu bhārata .
yāmupoṣya na vaidhavyaṃ strī prayāti narādhipa . .
patnīviyuktaśca naro na kadācitprajāyate . .4
1.20.d:
सुमन्तुरुवाच
अशून्यशयनां नाम द्वितीयां शृणु भारत ।
यामुपोष्य न वैधव्यं स्त्री प्रयाति नराधिप ॥
पत्नीवियुक्तश्च नरो न कदाचित्प्रजायते ॥4
1.20.m: Sumantu said: / Hear of the second lunar day named Aśūnyaśayanā, O Bhārata, / by fasting on which, O ruler of men, a woman does not suffer widowhood, / and a man is never born separated from his wife.

1.20.s:
śete jagatpatiḥ kṛṣṇaḥ śriyā sārdhaṃ yadā nṛpa .
aśūnyaśayanā nāma tadā grāhyā hi sā tithiḥ . . 5
1.20.d:
शेते जगत्पतिः कृष्णः श्रिया सार्धं यदा नृप ।
अशून्यशयना नाम तदा ग्राह्या हि सा तिथिः ॥ 5
1.20.m: When Kṛṣṇa, the lord of the universe, lies down together with Śrī, O king, / then indeed that lunar day should be observed, known as Aśūnyaśayanā.

1.20.s:
kṛṣṇapakṣe dvitīyāyāṃ śrāvaṇe māsi bhārata .
idamuccārayetsnātaḥ praṇamya jagataḥ patim . .
śrīvatsadhāriṇaṃ devaṃ bhaktyābhyarcya śriyā saha . . 6
1.20.d:
कृष्णपक्षे द्वितीयायां श्रावणे मासि भारत ।
इदमुच्चारयेत्स्नातः प्रणम्य जगतः पतिम् ॥
श्रीवत्सधारिणं देवं भक्त्याभ्यर्च्य श्रिया सह ॥ 6
1.20.m: On the second lunar day of the dark fortnight in the month of Śrāvaṇa, O Bhārata, / having bathed, bowing down to the lord of the universe, / having devoutly worshipped with Śrī the god who bears the Śrīvatsa, one should recite this:

1.20.s:
śrīvatsadhāriñchrīkānta śrīvatsa śrīpate'vyaya .
gārhasthyaṃ mā praṇāśaṃ me yātu dharmārthakāmadam . . 7
1.20.d:
श्रीवत्सधारिञ्छ्रीकान्त श्रीवत्स श्रीपतेऽव्यय ।
गार्हस्थ्यं मा प्रणाशं मे यातु धर्मार्थकामदम् ॥ 7
1.20.m: 'O bearer of the Śrīvatsa, O beloved of Śrī, O Śrīvatsa, O Lord of Śrī, O imperishable one! / May my householder's life, which grants duty, wealth, and desire, never perish.

1.20.s: gāvaśca mā praṇaśyantu mā praṇaśyantu me janāḥ . . 8
1.20.d: गावश्च मा प्रणश्यन्तु मा प्रणश्यन्तु मे जनाः ॥ 8
1.20.m: May my cattle not perish, and may my people not perish.

1.20.s:
jāmayo mā praṇaśyantu matto dāmpatyabhedataḥ .
lakṣmyā viyujye'haṃ deva na kadācidyathā bhavān . . 9
1.20.d:
जामयो मा प्रणश्यन्तु मत्तो दाम्पत्यभेदतः ।
लक्ष्म्या वियुज्येऽहं देव न कदाचिद्यथा भवान् ॥ 9
1.20.m: May my female kin not perish from me through division of husband and wife. / O God, just as you are never separated from Lakṣmī,

1.20.s:
tathā kalatrasambandho deva mā me viyujyatām .
lakṣmyā na śūnyaṃ varada yathā te śayanaṃ sadā . . 1.20.10
1.20.d:
तथा कलत्रसम्बन्धो देव मा मे वियुज्यताम् ।
लक्ष्म्या न शून्यं वरद यथा ते शयनं सदा ॥ 1.20.10
1.20.m: O God, so let not my union with my wife be broken. / Just as your couch is never empty of Lakṣmī, O granter of boons,

1.20.s:
śayyā mamāpyaśūnyāstu tathā tu madhusūdana .
evaṃ pramādya pūjāṃ ca kṛtvā lakṣmyāstathā hareḥ . . 11
1.20.d:
शय्या ममाप्यशून्यास्तु तथा तु मधुसूदन ।
एवं प्रमाद्य पूजां च कृत्वा लक्ष्म्यास्तथा हरेः ॥ 11
1.20.m: so also let my bed not be empty, O Madhusūdana!' / Having thus bowed down and worshipped Lakṣmī and Hari,

1.20.s:
phalāni dadyācchāyāyāmabhīṣṭāni jagatpatim .
naktaṃ 1 praṇamyāyatane havirbhuñjīta vāgyataḥ . . 12
1.20.d:
फलानि दद्याच्छायायामभीष्टानि जगत्पतिम् ।
नक्तं 1 प्रणम्यायतने हविर्भुञ्जीत वाग्यतः ॥ 12
1.20.m: one should present desirable fruits on the bed to the lord of the universe. / At night, having bowed down at the shrine, restrained in speech, one should eat sacrificial food.

1.20.s: brāhmaṇāya dvitīye'hni śaktyā dadyācca dakṣiṇām . . 13
1.20.d: ब्राह्मणाय द्वितीयेऽह्नि शक्त्या दद्याच्च दक्षिणाम् ॥ 13
1.20.m: And on the second day, one should give a priestly fee to a brāhmaṇa according to one's means.

1.20.s:
śatānīka uvāca
kāni tāni abhīṣṭāni keśavasya phalāni tu .
yojyāni śayane vipra devadevasya kathyatām . . 14
1.20.d:
शतानीक उवाच
कानि तानि अभीष्टानि केशवस्य फलानि तु ।
योज्यानि शयने विप्र देवदेवस्य कथ्यताम् ॥ 14
1.20.m: Śatānīka said: / What are those desirable fruits of Keśava / to be offered on the bed of the god of gods? Let it be told, O brāhmaṇa.

1.20.s:
kiṃ ca dānaṃ dvitīye'hni dātavyaṃ brāhmaṇasya tu .
bhaktairnarairdvijaśreṣṭha devadevasya śaktitaḥ . . 15
1.20.d:
किं च दानं द्वितीयेऽह्नि दातव्यं ब्राह्मणस्य तु ।
भक्तैर्नरैर्द्विजश्रेष्ठ देवदेवस्य शक्तितः ॥ 15
1.20.m: And what gift is to be given to a brāhmaṇa on the second day / by devoted men according to their means, O best of the twice-born, for the god of gods?

1.20.s:
sumanturuvāca
yāni tatra mahābāho kāle santi phalāni tu.
madhurāṇi sutīvrāṇi na cāpi kaṭukāni tu . . 16
1.20.d:
सुमन्तुरुवाच
यानि तत्र महाबाहो काले सन्ति फलानि तु।
मधुराणि सुतीव्राणि न चापि कटुकानि तु ॥ 16
1.20.m: Sumantu said: / Whatever fruits exist in that season, O mighty-armed one, / that are sweet, and neither very sharp nor pungent,

1.20.s:
dātavyāni nṛpaśreṣṭha svaśaktyā śayane nṛpa .
madhurāṇi pradattāni naro vallabhatāṃ yajet . . 17
1.20.d:
दातव्यानि नृपश्रेष्ठ स्वशक्त्या शयने नृप ।
मधुराणि प्रदत्तानि नरो वल्लभतां यजेत् ॥ 17
1.20.m: are to be offered on the bed according to one's ability, O king. / If sweet ones are presented, a man attains belovedness;

1.20.s:
yoṣicca kuruśārdūla bharturvallabhatāmiyāt .
tasmātkaṭukatīvrāṇi strīliṅgāni vivarjayet . . 18
1.20.d:
योषिच्च कुरुशार्दूल भर्तुर्वल्लभतामियात् ।
तस्मात्कटुकतीव्राणि स्त्रीलिङ्गानि विवर्जयेत् ॥ 18
1.20.m: and a woman, O tiger of the Kurus, attains the love of her husband. / Therefore, one should avoid pungent, sharp fruits of feminine gender.

1.20.s:
kharjūramātuliṅgāni śvetena śirasā saha .
phalāni śayane rājanyajñabhāgaharasya tu . . 19
1.20.d:
खर्जूरमातुलिङ्गानि श्वेतेन शिरसा सह ।
फलानि शयने राजन्यज्ञभागहरस्य तु ॥ 19
1.20.m: Dates and citrons with white tips— / such fruits on the bed, O king, of the recipient of the sacrificial share,

1.20.s:
deyāni kuruśārdūla svaśaktyā muñjakeśine .
etānyeva tu viprasya gāṅgeyasahitāni tu . . 1.20.20
1.20.d:
देयानि कुरुशार्दूल स्वशक्त्या मुञ्जकेशिने ।
एतान्येव तु विप्रस्य गाङ्गेयसहितानि तु ॥ 1.20.20
1.20.m: are to be offered to Muñjakeśin according to one's means, O tiger of the Kurus. / These very same, along with gold,

1.20.s:
dvitīye'hni pradeyāni bhaktyā śaktyā ca bhārata .
vāsodānaṃ tathā dhānyaphaladānasamanvitam . .
gāṅgeyasya viśeṣeṇa dhānyadānaṃ pracakṣate . . 21
1.20.d:
द्वितीयेऽह्नि प्रदेयानि भक्त्या शक्त्या च भारत ।
वासोदानं तथा धान्यफलदानसमन्वितम् ॥
गाङ्गेयस्य विशेषेण धान्यदानं प्रचक्षते ॥ 21
1.20.m: should be presented to a brāhmaṇa on the second day with devotion and according to one's means, O Bhārata, / together with a gift of cloth, grain, and fruit. / They especially praise the gift of grain along with gold.

1.20.s:
evaṃ karoti yaḥ samyaṅnaro māsacatuṣṭayam .
tato janmatrayaṃ vīra gṛhabhaṅgo na jāyate . . 22
1.20.d:
एवं करोति यः सम्यङ्नरो मासचतुष्टयम् ।
ततो जन्मत्रयं वीर गृहभङ्गो न जायते ॥ 22
1.20.m: Whatever man performs this properly for four months, / for three births after that, O hero, no ruin of his home occurs.

1.20.s:
aśūnyaśayanaścāsau dharmakāmārthasādhanaḥ .
bhavatyavyāhataiśvaryaḥ puruṣo nātra saṃśayaḥ . . 23
1.20.d:
अशून्यशयनश्चासौ धर्मकामार्थसाधनः ।
भवत्यव्याहतैश्वर्यः पुरुषो नात्र संशयः ॥ 23
1.20.m: His bed never empty, he achieves duty, desire, and wealth; / a man attains unhindered sovereignty—there is no doubt of this.

1.20.s:
1nārī ca rājandharmajñā vratametadyathāvidhi .
yā karoti na sā śocyā bandhuvargasya jāyate . . 24
1.20.d:
1नारी च राजन्धर्मज्ञा व्रतमेतद्यथाविधि ।
या करोति न सा शोच्या बन्धुवर्गस्य जायते ॥ 24
1.20.m: And the woman who knows dharma, O king, and performs this votive observance according to rule, / does not become a cause of grief for her kin.

1.20.s:
vaidhavyaṃ durbhagatvaṃ ca bhartṛtyāgaṃ ca sattama .
nāpnoti janma triyatametaccīrtvā2 mahāvratam . . 25
1.20.d:
वैधव्यं दुर्भगत्वं च भर्तृत्यागं च सत्तम ।
नाप्नोति जन्म त्रियतमेतच्चीर्त्वा2 महाव्रतम् ॥ 25
1.20.m: Widowhood, misfortune, and abandonment by her husband, O best of men, / she never meets for three hundred births, having performed this great votive observance.

1.20.s:
adattvā kaṭukānīha phalāni kurunandana .
kharjūramātuliṅgāni bṛhatphalaśirāṃsi ca . . 26
1.20.d:
अदत्त्वा कटुकानीह फलानि कुरुनन्दन ।
खर्जूरमातुलिङ्गानि बृहत्फलशिरांसि च ॥ 26
1.20.m: Not giving pungent fruits here, O delight of the Kurus, / [but] dates, citrons, and large-topped fruits,

1.20.s:
dattvā dvijebhyo rājendra madhurāṇi parāṇi ca .
tasmātsvaśaktyā yattena deyāni madhurāṇi ca . . 27
1.20.d:
दत्त्वा द्विजेभ्यो राजेन्द्र मधुराणि पराणि च ।
तस्मात्स्वशक्त्या यत्तेन देयानि मधुराणि च ॥ 27
1.20.m: having given other sweet ones to the twice-born, O lord of kings; / therefore, sweet ones should be given with effort according to one's means.

1.20.s:
ityeṣā kathitā kṛṣṇadvitīyā tithiruttamā .
yāmupoṣya naro rājannṛddhiṃ vṛddhiṃ tathā vrajet . . 28
1.20.d:
इत्येषा कथिता कृष्णद्वितीया तिथिरुत्तमा ।
यामुपोष्य नरो राजन्नृद्धिं वृद्धिं तथा व्रजेत् ॥ 28
1.20.m: Thus has the excellent second lunar day of the dark fortnight been related, / by fasting on which a man attains prosperity and growth, O king.

1.20.s:
śatānīka uvāca
bhavatā kathiteyaṃ vai dvitīyā tithiruttamā .
aśvibhyāṃ dvijaśārdūla kathamasyāṃ janārdanaḥ . . 29
1.20.d:
शतानीक उवाच
भवता कथितेयं वै द्वितीया तिथिरुत्तमा ।
अश्विभ्यां द्विजशार्दूल कथमस्यां जनार्दनः ॥ 29
1.20.m: Śatānīka said: / This excellent second lunar day was spoken of by you / as belonging to the two Aśvins, O tiger among the twice-born. How then is Janārdana

1.20.s:
sampūjyaḥ phalasaṃjñāyāṃ kathitaḥ padmayā saha .
tadatra kautukaṃ mahyaṃ sumahajjāyate dvija . . 1.20.30
1.20.d:
सम्पूज्यः फलसंज्ञायां कथितः पद्मया सह ।
तदत्र कौतुकं मह्यं सुमहज्जायते द्विज ॥ 1.20.30
1.20.m: said to be worshipped on this [day] called Phalā along with Padmā? / Therefore, very great curiosity arises in me on this point, O twice-born one.

1.20.s:
sumanturuvāca
evametanna sandeho tathā vadasi bhārata .
aśvinorvai tithiriyaṃ kiṃ tu vākyaṃ nibodha me . . 31
1.20.d:
सुमन्तुरुवाच
एवमेतन्न सन्देहो तथा वदसि भारत ।
अश्विनोर्वै तिथिरियं किं तु वाक्यं निबोध मे ॥ 31
1.20.m: Sumantu said: / It is just so, there is no doubt, as you say, O Bhārata; / this lunar day indeed belongs to the Aśvins. But hear my words:

1.20.s:
aśūnyaśayanā dattā 1viṣṇoramitatejasaḥ .
aśvibhyāṃ kuru śārdūla prītaye muñjakeśinaḥ . . 32
1.20.d:
अशून्यशयना दत्ता 1विष्णोरमिततेजसः ।
अश्विभ्यां कुरु शार्दूल प्रीतये मुञ्जकेशिनः ॥ 32
1.20.m: Aśūnyaśayanā was given to Viṣṇu of immeasurable splendour / by the two Aśvins, O tiger of the Kurus, for the pleasure of Muñjakeśin.

1.20.s:
tāveva kuruśārdūla pūjyete'tra mahīpate .
nāsatyau bhagavānviṣṇurdattaśca śrīrvibhāvyate . . 33
iti śrībhaviṣye mahāpurāṇe śatārddhasāhasryāṃ saṃhitāyāṃ brāhme parvaṇi
dvitīyākalpasamāptau viṃśo'dhyāyaḥ . 20 .
tṛtīyātithivratamāhātmyam
1.20.d:
तावेव कुरुशार्दूल पूज्येतेऽत्र महीपते ।
नासत्यौ भगवान्विष्णुर्दत्तश्च श्रीर्विभाव्यते ॥ 33
इति श्रीभविष्ये महापुराणे शतार्द्धसाहस्र्यां संहितायां ब्राह्मे पर्वणि
द्वितीयाकल्पसमाप्तौ विंशोऽध्यायः । 20 ।
तृतीयातिथिव्रतमाहात्म्यम्
1.20.m:
Those two alone, O tiger among the Kurus, are worshipped here, O king: / the Nāsatyas, Lord Viṣṇu, Datta, and Śrī are contemplated.
Thus ends the twentieth chapter in the Brāhmaparvan, on the completion of the procedure for the second lunar day, in the Śatārdhasāhasrī Saṃhitā of the glorious Bhaviṣya Mahāpurāṇa.
The greatness of the votive observance of the third lunar day

1.21.s:
sumantaruvāca
pativratā patiprāṇā patiśuśrūṣaṇe ratā .
evaṃvidhāpi yā proktā śuciḥ saṃśobhanā satī . . 1
1.21.d:
सुमन्तरुवाच
पतिव्रता पतिप्राणा पतिशुश्रूषणे रता ।
एवंविधापि या प्रोक्ता शुचिः संशोभना सती ॥ 1
1.21.m: Sumantu said: / A wife devoted to her husband, having her husband as her life-breath, delighting in attendance on her husband— / even being such, she who is proclaimed pure, radiant, and virtuous,

1.21.s:
sopavāsā tṛtīyāṃ tu lavaṇaṃ parivarjayet .
sā gṛhṇāti ca vai bhaktyā vratamāmaraṇāntikam . . 2
1.21.d:
सोपवासा तृतीयां तु लवणं परिवर्जयेत् ।
सा गृह्णाति च वै भक्त्या व्रतमामरणान्तिकम् ॥ 2
1.21.m: fasting on the third lunar day, should avoid salt. / And she undertakes with devotion this votive observance that lasts until death.

1.21.s:
gaurī dadāti santuṣṭā rūpaṃ saubhāgyameva ca .
lāvaṇyaṃ lalitaṃ hṛdyaṃ ślāghyaṃ puṃsāṃ manoramam . . 3
1.21.d:
गौरी ददाति सन्तुष्टा रूपं सौभाग्यमेव च ।
लावण्यं ललितं हृद्यं श्लाघ्यं पुंसां मनोरमम् ॥ 3
1.21.m: Gaurī, being pleased, bestows beauty and good fortune, / charm that is delicate, endearing, praiseworthy, and delightful to men.

1.21.s:
puṃso manoramā nārī bharttā nāryā manoramaḥ .
gaurīvratena bhavati rājam̐llavaṇavarjanāt . . 4
1.21.d:
पुंसो मनोरमा नारी भर्त्ता नार्या मनोरमः ।
गौरीव्रतेन भवति राजम्̐ल्लवणवर्जनात् ॥ 4
1.21.m: A woman becomes delightful to a man, and a husband delightful to a woman, / through the votive observance of Gaurī by abandoning salt, O king.

1.21.s:
idaṃ vrataṃ prati vibho dharmarājasya śṛṇvataḥ .
umayā ca purā proktaṃ yadvākyaṃ tannibodha me . . 5
1.21.d:
इदं व्रतं प्रति विभो धर्मराजस्य शृण्वतः ।
उमया च पुरा प्रोक्तं यद्वाक्यं तन्निबोध मे ॥ 5
1.21.m: Regarding this votive observance, O mighty one, hear from me the speech / that was spoken long ago by Umā to Dharmarāja as he listened:

1.21.s:
mayā vratamidaṃ sṛṣṭaṃ saubhāgyakaraṇaṃ nṛṇām .
martye tu niyatā nārī vratametaccariṣyati . .
saha bhartrā sa modeta yathā bhartā haro mama . . 6
1.21.d:
मया व्रतमिदं सृष्टं सौभाग्यकरणं नृणाम् ।
मर्त्ये तु नियता नारी व्रतमेतच्चरिष्यति ॥
सह भर्त्रा स मोदेत यथा भर्ता हरो मम ॥ 6
1.21.m: “This votive observance was created by me to bestow good fortune on human beings. / In the mortal realm, a restrained woman will perform this votive observance; / she will rejoice with her husband, just as my husband Hara [rejoices with me].

1.21.s:
yā ca kanyā na bhartāraṃ vindate śobhanā satī .
sā tvidaṃ vratamuddiśya bhavedakṣārabhojanā . .
maccittā manmanāḥ kuryānmadbhaktā matparigrahā . . 7
1.21.d:
या च कन्या न भर्तारं विन्दते शोभना सती ।
सा त्विदं व्रतमुद्दिश्य भवेदक्षारभोजना ॥
मच्चित्ता मन्मनाः कुर्यान्मद्भक्ता मत्परिग्रहा ॥ 7
1.21.m: And an unmarried girl, beautiful and virtuous, who does not obtain a husband, / should eat food free of salt with this votive observance as her goal. / With mind on me, with thought on me, devoted to me, and accepting me, she should perform it.

1.21.s:
gaurīṃ saṃsthāpya sauvarṇīṃ gandhālaṅkārabhūṣitām .
vastrālaṅkārasaṃvītāṃ puṣpamaṇḍalamaṇḍitām . . 8
lavaṇaṃ guḍaṃ ghṛtaṃ tailaṃ devyai śaktyā nivedayet . 1
1.21.d:
गौरीं संस्थाप्य सौवर्णीं गन्धालङ्कारभूषिताम् ।
वस्त्रालङ्कारसंवीतां पुष्पमण्डलमण्डिताम् ॥ 8
लवणं गुडं घृतं तैलं देव्यै शक्त्या निवेदयेत् । 1
1.21.m:
Having installed a golden image of Gaurī, adorned with perfumes and ornaments, / clothed in garments and adornments, and decorated with a circle of flowers,
she should offer salt, jaggery, clarified butter, and oil to the goddess according to her ability,

1.21.s: kaṭukhaṇḍaṃ jīrakaṃ ca patraśākaṃ ca bhārata . . 9
1.21.d: कटुखण्डं जीरकं च पत्रशाकं च भारत ॥ 9
1.21.m: and pieces of pungent roots, cumin, and leafy vegetables, O Bhārata,

1.21.s:
guḍaghṛṣṭāṃstathāpūpānkhaḍaveṣṭāṃstathā nṛpa .
brāhmaṇe vratasampanne pradadyātsubahuśrute . . 1.21.10
1.21.d:
गुडघृष्टांस्तथापूपान्खडवेष्टांस्तथा नृप ।
ब्राह्मणे व्रतसम्पन्ने प्रदद्यात्सुबहुश्रुते ॥ 1.21.10
1.21.m: as well as cakes smeared with jaggery and pastries fried in ghee, O king; / she should give them to a learned brāhmaṇa accomplished in votive observances.

1.21.s:
śuklapakṣe sadā deyā yathā śaktyā hiraṇmayī .
dhanahīne tu bhaktyā2 ca madhuvṛkṣamayī nṛpa . . 11
1.21.d:
शुक्लपक्षे सदा देया यथा शक्त्या हिरण्मयी ।
धनहीने तु भक्त्या2 च मधुवृक्षमयी नृप ॥ 11
1.21.m: In the bright fortnight, a golden image should always be given according to one’s means, / but if devoid of wealth, O king, an image made of madhūka wood [may be given] with devotion.

1.21.s:
arcyā nityaṃ saṃnidhānāttatra gaurī na saṃśayaḥ .
akṣāralavaṇaṃ rātrau bhuṃkte caiva suvāgyatā . . 12
1.21.d:
अर्च्या नित्यं संनिधानात्तत्र गौरी न संशयः ।
अक्षारलवणं रात्रौ भुंक्ते चैव सुवाग्यता ॥ 12
1.21.m: She should constantly worship Gaurī who is present there, without a doubt; / and restrained in speech, she eats in the night food free of alkaline matter and salt.

1.21.s:
gaurī sannihitā nityaṃ bhūmau prastaraśāyinī3 .
evaṃ niyamayuktasya4 devyā yatsamudāhṛtam . . 13
1.21.d:
गौरी सन्निहिता नित्यं भूमौ प्रस्तरशायिनी3 ।
एवं नियमयुक्तस्य4 देव्या यत्समुदाहृतम् ॥ 13
1.21.m: Gaurī is constantly present, sleeping on the ground on a spread of grass. / What was proclaimed by the goddess for one who maintains such a discipline,

1.21.s:
tacchṛṇuṣva mahābāho kathyamānaṃ mahāphalam .
bhartāraṃ tu labhetkanyā yaṃ vācchati mano'nugam . . 14
1.21.d:
तच्छृणुष्व महाबाहो कथ्यमानं महाफलम् ।
भर्तारं तु लभेत्कन्या यं वाच्छति मनोऽनुगम् ॥ 14
1.21.m: listen to that great fruit being described, O mighty-armed one: / an unmarried girl will obtain the husband whom she desires in accordance with her heart.

1.21.s:
suciraṃ saha vai bhartrā krīḍayitvā5 ihaiva sā .
santatiṃ ca pratiṣṭhāpya saha tenaiva gacchati . . 15
1.21.d:
सुचिरं सह वै भर्त्रा क्रीडयित्वा5 इहैव सा ।
सन्ततिं च प्रतिष्ठाप्य सह तेनैव गच्छति ॥ 15
1.21.m: Having sported for a very long time in this very world with her husband, / and having established her lineage, she departs along with him.

1.21.s:
helilokaṃ candralokaṃ lokaṃ citraśikhaṇḍinaḥ .
gatvā yāti sado rājanvāmadevasya bhārata . . 16
1.21.d:
हेलिलोकं चन्द्रलोकं लोकं चित्रशिखण्डिनः ।
गत्वा याति सदो राजन्वामदेवस्य भारत ॥ 16
1.21.m: Having gone to the world of the sun, the world of the moon, and the world of Citraśikhaṇḍin, / she goes, O king, to the assembly of Vāmadeva, O Bhārata.

1.21.s:
vidhavā tu yadā rājandevyā vrataparāyaṇā6 .
bharttāraṃ niyatā nityaṃ sadārcanaparāyaṇā . . 17
1.21.d:
विधवा तु यदा राजन्देव्या व्रतपरायणा6 ।
भर्त्तारं नियता नित्यं सदार्चनपरायणा ॥ 17
1.21.m: When a widow, O king, is devoted to the goddess’s votive observance, / restrained, always intent on the perpetual worship of her husband,

1.21.s:
iha cotsṛjya dehaṃ svaṃ dṛṣṭvā haripure priyam .
ākṣipya yamadūtebhyaḥ saha bhartrā rameddivi . . 18
1.21.d:
इह चोत्सृज्य देहं स्वं दृष्ट्वा हरिपुरे प्रियम् ।
आक्षिप्य यमदूतेभ्यः सह भर्त्रा रमेद्दिवि ॥ 18
1.21.m: she leaves her body here, sees her beloved in the city of Hari, / snatches him from the messengers of Yama, and rejoices with her husband in heaven.

1.21.s:
varṣakoṭiṃ daśaguṇāṃ ramitvā sā ihāgatā .
bhartrā sahaiva pūrvoktaṃ labhate phalamīpsitam . . 19
1.21.d:
वर्षकोटिं दशगुणां रमित्वा सा इहागता ।
भर्त्रा सहैव पूर्वोक्तं लभते फलमीप्सितम् ॥ 19
1.21.m: Having rejoiced there for a ten-fold crore of years, she comes back to this world, / and along with her husband she obtains the previously described desired fruit.

1.21.s:
indrāṇyāpi vratamidaṃ putrārthinyā narādhipa .
labdhaḥ putro vratasyānte jayanto nāma nāmataḥ . . 1.21.20
1.21.d:
इन्द्राण्यापि व्रतमिदं पुत्रार्थिन्या नराधिप ।
लब्धः पुत्रो व्रतस्यान्ते जयन्तो नाम नामतः ॥ 1.21.20
1.21.m: This votive observance was also observed by Indrāṇī when she desired a son, O ruler of men; / at the end of the votive observance a son was obtained, named Jayanta by name.

1.21.s:
arundhatyā tathā cīrṇaṃ vaśiṣṭhaṃ prati kāmataḥ .
dṛśyate divi cādyāpi vaśiṣṭhasya samīpataḥ . . 21
1.21.d:
अरुन्धत्या तथा चीर्णं वशिष्ठं प्रति कामतः ।
दृश्यते दिवि चाद्यापि वशिष्ठस्य समीपतः ॥ 21
1.21.m: So too it was performed by Arundhatī out of love for Vasiṣṭha; / and even today she is seen in the sky near Vasiṣṭha.

1.21.s:
rohiṇyā lavaṇatyāgātsapannīgaṇamardanam .
labdhaṃ devyāḥ prasādena saubhāgyamacalaṃ divi . . 22
1.21.d:
रोहिण्या लवणत्यागात्सपन्नीगणमर्दनम् ।
लब्धं देव्याः प्रसादेन सौभाग्यमचलं दिवि ॥ 22
1.21.m: By giving up salt, Rohiṇī obtained the subjugation of her co-wives / and unshakeable good fortune in heaven, through the grace of the goddess.

1.21.s:
ityeṣā tithirityeva tṛtīyā lokapūjitā .
sadā viśeṣataḥ puṇyā vaiśākhe māsi yā bhavet . . 23
1.21.d:
इत्येषा तिथिरित्येव तृतीया लोकपूजिता ।
सदा विशेषतः पुण्या वैशाखे मासि या भवेत् ॥ 23
1.21.m: In this way, this third lunar day is revered by the world; / it is always especially holy when it falls in the month of Vaiśākha.

1.21.s:
puṇyā bhādrapade māsi māghepyevaṃ na saṃśayaḥ .
māghe bhādrapade cāpi strīṇāṃ dhanyā1 pracakṣate . . 24
1.21.d:
पुण्या भाद्रपदे मासि माघेप्येवं न संशयः ।
माघे भाद्रपदे चापि स्त्रीणां धन्या1 प्रचक्षते ॥ 24
1.21.m: It is holy in the month of Bhādrapada, and also in Māgha, without a doubt; / in Māgha and in Bhādrapada it is proclaimed to bring good fortune to women.

1.21.s:
sādhāraṇī tu vaiśākhe sarvalokasya bhārata .
māghamāse tṛtīyāyāṃ guḍasya lavaṇasya ca . .
dānaṃ śreyaskaraṃ rājanstrīṇāṃ2 ca puruṣasya ca . . 25
1.21.d:
साधारणी तु वैशाखे सर्वलोकस्य भारत ।
माघमासे तृतीयायां गुडस्य लवणस्य च ॥
दानं श्रेयस्करं राजन्स्त्रीणां2 च पुरुषस्य च ॥ 25
1.21.m: In Vaiśākha it is common to all people, O Bhārata. / On the third lunar day in the month of Māgha, the gift of jaggery and salt / brings welfare, O king, to women and to men.

1.21.s:
guḍena tuṣyate datto lavaṇena tu viśvabhūḥ .
guḍapūpāstu dātavyā māsi bhādrapade tathā . . 26
1.21.d:
गुडेन तुष्यते दत्तो लवणेन तु विश्वभूः ।
गुडपूपास्तु दातव्या मासि भाद्रपदे तथा ॥ 26
1.21.m: Datta is pleased with jaggery, while Viśvabhū is pleased with salt; / and cakes made of jaggery should be given likewise in the month of Bhādrapada.

1.21.s:
tṛtīyāyāṃ tu māghasya vāmadevasya prītaye .
vāridānaṃ praśastaṃ syānmodakānāṃ ca bhārata . . 27
1.21.d:
तृतीयायां तु माघस्य वामदेवस्य प्रीतये ।
वारिदानं प्रशस्तं स्यान्मोदकानां च भारत ॥ 27
1.21.m: On the third lunar day of Māgha, for the pleasure of Vāmadeva, / the gift of water and sweetmeat balls is commended, O Bhārata.

1.21.s:
vaiśākhe māsi rājendra tṛtīyā candanasya ca .
vāriṇā tuṣyate vedhā modakairbhīma eva hi . .
dānāttu candanasyeha kañjajo nātra saṃśayaḥ . . 28
1.21.d:
वैशाखे मासि राजेन्द्र तृतीया चन्दनस्य च ।
वारिणा तुष्यते वेधा मोदकैर्भीम एव हि ॥
दानात्तु चन्दनस्येह कञ्जजो नात्र संशयः ॥ 28
1.21.m: In the month of Vaiśākha, O best of kings, on the third lunar day, / the Creator is pleased with water and sandalwood, and Bhīma indeed with sweetmeat balls; / and from the gift of sandalwood here, the Lotus-born is pleased, there is no doubt.

1.21.s:
yātveṣā kuruśārdūla vaiśākhe māsi vai tithiḥ .
tṛtīyā sā'kṣayā loke gīrvāṇairabhinanditā . . 29
1.21.d:
यात्वेषा कुरुशार्दूल वैशाखे मासि वै तिथिः ।
तृतीया साऽक्षया लोके गीर्वाणैरभिनन्दिता ॥ 29
1.21.m: The lunar day which falls on the third in the month of Vaiśākha, O tiger among the Kurus, / is praised in the world as Akṣayā, applauded by the gods.

1.21.s:
āgateyaṃ mahābāho bhūri candraṃ vasuvratā .
kaladhautaṃ tathānnaṃ ca ghṛtaṃ cāpi viśeṣataḥ . .
yadyaddattaṃ tvakṣayaṃ syātteneyamakṣayā smṛtā . . 1.21.30
1.21.d:
आगतेयं महाबाहो भूरि चन्द्रं वसुव्रता ।
कलधौतं तथान्नं च घृतं चापि विशेषतः ॥
यद्यद्दत्तं त्वक्षयं स्यात्तेनेयमक्षया स्मृता ॥ 1.21.30
1.21.m: When this arrives, O mighty-armed one, bringing abundant vows of wealth, / gold, food, and especially clarified butter— / whatever is given becomes imperishable; therefore it is remembered as Akṣayā.

1.21.s:
yatkiñciddīyate dānaṃ svalpaṃ vā yadi vā bahu .
tatsarvamakṣayaṃ syādvai teneyamakṣayā smṛtā . . 31
1.21.d:
यत्किञ्चिद्दीयते दानं स्वल्पं वा यदि वा बहु ।
तत्सर्वमक्षयं स्याद्वै तेनेयमक्षया स्मृता ॥ 31
1.21.m: Whatever gift is given, whether small or great, / all of that indeed becomes imperishable; therefore it is remembered as Akṣayā.

1.21.s:
yo'syāṃ dadāti karakanvāribījasamanvitān .
sa yāti puruṣo vīra lokaṃ vai hemamālinaḥ . . 32
1.21.d:
योऽस्यां ददाति करकन्वारिबीजसमन्वितान् ।
स याति पुरुषो वीर लोकं वै हेममालिनः ॥ 32
1.21.m: The man who on this day gives water pots provided with water and seeds, / that heroic man goes to the world of the Golden-Garlanded One.

1.21.s:
ityeṣā kathitā vīra tṛtīyā tithiruttamā .
yāmupoṣya naro rājannṛddhiṃ vṛddhiṃ śriyaṃ bhajet . . 33
iti śrībhaviṣye mahāpurāṇe śatārddhasāhasryāṃ brāhme parvaṇi tṛtīyākalpavidhivarṇanaṃ
nāmaikaviṃśo'dhyāyaḥ . 21 .
caturthītithivratamāhātmyam
1.21.d:
इत्येषा कथिता वीर तृतीया तिथिरुत्तमा ।
यामुपोष्य नरो राजन्नृद्धिं वृद्धिं श्रियं भजेत् ॥ 33
इति श्रीभविष्ये महापुराणे शतार्द्धसाहस्र्यां ब्राह्मे पर्वणि तृतीयाकल्पविधिवर्णनं
नामैकविंशोऽध्यायः । 21 ।
चतुर्थीतिथिव्रतमाहात्म्यम्
1.21.m:
Thus has been declared, O hero, the supreme third lunar day, / by fasting on which a man, O king, attains prosperity, growth, and fortune.
Thus ends the twenty-first chapter, entitled “Description of the Rules for the Observance of the Third Lunar Day”, in the Brāhmaparvan, in the Śatārdhasāhasrī [Saṃhitā] of the glorious Bhaviṣya Mahāpurāṇa.
The greatness of the votive observance of the fourth lunar day

1.22.s:
sumanturuvāca
caturthyāṃ tu sadā rājannirāhāravratānvitaḥ .
dattvā tilānnaṃ viprasya svayaṃ bhuṃkte tilaudanam . . 1
1.22.d:
सुमन्तुरुवाच
चतुर्थ्यां तु सदा राजन्निराहारव्रतान्वितः ।
दत्त्वा तिलान्नं विप्रस्य स्वयं भुंक्ते तिलौदनम् ॥ 1
1.22.m: Sumantu said: / On the fourth lunar day, O king, always observing a fast, / having given sesamum food to a vipra, he himself eats sesamum rice.

1.22.s:
varṣadvaye samāptirhi vratasya tu yadā bhavet .
vināyakastasya tuṣṭo dadāti phalamīhitam1 . . 2
1.22.d:
वर्षद्वये समाप्तिर्हि व्रतस्य तु यदा भवेत् ।
विनायकस्तस्य तुष्टो ददाति फलमीहितम्1 ॥ 2
1.22.m: When the completion of the votive observance takes place after two years, / Vināyaka, being pleased, bestows upon him his desired fruit.

1.22.s:
yāti bhāgyanivāsaṃ hi krīḍate vibhavaiḥ saha .
iha cāgatya puṇyānte divyo divyavapuryaśāḥ . . 3
1.22.d:
याति भाग्यनिवासं हि क्रीडते विभवैः सह ।
इह चागत्य पुण्यान्ते दिव्यो दिव्यवपुर्यशाः ॥ 3
1.22.m: He goes to the abode of fortune and sports with riches; / and coming back to this world at the end of his merit, divine, with a divine body and fame,

1.22.s:
matimāndhṛtimānvāgmī bhāgyavānkāmakāravān2 .
asādhyānyapi sādhyeha kṣaṇādeva mahāntyapi . . 4
1.22.d:
मतिमान्धृतिमान्वाग्मी भाग्यवान्कामकारवान्2 ।
असाध्यान्यपि साध्येह क्षणादेव महान्त्यपि ॥ 4
1.22.m: intelligent, resolute, eloquent, fortunate, acting as he desires, / accomplishing instantly even insurmountable and great tasks in this world,

1.22.s:
hantyaśvarathasampannaṃ ṣalīputrasahāyavān .
rājā bhavati dīrghāyuḥ saptajanmānyasau nṛpa . .
etaddadāti santuṣṭo vighnahantā4 vināyakaḥ . . 5
1.22.d:
हन्त्यश्वरथसम्पन्नं षलीपुत्रसहायवान् ।
राजा भवति दीर्घायुः सप्तजन्मान्यसौ नृप ॥
एतद्ददाति सन्तुष्टो विघ्नहन्ता4 विनायकः ॥ 5
1.22.m: equipped with elephants, horses, and chariots, accompanied by strong sons, / he becomes a long-lived king for seven births, O king. / Pleased, the slayer of obstacles, Vināyaka, grants this.

1.22.s:
śatānīka uvāca
vighnaḥ kasya kṛtastena yena vighnavināyakaḥ .
etadvadasva vighneśa vighnakāraṇamadya me . . 6
1.22.d:
शतानीक उवाच
विघ्नः कस्य कृतस्तेन येन विघ्नविनायकः ।
एतद्वदस्व विघ्नेश विघ्नकारणमद्य मे ॥ 6
1.22.m: Śatānīka said: / For whom was an obstacle created by him, on account of which he is the Vināyaka of obstacles? / Tell me today this cause of obstacles, O lord of obstacles.

1.22.s:
sumanturuvāca
kaumāre lakṣaṇe puṃsāṃ strīṇāṃ ca sukṛte kṛte .
vighnaṃ cakāra vighneśo gāṅgeyasya vināyakaḥ . . 7
1.22.d:
सुमन्तुरुवाच
कौमारे लक्षणे पुंसां स्त्रीणां च सुकृते कृते ।
विघ्नं चकार विघ्नेशो गाङ्गेयस्य विनायकः ॥ 7
1.22.m:
Sumantu said:
When the treatise on the marks of men and women was composed by Kumāra,
Vināyaka, the lord of obstacles, caused an obstacle for the son of Gaṅgā.

1.22.s:
taṃ tu vighnaṃ viditvāsau kārttikeyo ruṣānvitaḥ .
utkṛṣya dantaṃ tasyāsyāddhantuṃ taṃ ca samudyataḥ . . 8
1.22.d:
तं तु विघ्नं विदित्वासौ कार्त्तिकेयो रुषान्वितः ।
उत्कृष्य दन्तं तस्यास्याद्धन्तुं तं च समुद्यतः ॥ 8
1.22.m:
Knowing of that obstacle, Kārttikeya, filled with wrath,
pulled a tusk from his mouth and prepared to slay him.

1.22.s:
nivāryāpṛcchaddeveśo roṣaḥ kāryaḥ kutastvayā .
taṃ cācakhyau sa pitre vai kṛtaṃ pūruṣalakṣaṇam . .
tatra vighnakṛte mahyaṃ yoṣitā na ca lakṣaṇam . . 9
1.22.d:
निवार्यापृच्छद्देवेशो रोषः कार्यः कुतस्त्वया ।
तं चाचख्यौ स पित्रे वै कृतं पूरुषलक्षणम् ॥
तत्र विघ्नकृते मह्यं योषिता न च लक्षणम् ॥ 9

1.22.s:
athovāca mahādevaḥ prahasantsvasutaṃ kila .
mama kiṃ lakṣaṇaṃ putra paśyase tvaṃ vadasva me . . 1.22.10
1.22.d:
अथोवाच महादेवः प्रहसन्त्स्वसुतं किल ।
मम किं लक्षणं पुत्र पश्यसे त्वं वदस्व मे ॥ 1.22.10
1.22.m:
Then Mahādeva, laughing, said to his son:
“What mark of mine, O son, do you see? Tell me.”

1.22.s:
sa covāca kare tubhyaṃ kapālaṃ dvijalakṣitam .
avicāreṇa saṃsthāpyaṃ kapālī tena cocyate . .
sa tallakṣaṇamādāya samudre prākṣipadruṣā . . 11
1.22.d:
स चोवाच करे तुभ्यं कपालं द्विजलक्षितम् ।
अविचारेण संस्थाप्यं कपाली तेन चोच्यते ॥
स तल्लक्षणमादाय समुद्रे प्राक्षिपद्रुषा ॥ 11
1.22.m:
And he said: “In your hand a skull marked by a twice-born [Brahmin]
was placed without deliberation; therefore you are called Kapālī.”
In anger he took that treatise on marks and cast it into the ocean.

1.22.s:
atha devasamāje vai pravṛtte brahmarudrayoḥ .
ahaṃ jyāyānahaṃ jyāyānvivādo'bhūttayordvayoḥ . .
tava saṃbhūtyabhijño'sti māṃ tu veda na kaścana . . 12
1.22.d:
अथ देवसमाजे वै प्रवृत्ते ब्रह्मरुद्रयोः ।
अहं ज्यायानहं ज्यायान्विवादोऽभूत्तयोर्द्वयोः ॥
तव संभूत्यभिज्ञोऽस्ति मां तु वेद न कश्चन ॥ 12
1.22.m:
Then, when an assembly of the gods had convened between Brahmā and Rudra,
a dispute arose between the two of them: “I am greater!” “I am greater!”
[Rudra said:] “There is one who knows of your birth, but no one knows of mine.”

1.22.s:
evaṃ śive'ti bruvati brahmaṇaḥ pañcamaṃ śiraḥ .
muktāṭṭahāsaṃ provāca tvāmahaṃ veditā bhava . . 13
1.22.d:
एवं शिवेऽति ब्रुवति ब्रह्मणः पञ्चमं शिरः ।
मुक्ताट्टहासं प्रोवाच त्वामहं वेदिता भव ॥ 13
1.22.m:
As Śiva was saying this, the fifth head of Brahmā,
bursting into a loud laugh, said: “I know you, O Bhava!”

1.22.s:
evaṃ bruvantu rudreṇa brāhmaṃ hayaśiro mahat .
nakhāgreṇa nikṛttaṃ ca tasyaiva ca kare sthitam . . 14
1.22.d:
एवं ब्रुवन्तु रुद्रेण ब्राह्मं हयशिरो महत् ।
नखाग्रेण निकृत्तं च तस्यैव च करे स्थितम् ॥ 14
1.22.m:
As it spoke thus, the great horse-head of Brahmā
was severed by Rudra with the tip of his fingernail and remained right in his hand.

1.22.s:
karasthenaiva tenāsāvāgacchadyatra vai hariḥ .
tapastepe tadā merau tatrāsau bhagavānvaśī . . 15
1.22.d:
करस्थेनैव तेनासावागच्छद्यत्र वै हरिः ।
तपस्तेपे तदा मेरौ तत्रासौ भगवान्वशी ॥ 15
1.22.m:
With it remaining in his hand, he went to where Hari was;
the lord, self-controlled, was then performing austerities on Mount Meru.

1.22.s:
kṛtte hayaśire tasminsthānāttasmāttu brahmaṇaḥ .
roṣādviniḥsṛtastvanyaḥ puruṣaḥ śvetakuṇḍalī . . 16
1.22.d:
कृत्ते हयशिरे तस्मिन्स्थानात्तस्मात्तु ब्रह्मणः ।
रोषाद्विनिःसृतस्त्वन्यः पुरुषः श्वेतकुण्डली ॥ 16
1.22.m:
When that horse-head was severed, from that place of Brahmā
another man wearing white earrings came forth in wrath.

1.22.s:
kavacī saśiraskaśca saśaraḥ saśarāsanaḥ .
anirdeśyavapuḥ sragvī kiṃ karomi sa cābravīt . . 17
1.22.d:
कवची सशिरस्कश्च सशरः सशरासनः ।
अनिर्देश्यवपुः स्रग्वी किं करोमि स चाब्रवीत् ॥ 17
1.22.m:
Armoured, wearing a helmet, with arrows and a bow,
of indescribable form and wearing a garland, he said, “What shall I do?”

1.22.s:
athovāca ruṣā brahmā hanyatāṃ sa sudurmatiḥ .
sa tu mārgeṇa rudrasya āgacchadroṣato drutam . . 18
1.22.d:
अथोवाच रुषा ब्रह्मा हन्यतां स सुदुर्मतिः ।
स तु मार्गेण रुद्रस्य आगच्छद्रोषतो द्रुतम् ॥ 18
1.22.m:
Then Brahmā said in fury, “Let that utterly wicked one be slain!”
And he went swiftly following Rudra's path in anger.

1.22.s:
rudro'pi viṣṇutejobhiḥ praviṣṭaḥ sa tvadhiṣṭhitaḥ .
sa praviśya tadāpaśyattapantaṃ cottamaṃ tapaḥ . .
haro nārāyaṇaṃ devaṃ vaikuṇṭhamaparājitam . . 19
1.22.d:
रुद्रोऽपि विष्णुतेजोभिः प्रविष्टः स त्वधिष्ठितः ।
स प्रविश्य तदापश्यत्तपन्तं चोत्तमं तपः ॥
हरो नारायणं देवं वैकुण्ठमपराजितम् ॥ 19
1.22.m:
Rudra too, having entered, established himself in the splendours of Viṣṇu.
Having entered, Hara then saw the god Nārāyaṇa,
Vaikuṇṭha, the undefeated, performing supreme austerities.

1.22.s:
haraṃ dṛṣṭvātha samprāptaṃ kāryaṃ cāsya vicintya ca .
uvāca śūlinaṃ devo bhindhi śūlena me bhujam . . 1.22.20
1.22.d:
हरं दृष्ट्वाथ सम्प्राप्तं कार्यं चास्य विचिन्त्य च ।
उवाच शूलिनं देवो भिन्धि शूलेन मे भुजम् ॥ 1.22.20
1.22.m:
Seeing Hara arrived and considering his purpose,
the god said to the trident-bearer, “Pierce my arm with your trident!”

1.22.s: sa bibheda mahātejā bhujaṃ śūlena taṃ haraḥ . . 21
1.22.d: स बिभेद महातेजा भुजं शूलेन तं हरः ॥ 21
1.22.m: Hara, possessing great splendour, pierced that arm with his trident.

1.22.s:
śūlabhedādasṛkcordhvaṃ jagāmāvṛtya rodasī .
vinivṛtya tataḥ paścātkapāle nipapāta ha . . 22
1.22.d:
शूलभेदादसृक्चोर्ध्वं जगामावृत्य रोदसी ।
विनिवृत्य ततः पश्चात्कपाले निपपात ह ॥ 22
1.22.m:
From the piercing of the trident, blood went upward, covering heaven and earth;
then, turning back afterwards, it fell into the skull.

1.22.s:
asṛkkapāle patitaṃ pradeśinyā vyavarddhayat .
yadā hi vinivṛttiḥ syāddevasya rudhiraṃ prati . . 23
1.22.d:
असृक्कपाले पतितं प्रदेशिन्या व्यवर्द्धयत् ।
यदा हि विनिवृत्तिः स्याद्देवस्य रुधिरं प्रति ॥ 23
1.22.m:
He caused the blood that had fallen into the skull to swell with his forefinger,
so that there might be a turning away of the god towards the blood.

1.22.s:
tadā tu vyasṛjattoyaṃ sa kṛtvā vāruṇīṃ tanum .
toye pravṛtte'sṛgbhūte kapāle yatra tacchiraḥ . . 24
1.22.d:
तदा तु व्यसृजत्तोयं स कृत्वा वारुणीं तनुम् ।
तोये प्रवृत्तेऽसृग्भूते कपाले यत्र तच्छिरः ॥ 24
1.22.m:
Then, assuming a watery form, he released water.
When the water turned into blood in the skull where that head was,

1.22.s:
kapāle tu pradeśinyā rudro'sau rudhire'sṛjat .
āmuktakavacaṃ raktaṃ raktakuṇḍalinaṃ naram . . 25
1.22.d:
कपाले तु प्रदेशिन्या रुद्रोऽसौ रुधिरेऽसृजत् ।
आमुक्तकवचं रक्तं रक्तकुण्डलिनं नरम् ॥ 25
1.22.m:
in the skull, with his forefinger, Rudra created in the blood
a man clad in armour, red, and wearing red earrings.

1.22.s:
athovāca bhavaṃ devaṃ kiṃ karomīti mānada .
asāvapi sasarjātha śvetakuṇḍalinaṃ naram . . 26
1.22.d:
अथोवाच भवं देवं किं करोमीति मानद ।
असावपि ससर्जाथ श्वेतकुण्डलिनं नरम् ॥ 26
1.22.m:
Then he said to the god Bhava, “What shall I do, O giver of honour?”
And he too then created a man wearing white earrings.

1.22.s:
tāvubhau samayudhyetāṃ dhanuṣpravaradhāriṇau .
yathā rājanbalīyāṃsau kujaketū yugātyaye . . 27
1.22.d:
तावुभौ समयुध्येतां धनुष्प्रवरधारिणौ ।
यथा राजन्बलीयांसौ कुजकेतू युगात्यये ॥ 27
1.22.m:
The two of them, bearing excellent bows, fought together,
just as, O king, the two mighty planets Mars and Ketu fight at the end of an aeon.

1.22.s:
tayostu yudhyatorevaṃ saṃvartaścādhiko gataḥ .
na cādṛśyata vijaya ekasyāpi tadā tayoḥ . . 28
1.22.d:
तयोस्तु युध्यतोरेवं संवर्तश्चाधिको गतः ।
न चादृश्यत विजय एकस्यापि तदा तयोः ॥ 28
1.22.m:
As the two were fighting thus, more than a cosmic dissolution elapsed,
and yet victory was not seen for either one of the two.

1.22.s:
athāntarikṣe tau dṛṣṭvā vāguvācāśarīriṇī .
avatāro'tha bhavitā yuvayorhi mayā saha . . 29
1.22.d:
अथान्तरिक्षे तौ दृष्ट्वा वागुवाचाशरीरिणी ।
अवतारोऽथ भविता युवयोर्हि मया सह ॥ 29
1.22.m:
Then, seeing them, a bodiless voice spoke in the sky:
“An incarnation of the two of you shall come to pass along with me.

1.22.s:
bhārāpanodaḥ karttavyaḥ pṛthivyarthe suraiḥ saha .
tadāścaryo hi bhavitā devakāryārthasiddhaye . . 1.22.30
1.22.d:
भारापनोदः कर्त्तव्यः पृथिव्यर्थे सुरैः सह ।
तदाश्चर्यो हि भविता देवकार्यार्थसिद्धये ॥ 1.22.30
1.22.m:
The removal of the burden must be accomplished for the sake of the earth, along with the gods;
then it will indeed be miraculous for the success of the gods' purpose.

1.22.s:
bhūlokabhāvaṃ nirdhūya bhūyo gantā surālayam .
evamuktvā tu vaikuṇṭho dadāvekaṃ ravestadā . . 31
1.22.d:
भूलोकभावं निर्धूय भूयो गन्ता सुरालयम् ।
एवमुक्त्वा तु वैकुण्ठो ददावेकं रवेस्तदा ॥ 31
1.22.m:
Having cast off worldly existence, you shall go once again to the abode of the gods.”
Having spoken thus, Vaikuṇṭha then gave one to Ravi.

1.22.s:
śvetakuṇḍalinaṃ dṛptaṃ1 taṃ jagrāha ravirmudā .
indrasyāpi tataḥ paścādraktakuṇḍalinaṃ dadau ..32
1.22.d:
श्वेतकुण्डलिनं दृप्तं1 तं जग्राह रविर्मुदा ।
इन्द्रस्यापि ततः पश्चाद्रक्तकुण्डलिनं ददौ ॥32
1.22.m:
Ravi joyfully received the proud one with white earrings;
then, after that, he gave the one with red earrings to Indra.

1.22.s:
jagrāha ca mudā yukta indraḥ svaṃ ca puraṃ yayau .
gatau ravīndrau pragṛhya puruṣau krodhasambhavau ..3 3
athovāca tadā rudraṃ devaḥ kamalasaṃsthitaḥ .
gaccha tvamapi kāpāle kapālavratacaryayā ..
avatāro vratasyāsya martyaloke bhaviṣyati .. 34
1.22.d:
जग्राह च मुदा युक्त इन्द्रः स्वं च पुरं ययौ ।
गतौ रवीन्द्रौ प्रगृह्य पुरुषौ क्रोधसम्भवौ ॥3 3
अथोवाच तदा रुद्रं देवः कमलसंस्थितः ।
गच्छ त्वमपि कापाले कपालव्रतचर्यया ॥
अवतारो व्रतस्यास्य मर्त्यलोके भविष्यति ॥ 34
1.22.m:
Filled with joy, Indra received him and went to his own city.
When Ravi and Indra had departed, taking the two men born of anger,
the god seated on the lotus then said to Rudra:
“You too, go, bearing the skull, performing the practice of the skull-observance;
there will be an incarnation of this observance in the mortal world.

1.22.s:
ye ca vrataṃ tvadīyaṃ vai dhārayiṣyanti mānavāḥ .
na teṣāṃ durlabhaṃ kiñcidbhaviteha paratra ca ..35
1.22.d:
ये च व्रतं त्वदीयं वै धारयिष्यन्ति मानवाः ।
न तेषां दुर्लभं किञ्चिद्भवितेह परत्र च ॥35
1.22.m:
And whatever humans shall maintain this observance of yours,
nothing will be difficult for them to attain, here or in the hereafter.”

1.22.s:
evaṃ saṃlapya bahuśaḥ sumukhaṃ pratinandya ca .
āhūya ca samudraṃ sa pratyuvācāvicārayan ..36
1.22.d:
एवं संलप्य बहुशः सुमुखं प्रतिनन्द्य च ।
आहूय च समुद्रं स प्रत्युवाचाविचारयन् ॥36
1.22.m:
Having conversed thus at length, and having cheered Sumukha,
he summoned the Ocean and replied without hesitation:

1.22.s:
kuruṣvābharaṇaṃ2 strīṇāṃ lakṣaṇaṃ yadvilakṣaṇam .
kārttikeyena yatproktaṃ tadvadasvāvicārayan .. 37
1.22.d:
कुरुष्वाभरणं2 स्त्रीणां लक्षणं यद्विलक्षणम् ।
कार्त्तिकेयेन यत्प्रोक्तं तद्वदस्वाविचारयन् ॥ 37
1.22.m:
“Make the marks that serve as ornaments for women, and those that are contrary;
proclaim without hesitation that which was spoken by Kārttikeya.”

1.22.s:
sa cāha mama nāmnedaṃ bhavetpuruṣalakṣaṇam .
devena tatpratijñātamevametadbhaviṣyati ..38
1.22.d:
स चाह मम नाम्नेदं भवेत्पुरुषलक्षणम् ।
देवेन तत्प्रतिज्ञातमेवमेतद्भविष्यति ॥38
1.22.m:
And he said: “Let this treatise on the marks of men be known by my name.”
The god agreed to that: “So shall it be!”

1.22.s: kārttikeyena yatproktaṃ tadvadasvāvicārayan ..39
1.22.d: कार्त्तिकेयेन यत्प्रोक्तं तद्वदस्वाविचारयन् ॥39
1.22.m: “Proclaim without hesitation that which was spoken by Kārttikeya.

1.22.s:
prayacchāsya viṣāṇaṃ vai niṣkṛṣṭaṃ yattvayā'dhunā .
avaśyameva tadbhūtaṃ bhavitavyaṃ tu kasyacit ..1.22.40
1.22.d:
प्रयच्छास्य विषाणं वै निष्कृष्टं यत्त्वयाऽधुना ।
अवश्यमेव तद्भूतं भवितव्यं तु कस्यचित् ॥1.22.40
1.22.m:
Give back his tusk, which you pulled out just now;
for that must inevitably come to be for someone.

1.22.s:
ṛte vināyakaṃ tadvai daivayogānna kāmataḥ .
gṛhāṇa etatsāmudraṃ yattvayā parikīrtitam ..41
1.22.d:
ऋते विनायकं तद्वै दैवयोगान्न कामतः ।
गृहाण एतत्सामुद्रं यत्त्वया परिकीर्तितम् ॥41
1.22.m:
Except for Vināyaka, it happened by destiny and not by desire.
Receive this Sāmudra [treatise] which was proclaimed by you.

1.22.s:
strīpuṃsorlakṣaṇaṃ śreṣṭhaṃ sāmudramiti viśrutama .
imaṃ ca saviṣāṇaṃ vai kuru devavināyakama ..42
1.22.d:
स्त्रीपुंसोर्लक्षणं श्रेष्ठं सामुद्रमिति विश्रुतम ।
इमं च सविषाणं वै कुरु देवविनायकम ॥42
1.22.m:
The excellent treatise on the marks of men and women is renowned as Sāmudra;
and make this god Vināyaka possessed of his tusk.”

1.22.s:
athovāca ca deveśaṃ bāhuleyaḥ samatsaram .
viṣāṇaṃ dadmi cāsyāhaṃ tava vākyānna saṃśayaḥ . . 43
1.22.d:
अथोवाच च देवेशं बाहुलेयः समत्सरम् ।
विषाणं दद्मि चास्याहं तव वाक्यान्न संशयः ॥ 43
1.22.m:
Then Bāhuleya spoke with envy to the lord of the gods:
“I give him the tusk at your command, no doubt.

1.22.s:
yadā tvayaṃ viṣāṇaṃ ca muktvā tu vicariṣyati .
tadā viṣāṇamuktaḥ sanbhasma aitaṃ kariṣyati . . 44
1.22.d:
यदा त्वयं विषाणं च मुक्त्वा तु विचरिष्यति ।
तदा विषाणमुक्तः सन्भस्म ऐतं करिष्यति ॥ 44
1.22.m:
However, when he roams about having set aside this tusk,
then, stripped of the tusk, he shall reduce this to ashes.”

1.22.s:
evamastviti taṃ coktvā viṣāṇaṃ tatkare dadau .
vināyakasya deveśaḥ kārtikeyamate sthitaḥ . . 45
1.22.d:
एवमस्त्विति तं चोक्त्वा विषाणं तत्करे ददौ ।
विनायकस्य देवेशः कार्तिकेयमते स्थितः ॥ 45
1.22.m:
Saying to him, “So be it,” the lord of the gods, abiding by Kārttikeya's view,
placed that tusk in the hand of Vināyaka.

1.22.s:
saviṣāṇakaro'dyāpi dṛśyate pratimā nṛpa .
bhīmasūnormahābāhorvighnaṃ karttuṃ mahātmanaḥ . . 46
1.22.d:
सविषाणकरोऽद्यापि दृश्यते प्रतिमा नृप ।
भीमसूनोर्महाबाहोर्विघ्नं कर्त्तुं महात्मनः ॥ 46
1.22.m:
Even today an image is seen with a tusk in hand, O king,
to cause an obstacle for the mighty-armed, great-souled son of Bhīma.

1.22.s:
etadrahasyaṃ devānāṃ mayā te samudāhṛtam .
yatra devo na vai veda devānāṃ bhuvi durlabham . . 47
1.22.d:
एतद्रहस्यं देवानां मया ते समुदाहृतम् ।
यत्र देवो न वै वेद देवानां भुवि दुर्लभम् ॥ 47
1.22.m:
This secret of the gods has been related to you by me,
which a god does not know, hard to attain in the world of the gods.

1.22.s:
mayā prasannena tava guhyametadudāhṛtam .
kathitaṃ tithisaṃyoge vināyakakathāmṛtam . . 48
1.22.d:
मया प्रसन्नेन तव गुह्यमेतदुदाहृतम् ।
कथितं तिथिसंयोगे विनायककथामृतम् ॥ 48
1.22.m:
Being pleased, I have related this secret to you;
the nectar-like tale of Vināyaka, narrated in connection with the lunar day.

1.22.s:
ya idaṃ śrāvayedvidvānbrāhmaṇānvedapāragān .
kṣatriyāṃśca svavṛttisthānviṭśūdrāṃśca guṇānvitān . . 49
1.22.d:
य इदं श्रावयेद्विद्वान्ब्राह्मणान्वेदपारगान् ।
क्षत्रियांश्च स्ववृत्तिस्थान्विट्शूद्रांश्च गुणान्वितान् ॥ 49
1.22.m:
Whatever learned man recites this to Brahmins who have mastered the Vedas,
to Kṣatriyas abiding in their proper duties, and to Vaiśyas and Śūdras endowed with virtues,

1.22.s:
na tasya durlabhaṃ kiñcidiha cāmutra vidyate .
na ca durgatimāpnoti na ca yāti parābhavam . . 1.22.50
1.22.d:
न तस्य दुर्लभं किञ्चिदिह चामुत्र विद्यते ।
न च दुर्गतिमाप्नोति न च याति पराभवम् ॥ 1.22.50
1.22.m:
nothing is difficult for him to attain, here or in the world beyond;
he neither meets with misfortune nor suffers defeat.

1.22.s:
nirvighnaṃ sarvakāryāṇi sādhayennātra saṃśayaḥ .
ṛddhiṃ vṛddhiṃ śriyaṃ cāpi vindeta bharatottama . . 51
iti śrībhaviṣye mahāpurāṇe śatārddhasāhasryāṃ saṃhitāyāṃ brāhme parvaṇi caturthīkalpavarṇanaṃ
nāma dvāviṃśo'dhyāyaḥ . 22 .
vighna-vināyakakathāvarṇanam
1.22.d:
निर्विघ्नं सर्वकार्याणि साधयेन्नात्र संशयः ।
ऋद्धिं वृद्धिं श्रियं चापि विन्देत भरतोत्तम ॥ 51
इति श्रीभविष्ये महापुराणे शतार्द्धसाहस्र्यां संहितायां ब्राह्मे पर्वणि चतुर्थीकल्पवर्णनं
नाम द्वाविंशोऽध्यायः । 22 ।
विघ्न-विनायककथावर्णनम्
1.22.m:
He will accomplish all undertakings without hindrance, there is no doubt in this; / and he will obtain prosperity, increase, and fortune, O best of the Bharatas.
Thus ends the twenty-second chapter, titled "Description of the Caturthī Rite", in the Brāhma Book of the holy and great Bhaviṣyapurāṇa consisting of fifty thousand verses.
Description of the Narrative of Vighna-Vināyaka

1.23.s:
śatānīka uvāca
kenāyaṃ bhīmajo vipra pramathādhipatiḥ kṛtaḥ .
bhartṛtve cāpi vighnānāmadhikārī kathaṃ babhau . . 1
1.23.d:
शतानीक उवाच
केनायं भीमजो विप्र प्रमथाधिपतिः कृतः ।
भर्तृत्वे चापि विघ्नानामधिकारी कथं बभौ ॥ 1
1.23.m: Śatānīka said: / By whom was this son of Bhīmā made the lord of the Pramathas, O vipra? / And how did he become the officer presiding over obstacles?

1.23.s:
sumanturuvāca
sādhu pṛṣṭo'smi rājendra yadayaṃ vighnakārakaḥ .
yairvāpi vighnakaraṇairniryukto'pi vināyakaḥ . .
tatte vacmi mahābāho śṛṇuṣvaikamanādhunā . . 2
1.23.d:
सुमन्तुरुवाच
साधु पृष्टोऽस्मि राजेन्द्र यदयं विघ्नकारकः ।
यैर्वापि विघ्नकरणैर्निर्युक्तोऽपि विनायकः ॥
तत्ते वच्मि महाबाहो शृणुष्वैकमनाधुना ॥ 2
1.23.m: Sumantu said: / I am well questioned, O king of kings, as to why he causes obstacles, / and by what obstacle-causing acts Vināyaka was appointed. / I shall tell you that, O mighty-armed one; listen now with a single-minded focus.

1.23.s:
ādye kṛtayuge vīra prajāsargamavāpa ha .
dṛṣṭvā karmāṇi siddhāni vinā vighnena bhārata . . 3
1.23.d:
आद्ये कृतयुगे वीर प्रजासर्गमवाप ह ।
दृष्ट्वा कर्माणि सिद्धानि विना विघ्नेन भारत ॥ 3
1.23.m: In the first Kṛtayuga, O hero, the creation of beings came about. / Seeing actions succeed without obstacle, O Bhārata,

1.23.s:
agatakleśāṃ prajāṃ dṛṣṭvā garvitāṃ kṛtsnaśo nṛpa .
bahuśaścintayityā tu idaṃ karma mahīpate . . 4
1.23.d:
अगतक्लेशां प्रजां दृष्ट्वा गर्वितां कृत्स्नशो नृप ।
बहुशश्चिन्तयित्या तु इदं कर्म महीपते ॥ 4
1.23.m: and seeing beings free from distress and wholly arrogant, O king, / thinking repeatedly about this deed, O ruler of the earth,

1.23.s:
vināyakaḥ samṛddhyarthaṃ prajānāṃ viniyojitaḥ .
gaṇānāṃ cādhipatye ca bhīmaḥ kañjajasāttvataiḥ . .
tatopasṛṣṭo yastasya lakṣaṇāni nibodha me . . 5
1.23.d:
विनायकः समृद्ध्यर्थं प्रजानां विनियोजितः ।
गणानां चाधिपत्ये च भीमः कञ्जजसात्त्वतैः ॥
ततोपसृष्टो यस्तस्य लक्षणानि निबोध मे ॥ 5
1.23.m: Vināyaka was appointed for the prosperity of beings / and for the lordship over the Gaṇas—the terrible one, by Brahmā and the Sāttvatas. / Hear from me the signs of one who is possessed by him:

1.23.s:
svapnevagāhate'tyarthaṃ jalaṃ muṇḍāṃśca paśyati .
kāṣāyavāsasaścaiva kravyādāṃścādhirohati . . 6
1.23.d:
स्वप्नेवगाहतेऽत्यर्थं जलं मुण्डांश्च पश्यति ।
काषायवाससश्चैव क्रव्यादांश्चाधिरोहति ॥ 6
1.23.m: In a dream he repeatedly plunges into water and sees shaven-headed men / and men wearing ochre garments, and he mounts carnivorous beasts.

1.23.s:
antyajairgardabhairuṣṭraiḥ sahaikatrāvatiṣṭhate .
vrajamānastathātmānaṃ manyate'nugataṃ paraiḥ . . 7
1.23.d:
अन्त्यजैर्गर्दभैरुष्ट्रैः सहैकत्रावतिष्ठते ।
व्रजमानस्तथात्मानं मन्यतेऽनुगतं परैः ॥ 7
1.23.m: He stays in one place with outcasts, donkeys, and camels; / and as he walks, he imagines himself pursued by enemies.

1.23.s:
vimanā viphalārambhaḥ saṃsīdatyanimittataḥ .
karaṭārūḍhamātmānamambhasontaragaṃ tathā . . 8
1.23.d:
विमना विफलारम्भः संसीदत्यनिमित्ततः ।
करटारूढमात्मानमम्भसोन्तरगं तथा ॥ 8
1.23.m: Despondent, with all undertakings fruitless, he sinks down for no cause; / and in a dream he sees himself mounted on a crow, submerged in water,

1.23.s:
pattibhiścāvṛtaṃ yāntaṃ saṅgamanāntikaṃ nṛpa .
paśyate kuruśārdūla svapnānte nātra saṃśayaḥ . . 9
1.23.d:
पत्तिभिश्चावृतं यान्तं सङ्गमनान्तिकं नृप ।
पश्यते कुरुशार्दूल स्वप्नान्ते नात्र संशयः ॥ 9
1.23.m: and surrounded by foot-soldiers, going near death, O king; / he sees [this], O tiger among Kurus, there is no doubt.

1.23.s:
cittaṃ ca vikṛtākāraṃ karavīravibhūṣitam .
tenopasṛṣṭo labhate na rājyaṃ paurvasaṃbhavam . . 1.23.10
1.23.d:
चित्तं च विकृताकारं करवीरविभूषितम् ।
तेनोपसृष्टो लभते न राज्यं पौर्वसंभवम् ॥ 1.23.10
1.23.m: His mind becomes distorted in form, adorned with oleander. / Possessed by him, one does not attain an ancestral kingdom;

1.23.s:
kumārī na ca bhartāramapatyaṃ garbhiṇī tathā .
ācāryatvaṃ śrotriyaśca śiṣyāścādhyayanaṃ tathā . .
vaṇiglābhaṃ ca nāpnoti kṛṣiṃ caiva kṛṣīvalaḥ . . 11
1.23.d:
कुमारी न च भर्तारमपत्यं गर्भिणी तथा ।
आचार्यत्वं श्रोत्रियश्च शिष्याश्चाध्ययनं तथा ॥
वणिग्लाभं च नाप्नोति कृषिं चैव कृषीवलः ॥ 11
1.23.m: an unmarried girl does not obtain a husband, nor a pregnant woman an offspring; / a Vedic scholar does not obtain the status of a teacher, nor students their study; / a merchant obtains no profit, and a farmer no harvest.

1.23.s:
snapanaṃ tasya kartavyaṃ puṇye'hani ' mahīpate .
gaurasarṣapakalkena sājyenotsāditena tu . . 12
1.23.d:
स्नपनं तस्य कर्तव्यं पुण्येऽहनि ' महीपते ।
गौरसर्षपकल्केन साज्येनोत्सादितेन तु ॥ 12
1.23.m: A bath should be performed for him on an auspicious day, O ruler of the earth, / with a paste of white mustard rubbed [on the body] together with ghee,

1.23.s:
śuklapakṣe caturthyāṃ tu vāsare dhiṣaṇasya ca .
tiṣye ca vīranakṣatre tasyaiva purato nṛpa . . 13
1.23.d:
शुक्लपक्षे चतुर्थ्यां तु वासरे धिषणस्य च ।
तिष्ये च वीरनक्षत्रे तस्यैव पुरतो नृप ॥ 13
1.23.m: on the caturthī of the bright fortnight, and on the day of Dhiṣaṇa, / under the Tiṣya constellation, a heroic lunar mansion, right before him, O king;

1.23.s:
sarvauṣadhaiḥ sarvagandhairviliptaśirasastathā .
bhadrāsanopaviṣṭasya svasti vācya dvijāñchubhān . . 14
1.23.d:
सर्वौषधैः सर्वगन्धैर्विलिप्तशिरसस्तथा ।
भद्रासनोपविष्टस्य स्वस्ति वाच्य द्विजाञ्छुभान् ॥ 14
1.23.m: his head anointed with all herbs and all scents, / seated upon an auspicious seat, having auspicious twice-born recite blessings,

1.23.s:
vyomakeśaṃ tu sampūjya pārvatīṃ bhīmajaṃ tathā .
kṛṣṇaṃ sapitaraṃ tāta pavamānaṃ sitaṃ tathā . . 15
1.23.d:
व्योमकेशं तु सम्पूज्य पार्वतीं भीमजं तथा ।
कृष्णं सपितरं तात पवमानं सितं तथा ॥ 15
1.23.m: and having worshipped Vyomakeśa, Pārvatī, and the son of Bhīmā, / Kṛṣṇa along with his father, dear one, Pavamāna and Sita,

1.23.s:
dhiṣaṇaṃ cenduputraṃ ca koṇaṃ ketuṃ ca 3 bhārata .
vidhuntudaṃ bāhuleyaṃ nandakasya ca dhāriṇam . . 16
1.23.d:
धिषणं चेन्दुपुत्रं च कोणं केतुं च 3 भारत ।
विधुन्तुदं बाहुलेयं नन्दकस्य च धारिणम् ॥ 16
1.23.m: Dhiṣaṇa, the son of the Moon, Koṇa, and Ketu, O Bhārata, / Vidhuntuda, Bāhuleya, and the bearer of the Nandaka sword.

1.23.s:
aśvasthānādgajasthānādvalmīkātsaṅgamādhradāt .
mṛttikāṃ rocanāṃ gandhānguggulaṃ cāpsu nikṣipet . . 17
1.23.d:
अश्वस्थानाद्गजस्थानाद्वल्मीकात्सङ्गमाध्रदात् ।
मृत्तिकां रोचनां गन्धान्गुग्गुलं चाप्सु निक्षिपेत् ॥ 17
1.23.m: From a stable of horses, a place of elephants, an anthill, and the confluence of a lake, / one should throw earth, rocanā, perfumes, and bdellium into water,

1.23.s:
yadāhṛtaṃ hyekavarṇaiścaturbhiḥ kalaśairhradāt .
carmaṇyānaḍuhe rakte sthāpyaṃ bhadrāsanaṃ tathā . . 18
1.23.d:
यदाहृतं ह्येकवर्णैश्चतुर्भिः कलशैर्ह्रदात् ।
चर्मण्यानडुहे रक्ते स्थाप्यं भद्रासनं तथा ॥ 18
1.23.m: which was brought in four single-coloured pots from a lake. / An auspicious seat is to be placed upon a red bull-hide.

1.23.s:
sahasrākṣaṃ śatadhāramṛṣibhiḥ 1 pāvanaṃ kṛtam .
tena tvāmabhiṣiñcāmi pāvamānyaḥ punantu te . . 19
1.23.d:
सहस्राक्षं शतधारमृषिभिः 1 पावनं कृतम् ।
तेन त्वामभिषिञ्चामि पावमान्यः पुनन्तु ते ॥ 19
1.23.m: "The thousand-eyed, hundred-streamed [bath] made purifying by the sages, / with that I consecrate you; may the purifying verses cleanse you!

1.23.s:
bhagaṃ te varuṇo rājā bhagaṃ sūryo bṛhaspatiḥ .
bhagamindraśca vāyuśca bhagaṃ saptarṣayo daduḥ . . 1.23.20
1.23.d:
भगं ते वरुणो राजा भगं सूर्यो बृहस्पतिः ।
भगमिन्द्रश्च वायुश्च भगं सप्तर्षयो ददुः ॥ 1.23.20
1.23.m: May King Varuṇa grant you good fortune, may the Sun and Bṛhaspati grant you good fortune; / may Indra and Vāyu grant you good fortune, and may the seven sages grant you good fortune!

1.23.s:
yatte keśeṣu daurbhāgyaṃ sīmante yacca mūrdhani .
lalāṭe karṇayorakṣṇorāpastad ghnantu te sadā . . 21
1.23.d:
यत्ते केशेषु दौर्भाग्यं सीमन्ते यच्च मूर्धनि ।
ललाटे कर्णयोरक्ष्णोरापस्तद् घ्नन्तु ते सदा ॥ 21
1.23.m: Whatever misfortune is in your hair, in your parting, or on your head, / on your forehead, in your ears, or in your eyes, may the waters destroy that forever!"

1.23.s:
snātasya sārṣapaṃ tailaṃ suveṇaudumbareṇa tu .
juhuyānmūrdhani kuśānsavyena parigṛhya tu . . 22
1.23.d:
स्नातस्य सार्षपं तैलं सुवेणौदुम्बरेण तु ।
जुहुयान्मूर्धनि कुशान्सव्येन परिगृह्य तु ॥ 22
1.23.m: Of the one who has bathed, one should offer mustard oil upon the head with an udumbara ladle, / holding kuśa grass in the left hand.

1.23.s:
mitaśca sammitaścaiva tathā ca śālakaṃṭakaḥ .
kūṣmāṇḍo rājaśreṣṭhāste'gnayaḥ svāhāsamanvitāḥ . . 23
1.23.d:
मितश्च सम्मितश्चैव तथा च शालकंटकः ।
कूष्माण्डो राजश्रेष्ठास्तेऽग्नयः स्वाहासमन्विताः ॥ 23
1.23.m: "Mita, Sammita, Śālakaṭaṅkaṭa, / and Kūṣmāṇḍa, O best of kings, these fires accompanied by svāhā!"

1.23.s:
nāmabhirbalimantraiśca namaskārasamanvitaiḥ .
dadyāccatuṣpathe śūrpe kuśānāstīrya sarvataḥ . . 24
1.23.d:
नामभिर्बलिमन्त्रैश्च नमस्कारसमन्वितैः ।
दद्याच्चतुष्पथे शूर्पे कुशानास्तीर्य सर्वतः ॥ 24
1.23.m: With their names and offering-mantras accompanied by reverential salutations, / one should place [the offering] at a crossroads in a winnowing basket, having strewn kuśa grass all around:

1.23.s:
kṛtākṛtāṃstaṇḍulāṃśca palalaudanameva ca .
matsyānpakvāṃstathaivāmānmāṃsametāvadeva tu . . 25
1.23.d:
कृताकृतांस्तण्डुलांश्च पललौदनमेव च ।
मत्स्यान्पक्वांस्तथैवामान्मांसमेतावदेव तु ॥ 25
1.23.m: Husked and unhusked rice grains, rice cooked with sesamum, / cooked and raw fish, and flesh to this extent,

1.23.s:
puṣpaṃ citraṃ sagandhaṃ ca surāṃ ca trividhāmapi .
mūlakaṃ pūrikāḥ pūpāṃstathaivoṇḍerikāsrajam . .
dadhipāyasamannaṃ ca guḍaveṣṭānsamodakān . . 26
1.23.d:
पुष्पं चित्रं सगन्धं च सुरां च त्रिविधामपि ।
मूलकं पूरिकाः पूपांस्तथैवोण्डेरिकास्रजम् ॥
दधिपायसमन्नं च गुडवेष्टान्समोदकान् ॥ 26
1.23.m: variegated and fragrant flowers, three kinds of liquor, / radish, purīs, cakes, garlands of sweetmeats, / curd, rice-pudding, and food wrapped in jaggery along with modakas.

1.23.s:
vināyakasya jananīmupatiṣṭhettato'mbikām .
dūrvāsarṣapapuṣpāṇāṃ dattvā puṣpāñjalitrayam . . 27
1.23.d:
विनायकस्य जननीमुपतिष्ठेत्ततोऽम्बिकाम् ।
दूर्वासर्षपपुष्पाणां दत्त्वा पुष्पाञ्जलित्रयम् ॥ 27
1.23.m: Then one should wait upon Ambikā, the mother of Vināyaka, / offering three handfuls of flowers consisting of dūrvā grass and mustard blossoms:

1.23.s:
rūpaṃ dehi yaśo dehi bhagaṃ bhagavati dehi me .
putrāndehi dhanaṃ dehi sarvānkāmāṃśca dehi me . .
acalāṃ buddhiṃ me dehi dharāyāṃ khyātimeva ca . . 28
1.23.d:
रूपं देहि यशो देहि भगं भगवति देहि मे ।
पुत्रान्देहि धनं देहि सर्वान्कामांश्च देहि मे ॥
अचलां बुद्धिं मे देहि धरायां ख्यातिमेव च ॥ 28
1.23.m: "Grant beauty, grant fame, grant good fortune to me, O goddess! / Grant sons, grant wealth, and grant all desires to me! / Grant me unshakeable intellect, and renown upon earth!"

1.23.s:
tataḥ śuklāmbaradharaḥ śuklamālyānulepanaḥ .
bhojayed brāhmaṇāndadyādvastrayugmaṃ gurorapi . . 29
1.23.d:
ततः शुक्लाम्बरधरः शुक्लमाल्यानुलेपनः ।
भोजयेद् ब्राह्मणान्दद्याद्वस्त्रयुग्मं गुरोरपि ॥ 29
1.23.m: Then, dressed in white garments, wearing white garlands and unguent, / he should feed brāhmaṇas and give a pair of garments to the teacher.

1.23.s:
evaṃ vināyakaṃ pūjya grahāṃścaiva vidhānataḥ .
karmaṇāṃ phalamāpnoti śriyaṃ prāpnotyanuttamām . . 1.23.30
1.23.d:
एवं विनायकं पूज्य ग्रहांश्चैव विधानतः ।
कर्मणां फलमाप्नोति श्रियं प्राप्नोत्यनुत्तमाम् ॥ 1.23.30
1.23.m: Having thus worshipped Vināyaka and the planets according to the rule, / one attains the fruit of rites and attains unsurpassed fortune.

1.23.s:
ādityasya sadā pūjāṃ tilakaṃ svāminastathā .
vināyakapateścaiva sarvasiddhimavāpnuyāt . . 31
iti śrī bhaviṣye mahāpurāṇe śatārddhasāhasryāṃ saṃhitāyāṃ brāhme parvaṇi caturthīkalpavarṇanaṃ
nāma trayoviṃśo'dhyāyaḥ . 23 .
caturthīkalpe puruṣalakṣaṇavarṇanam
1.23.d:
आदित्यस्य सदा पूजां तिलकं स्वामिनस्तथा ।
विनायकपतेश्चैव सर्वसिद्धिमवाप्नुयात् ॥ 31
इति श्री भविष्ये महापुराणे शतार्द्धसाहस्र्यां संहितायां ब्राह्मे पर्वणि चतुर्थीकल्पवर्णनं
नाम त्रयोविंशोऽध्यायः । 23 ।
चतुर्थीकल्पे पुरुषलक्षणवर्णनम्
1.23.m:
By constant worship of the Sun, the tilaka mark of the Lord, / and the master of Vināyakas, one attains all success.
Thus ends the twenty-third chapter, titled "Description of the Caturthī Rite", in the Brāhma Book of the holy and great Bhaviṣyapurāṇa consisting of fifty thousand verses.
Description of the Characteristics of Men in the Caturthī Rite

1.24.s:
śatānīka uvāca
narāṇāṃ yoṣitāṃ caiva lakṣaṇāni mahāmate .
proktāni yāni viprendra vyomakeśasya sūnunā . . 1
1.24.d:
शतानीक उवाच
नराणां योषितां चैव लक्षणानि महामते ।
प्रोक्तानि यानि विप्रेन्द्र व्योमकेशस्य सूनुना ॥ 1
1.24.m: Śatānīka said: / The bodily characteristics of men and women, O great-minded one, / which were spoken, O best of vipras, by the son of Vyomakeśa,

1.24.s:
kruddhena yāni kṣiptāni īśvareṇa mahodadhau .
kṛṣṇasya vacanād bhūyaḥ samudreṇārpitāni vai . . 2
1.24.d:
क्रुद्धेन यानि क्षिप्तानि ईश्वरेण महोदधौ ।
कृष्णस्य वचनाद् भूयः समुद्रेणार्पितानि वै ॥ 2
1.24.m: which were cast into the great ocean by the enraged Lord, / and again offered back by the ocean at the command of Kṛṣṇa—

1.24.s:
arpitāni tatastasya tena prāptāni vai kathan .
bāhuleyena viprendra tāni me vada suvrata . . 3
1.24.d:
अर्पितानि ततस्तस्य तेन प्राप्तानि वै कथन् ।
बाहुलेयेन विप्रेन्द्र तानि मे वद सुव्रत ॥ 3
1.24.m: offered by him then, how were they obtained by him, / by Bāhuleya, O best of vipras? Tell me that, O you of good vows!

1.24.s:
sumanturuvāca
yathā guhena rājendra strīpuṃsāṃ lakṣaṇāni vai .
proktāni kuruśārdūla tathā te kathayāmi vai . . 4
1.24.d:
सुमन्तुरुवाच
यथा गुहेन राजेन्द्र स्त्रीपुंसां लक्षणानि वै ।
प्रोक्तानि कुरुशार्दूल तथा ते कथयामि वै ॥ 4
1.24.m: Sumantu said: / As the bodily characteristics of women and men were spoken / by Guha, O king of kings, O tiger among Kurus, so I shall tell you.

1.24.s:
śaktipātāddhate krauñce vyomakeśasya sūnunā .
brahmā tuṣṭo'bravīdenaṃ varaṃ varaya me'nagha . . 5
1.24.d:
शक्तिपाताद्धते क्रौञ्चे व्योमकेशस्य सूनुना ।
ब्रह्मा तुष्टोऽब्रवीदेनं वरं वरय मेऽनघ ॥ 5
1.24.m: When Mount Krauñca was struck down by the strike of the spear by the son of Vyomakeśa, / Brahmā, being pleased, said to him: "Choose a boon from me, sinless one!"

1.24.s:
asāvapi mahātejāḥ praṇamya śirasā vibhum .
pitāmahaṃ babhāṣedaṃ lakṣaṇaṃ brūhi me vibho . . 6
1.24.d:
असावपि महातेजाः प्रणम्य शिरसा विभुम् ।
पितामहं बभाषेदं लक्षणं ब्रूहि मे विभो ॥ 6
1.24.m: He, endowed with great splendour, bowing with his head to the lord, / spoke this to the Grandfather: "Tell me the characteristics, O lord,

1.24.s:
narāṇāṃ yuvatīnāṃ ca kautukaṃ paramaṃ mama .
yanmayoktaṃ purā deva prakṣiptaṃ lavaṇārṇave . . 7
1.24.d:
नराणां युवतीनां च कौतुकं परमं मम ।
यन्मयोक्तं पुरा देव प्रक्षिप्तं लवणार्णवे ॥ 7
1.24.m: of men and young women; it is my supreme curiosity. / That which was spoken by me of old, O god, was cast into the salt sea."

1.24.s:
matpitrā devadeveśa sakrodhena purā tathā .
prāptaṃ ca vismṛtaṃ bhūyastanme brūhi hyaśeṣataḥ . . 8
1.24.d:
मत्पित्रा देवदेवेश सक्रोधेन पुरा तथा ।
प्राप्तं च विस्मृतं भूयस्तन्मे ब्रूहि ह्यशेषतः ॥ 8
1.24.m: and likewise by my father, O lord of the gods of gods, in anger long ago, / and was obtained and then forgotten again—explain that to me in full.

1.24.s:
brahmovāca
sādhu pṛṣṭo'smi deveśa bhīmasyānandavardhana .
lakṣaṇāni nibodha tvaṃ puruṣāṇāmaśeṣataḥ . .
adhamottamamadhyāni yāni prāpa payonidhiḥ . . 9
1.24.d:
ब्रह्मोवाच
साधु पृष्टोऽस्मि देवेश भीमस्यानन्दवर्धन ।
लक्षणानि निबोध त्वं पुरुषाणामशेषतः ॥
अधमोत्तममध्यानि यानि प्राप पयोनिधिः ॥ 9
1.24.m: Brahmā said: / I have been well questioned, O lord of gods, O increaser of the joy of Bhīma. / Learn from me the marks of men in their entirety, / the lowest, highest, and middling, which the ocean obtained.

1.24.s:
śive'hani sunakṣatre grahe saumye śubhe ravau .
pūrvāhṇe maṅgalairyukte parīkṣeta vicakṣaṇaḥ . . 1.24.10
1.24.d:
शिवेऽहनि सुनक्षत्रे ग्रहे सौम्ये शुभे रवौ ।
पूर्वाह्णे मङ्गलैर्युक्ते परीक्षेत विचक्षणः ॥ 1.24.10
1.24.m: On an auspicious day, under an auspicious constellation, when a benefic planet rules and the sun is favorable, / in the forenoon, endowed with auspicious circumstances, an expert should examine:

1.24.s:
pramāṇaṃ saṃhatiṃ chāyāṃ gatiṃ sarvāṅgalakṣaṇam .
dantakeśanakhaśmaśru etatsarvaṃ vicakṣaṇaḥ . . 11
1.24.d:
प्रमाणं संहतिं छायां गतिं सर्वाङ्गलक्षणम् ।
दन्तकेशनखश्मश्रु एतत्सर्वं विचक्षणः ॥ 11
1.24.m: measure, compactness, radiance, gait, the marks of all limbs, / teeth, hair, nails, and beard—all this the expert [should examine].

1.24.s:
pūrvamāyuḥ parīkṣeta paścāllakṣaṇamādiśet .
kṣīṇe hyāyuṣi martyānāṃ lakṣaṇaiḥ kiṃ prayojanam . . 12
1.24.d:
पूर्वमायुः परीक्षेत पश्चाल्लक्षणमादिशेत् ।
क्षीणे ह्यायुषि मर्त्यानां लक्षणैः किं प्रयोजनम् ॥ 12
1.24.m: First he should examine the lifespan; afterwards he should declare the marks. / For when the lifespan of mortals is exhausted, what is the use of bodily marks?

1.24.s:
jaghanyo navatiḥ prokto madhyamastu śatāḍgulaḥ .
aṣṭottaraśataṃ yasya uttamaṃ tasya lakṣaṇam . . 13
1.24.d:
जघन्यो नवतिः प्रोक्तो मध्यमस्तु शताड्गुलः ।
अष्टोत्तरशतं यस्य उत्तमं तस्य लक्षणम् ॥ 13
1.24.m: Ninety [aṅgulas] is said to be the lowest, and a hundred aṅgulas is middling; / one who has a hundred and eight has the highest mark.

1.24.s:
pramāṇalakṣaṇaṃ proktaṃ samudreṇa śubhāśubham .
yanme purā devavara mayā vai kathitaṃ tava . .
ataḥ paraṃ pravakṣyāmi dehāvayavalakṣaṇam . . 14
1.24.d:
प्रमाणलक्षणं प्रोक्तं समुद्रेण शुभाशुभम् ।
यन्मे पुरा देववर मया वै कथितं तव ॥
अतः परं प्रवक्ष्यामि देहावयवलक्षणम् ॥ 14
1.24.m: The auspicious and inauspicious mark of measurement was declared by the ocean, / which was told to me long ago, O best of gods, and indeed by me to you. / Hereafter I shall declare the marks of the parts of the body.

1.24.s:
pādaiḥ samāṃsakaiḥ 2 snigdhai raktaṃ saumyaiḥ suśobhanaiḥ .
unnataiḥ svedarahitaiḥ śirāhīnaiśca pārthivaḥ . . 15
1.24.d:
पादैः समांसकैः 2 स्निग्धै रक्तं सौम्यैः सुशोभनैः ।
उन्नतैः स्वेदरहितैः शिराहीनैश्च पार्थिवः ॥ 15
1.24.m: With fleshy, smooth, red, pleasing, very handsome, / elevated, sweatless, and veinless feet, [one is] an earthly king.

1.24.s:
yasya pādatale rekhā sāṃkuśeva prakāśate .
satataṃ hi sukhaṃ tasya puruṣasya na saṃśayaḥ . . 16
1.24.d:
यस्य पादतले रेखा सांकुशेव प्रकाशते ।
सततं हि सुखं तस्य पुरुषस्य न संशयः ॥ 16
1.24.m: A man on the sole of whose foot a line appears like an elephant goad / certainly has constant happiness; of this there is no doubt.

1.24.s:
asvedanau mṛdutalau kamalodarasannibhau .
śliṣṭāṅgulī 1 tāmranakhau supārṣṇī vyomakeśaja . . 17
1.24.d:
अस्वेदनौ मृदुतलौ कमलोदरसन्निभौ ।
श्लिष्टाङ्गुली 1 ताम्रनखौ सुपार्ष्णी व्योमकेशज ॥ 17
1.24.m: Sweatless, soft-soled, resembling the interior of a lotus, / with close-set toes, copper-colored nails, and good heels, O son of Vyomakeśa,

1.24.s:
uṣṇau śirāvirahitau gūḍhagulphau ca bhīmaja .
kūrmonnatau ca caraṇau prakhyātau pārthivasya tu . 18
1.24.d:
उष्णौ शिराविरहितौ गूढगुल्फौ च भीमज ।
कूर्मोन्नतौ च चरणौ प्रख्यातौ पार्थिवस्य तु । 18
1.24.m: warm, free of veins, with hidden ankles, O son of Bhīma, / and feet raised like a tortoise are well known to belong to an earthly king.

1.24.s:
śūrpākṛtī mahābāho rūkṣau śvetanakhau tathā .
vakrau śirāsantatau ca saṃśuṣkau viralāṅgulī . . 19
1.24.d:
शूर्पाकृती महाबाहो रूक्षौ श्वेतनखौ तथा ।
वक्रौ शिरासन्ततौ च संशुष्कौ विरलाङ्गुली ॥ 19
1.24.m: Shaped like winnowing baskets, O mighty-armed one, rough, with white nails, / crooked, covered with veins, withered, and with widely separated toes,

1.24.s:
dāridryaduḥkhadau jñeyau caraṇau bhīmanandana .
brahmaghnau devaśārdūla 3 pakvamṛtsadṛśau padau . . 1.24.20
1.24.d:
दारिद्र्यदुःखदौ ज्ञेयौ चरणौ भीमनन्दन ।
ब्रह्मघ्नौ देवशार्दूल 3 पक्वमृत्सदृशौ पदौ ॥ 1.24.20
1.24.m: such feet are to be known as bringing poverty and sorrow, O son of Bhīma. / Feet resembling baked clay, O tiger among gods, belong to a slayer of brahmins.

1.24.s:
pītāvagamyāniratau kṛṣṇau pānaratau sadā .
abhakṣyabhakṣaṇe śvetau jñeyau senādhipottama . . 21
1.24.d:
पीतावगम्यानिरतौ कृष्णौ पानरतौ सदा ।
अभक्ष्यभक्षणे श्वेतौ ज्ञेयौ सेनाधिपोत्तम ॥ 21
1.24.m: Yellow [feet indicate] delight in forbidden women; black ones, constant addiction to drinking; / white ones are to be known [to indicate] the eating of uneatable food, O best of army commanders.

1.24.s:
aṅguṣṭhau pṛthulau yeṣāṃ te narā bhāgyavarjitāḥ .
kliśyante vikṛtāṅguṣṭhāste narāḥ pādagāminaḥ . . 22
1.24.d:
अङ्गुष्ठौ पृथुलौ येषां ते नरा भाग्यवर्जिताः ।
क्लिश्यन्ते विकृताङ्गुष्ठास्ते नराः पादगामिनः ॥ 22
1.24.m: Men whose big toes are broad are devoid of good fortune. / Men with deformed big toes suffer distress and travel on foot.

1.24.s:
cipiṭairvikṛtairbhagnairaṅguṣṭhairatininditāḥ .
vakrairbhagnaistathā hrasvairaṅguṣṭhaiḥ kleśabhāginaḥ . . 23
1.24.d:
चिपिटैर्विकृतैर्भग्नैरङ्गुष्ठैरतिनिन्दिताः ।
वक्रैर्भग्नैस्तथा ह्रस्वैरङ्गुष्ठैः क्लेशभागिनः ॥ 23
1.24.m: Men with flat, deformed, and broken big toes are utterly contemptible; / with crooked, broken, and short big toes they share in misery.

1.24.s:
śūrpākāraiśca vikṛtairbhagnarvakraiḥ śirātataiḥ .
sasvedaiḥ pāṇḍurūkṣaiśca caraṇairatininditāḥ . . 24
1.24.d:
शूर्पाकारैश्च विकृतैर्भग्नर्वक्रैः शिराततैः ।
सस्वेदैः पाण्डुरूक्षैश्च चरणैरतिनिन्दिताः ॥ 24
1.24.m: With feet shaped like winnowing baskets, deformed, broken, crooked, covered with veins, / sweaty, pale, and rough, [men] are utterly contemptible.

1.24.s:
yasya pradeśinī dīrghā aṅguṣṭhaṃ yā atikramet .
strībhogaṃ labhate nityaṃ puruṣo nātra saṃśayaḥ . .
kaniṣṭhāyāṃ tu dīrghāyāṃ suvarṇasya tu bhāginaḥ . . 25
1.24.d:
यस्य प्रदेशिनी दीर्घा अङ्गुष्ठं या अतिक्रमेत् ।
स्त्रीभोगं लभते नित्यं पुरुषो नात्र संशयः ॥
कनिष्ठायां तु दीर्घायां सुवर्णस्य तु भागिनः ॥ 25
1.24.m: A man whose second toe is long and surpasses the big toe / continually obtains enjoyment of women; of this there is no doubt. / When the little toe is long, they partake of gold.

1.24.s:
cipiṭā viralāḥ śuṣkā yasyāṅgulyo bhavanti vai .
sa bhavedduḥkhito nityaṃ dhanahīnaśca vai 4 guha . . 26
1.24.d:
चिपिटा विरलाः शुष्का यस्याङ्गुल्यो भवन्ति वै ।
स भवेद्दुःखितो नित्यं धनहीनश्च वै 4 गुह ॥ 26
1.24.m: He whose toes are flat, separated, and withered / would be constantly miserable and devoid of wealth, O Guha.

1.24.s:
śvetairnakhairvirūkṣaiśca puruṣā duḥkhajīvinaḥ .
kuśīlāḥ kunakhairjñeyāḥ kāmabhogavivarjitāḥ . .
vikṛtaiḥ sphuṭitairūkṣairnakhairdāridryabhāginaḥ . . 27
1.24.d:
श्वेतैर्नखैर्विरूक्षैश्च पुरुषा दुःखजीविनः ।
कुशीलाः कुनखैर्ज्ञेयाः कामभोगविवर्जिताः ॥
विकृतैः स्फुटितैरूक्षैर्नखैर्दारिद्र्यभागिनः ॥ 27
1.24.m: With white and rough nails, men lead a life of sorrow. / With bad nails they are to be known as ill-behaved and devoid of pleasures of love. / With deformed, cracked, and dry nails they partake of poverty.

1.24.s:
brahmahatyāṃ ca kurvanti puruṣā haritairnakhaiḥ .
bandhubhiśca viyujyante kulakṣayakarāśca te . . 28
1.24.d:
ब्रह्महत्यां च कुर्वन्ति पुरुषा हरितैर्नखैः ।
बन्धुभिश्च वियुज्यन्ते कुलक्षयकराश्च ते ॥ 28
1.24.m: Men with greenish nails commit the murder of a brahmin; / they are separated from their kinsmen and cause the ruin of their family.

1.24.s:
indragopakasaṃkāśairnakhairnṛpatayaḥ smṛtāḥ .
śaṅkhāvartapratīkāśairnakhairbhavati pārthivaḥ . . 29
1.24.d:
इन्द्रगोपकसंकाशैर्नखैर्नृपतयः स्मृताः ।
शङ्खावर्तप्रतीकाशैर्नखैर्भवति पार्थिवः ॥ 29
1.24.m: With nails resembling cochineal insects, they are remembered as kings. / With nails resembling the spiral of a conch, one becomes an earthly king.

1.24.s:
tāmrairnakhaistathaiśvaryaṃ dhanyāḥ padmanakhā narāḥ .
raktairnakhaistathaiśvaryaṃ puṣpitaiḥ subhago bhavet . .
sūkṣmairupacitaistāmrairnakhairnṛpatayaḥ smṛtāḥ . . 1.24.30
1.24.d:
ताम्रैर्नखैस्तथैश्वर्यं धन्याः पद्मनखा नराः ।
रक्तैर्नखैस्तथैश्वर्यं पुष्पितैः सुभगो भवेत् ॥
सूक्ष्मैरुपचितैस्ताम्रैर्नखैर्नृपतयः स्मृताः ॥ 1.24.30
1.24.m: With copper-colored nails there is sovereignty; men with lotus-like nails are fortunate. / With red nails there is sovereignty; with spotted ones one becomes fortunate. / With slender, well-developed, copper-colored nails they are remembered as kings.

1.24.s:
romaśābhyāṃ ca jaṅghābhyāṃ duḥkhadāridryabhāginaḥ .
bandhanaṃ hrasvajaṅghānāmaiśvaryaṃ caiva nirdiśet . . 31
1.24.d:
रोमशाभ्यां च जङ्घाभ्यां दुःखदारिद्र्यभागिनः ।
बन्धनं ह्रस्वजङ्घानामैश्वर्यं चैव निर्दिशेत् ॥ 31
1.24.m: With hairy shanks, they partake of sorrow and poverty. / One should indicate imprisonment for those with short shanks, and sovereignty [for well-proportioned ones].

1.24.s:
1mṛgajaṅghāśca rājāno jāyante nātra saṃśayaḥ .
dīrghajaṅghāḥ sthūlajaṅghā nityaṃ bhāgyavivarjitāḥ . . 32
1.24.d:
1मृगजङ्घाश्च राजानो जायन्ते नात्र संशयः ।
दीर्घजङ्घाः स्थूलजङ्घा नित्यं भाग्यविवर्जिताः ॥ 32
1.24.m: Men with shanks like a deer become kings; of this there is no doubt. / Those with long shanks and thick shanks are always devoid of good fortune.

1.24.s:
śṛgālajaṅghāḥ puruṣā nityaṃ bhāgyavivarjitāḥ .
kākajaṃghā narā ye tu bhaveyurduḥkhabhāginaḥ . . 33
1.24.d:
शृगालजङ्घाः पुरुषा नित्यं भाग्यविवर्जिताः ।
काकजंघा नरा ये तु भवेयुर्दुःखभागिनः ॥ 33
1.24.m: Men with shanks like a jackal are always devoid of good fortune. / Men who have shanks like a crow would partake of sorrow.

1.24.s:
2pīnajaṅghāstathaiśvaryaṃ prāpnuvanti na saṃśayaḥ .
siṃhavyāghrasamā jaṅghā dhaninaḥ parikīrtitāḥ . . 34
1.24.d:
2पीनजङ्घास्तथैश्वर्यं प्राप्नुवन्ति न संशयः ।
सिंहव्याघ्रसमा जङ्घा धनिनः परिकीर्तिताः ॥ 34
1.24.m: Those with plump shanks obtain sovereignty; of this there is no doubt. / Those whose shanks resemble a lion or tiger are proclaimed to be wealthy.

1.24.s:
pārthivānāṃ bhavedroma caikaikaṃ romakūpake .
paṃḍitaśrotriyāṇāṃ ca dvedve jñeye mahāmate . . 35
1.24.d:
पार्थिवानां भवेद्रोम चैकैकं रोमकूपके ।
पंडितश्रोत्रियाणां च द्वेद्वे ज्ञेये महामते ॥ 35
1.24.m: Earthly kings have a single hair in each hair follicle; / wise men and learned Vedic scholars are known to have two each, O high-minded one.

1.24.s:
tribhistribhistathā niḥsvā mānavā duḥkhabhāginaḥ .
keśāścaiva mahābāho ninditā pūjitāstathā . . 36
1.24.d:
त्रिभिस्त्रिभिस्तथा निःस्वा मानवा दुःखभागिनः ।
केशाश्चैव महाबाहो निन्दिता पूजितास्तथा ॥ 36
1.24.m: With three each, mortals are penniless and partake of sorrow. / And hairs, O mighty-armed one, are likewise condemned or praised.

1.24.s: nirmāṃsajānurmriyate pravāse śivanandana 3 . . 37
1.24.d: निर्मांसजानुर्म्रियते प्रवासे शिवनन्दन 3 ॥ 37
1.24.m: One with fleshless knees dies in a foreign land, O son of Śiva.

1.24.s:
saubhāgyamalpai kathitaṃ dāridryaṃ vikaṭaistathā .
nimnaiḥ svastrījitā jñeyāḥ samāṃsai rājyabhāginaḥ . . 38
1.24.d:
सौभाग्यमल्पै कथितं दारिद्र्यं विकटैस्तथा ।
निम्नैः स्वस्त्रीजिता ज्ञेयाः समांसै राज्यभागिनः ॥ 38
1.24.m: Good fortune is declared from small [knees], and poverty from prominent ones. / With depressed [knees] they are to be known as dominated by their own wives; with fleshy [knees] they partake of kingship.

1.24.s:
4haṃsabhāsaśukānāṃ ca tulyā yasya gatirbhavet .
sa bhavetpārthivaḥ pūjyaḥ samudravacanaṃ yathā . . 39
1.24.d:
4हंसभासशुकानां च तुल्या यस्य गतिर्भवेत् ।
स भवेत्पार्थिवः पूज्यः समुद्रवचनं यथा ॥ 39
1.24.m: He whose gait is equal to that of a goose, a cock, or a parrot / becomes a worshipful earthly king, according to the words of the ocean.

1.24.s:
anyeṣāmapi śastānāṃ pakṣiṇāṃ ca śubhā gatiḥ .
vṛṣasiṃhagajendrāṇāṃ 6gatirbhogavivardhinī . . 1.24.40
1.24.d:
अन्येषामपि शस्तानां पक्षिणां च शुभा गतिः ।
वृषसिंहगजेन्द्राणां 6गतिर्भोगविवर्धिनी ॥ 1.24.40
