1.29.m: 'Gāṃ namaḥ' is to be known as the heart; 'gīṃ' is proclaimed as the head; / the crest is to be known as 'gūṃ namaḥ'; 'gaiṃ namaḥ' is held to be the armour;

1.29.s:
gauṃ namo netramuddiṣṭaṃ gaḥ phaṭ kāmāstramucyate .
āgaccholkāmukhāyeti mantra āvāhane hyayam . . 11
1.29.d:
गौं नमो नेत्रमुद्दिष्टं गः फट् कामास्त्रमुच्यते ।
आगच्छोल्कामुखायेति मन्त्र आवाहने ह्ययम् ॥ 11
1.29.m: 'Gauṃ namaḥ' is declared as the eye; 'gaḥ phaṭ' is spoken of as the desire-weapon; / and this mantra, 'Come, O you whose face is a meteor!', is for the invocation.

1.29.s:
gaṃ gaṇeśāya namo gandhamantraḥ prakīrtitaḥ .
puṣpolkāya namaḥ puṣpamantra eṣa prakīrtitaḥ . . 12
1.29.d:
गं गणेशाय नमो गन्धमन्त्रः प्रकीर्तितः ।
पुष्पोल्काय नमः पुष्पमन्त्र एष प्रकीर्तितः ॥ 12
1.29.m: 'Gaṃ, homage to Gaṇeśa' is proclaimed as the incense/fragrance mantra; / 'Homage to Puṣpolka' is proclaimed as this flower mantra.

1.29.s:
dhūpolkāya namo dhūpamantra eṣa prakīrtitaḥ .
dīpolkāya namo dīpamantra eṣa prakīrtitaḥ . . 13
1.29.d:
धूपोल्काय नमो धूपमन्त्र एष प्रकीर्तितः ।
दीपोल्काय नमो दीपमन्त्र एष प्रकीर्तितः ॥ 13
1.29.m: 'Homage to Dhūpolka' is proclaimed as this incense mantra; / 'Homage to Dīpolka' is proclaimed as this lamp mantra.

1.29.s:
oṃ gaṃ maholkāya namo balimantraḥ prakīrtitaḥ .
oṃ saṃsiddholkāya namo mantraścāyaṃ visarjane . . 14
1.29.d:
ओं गं महोल्काय नमो बलिमन्त्रः प्रकीर्तितः ।
ओं संसिद्धोल्काय नमो मन्त्रश्चायं विसर्जने ॥ 14
1.29.m: 'Oṃ gaṃ, homage to Maholka' is proclaimed as the offering mantra; / and this mantra, 'Oṃ, homage to Saṃsiddholka', is used in dismissal.

1.29.s:
oṃ mahākarṇāya vidmahe vakratuṇḍāya dhīmahi .
tanno dantiḥ pracodayāt gāyatrī japaḥ pūrvataḥ . . 15
1.29.d:
ओं महाकर्णाय विद्महे वक्रतुण्डाय धीमहि ।
तन्नो दन्तिः प्रचोदयात् गायत्री जपः पूर्वतः ॥ 15
1.29.m: 'Oṃ, we know the large-eared one; we meditate upon the one with the curved trunk; / may that tusker inspire us': this Gāyatrī is the recitation in the east.

1.29.s:
mahāgaṇapataye vīra1 svāhā dakṣiṇataḥ sadā .
maholkāya paścimataḥ kūśmāṇḍāyottareṇa tu . .
ekadantatripurāntakāya āgneyyāṃ vīra nirdiśet . . 16
1.29.d:
महागणपतये वीर1 स्वाहा दक्षिणतः सदा ।
महोल्काय पश्चिमतः कूश्माण्डायोत्तरेण तु ॥
एकदन्तत्रिपुरान्तकाय आग्नेय्यां वीर निर्दिशेत् ॥ 16
1.29.m: 'To Mahāgaṇapati, svāhā', O hero, always in the south; / 'To Maholka' in the west; and 'To Kūśmāṇḍa' in the north; / 'To the one-tusked destroyer of Tripura' one should designate in the southeast, O hero.

1.29.s:
oṃ śivadatta vikaṭaharahāsa prāṇāya svā nairṛtyām .
2tulambanātyacaladantakāya svāhā vāyavyām . . 17
1.29.d:
ओं शिवदत्त विकटहरहास प्राणाय स्वा नैरृत्याम् ।
2तुलम्बनात्यचलदन्तकाय स्वाहा वायव्याम् ॥ 17
1.29.m: 'Oṃ, O Śivadatta, whose laugh is the dread laughter of Hara, svāhā to the breath' in the southwest; / 'To the one with suspended, unmoving teeth, svāhā' in the northwest.

1.29.s:
padmadaṃṣṭrāya narāyeti aiśānyāṃ homayedbudhaḥ .
huṃ phaṭ hum̐ phaṭ hastatāladhvanirhasanakūrdanaḥ . . 18
1.29.d:
पद्मदंष्ट्राय नरायेति ऐशान्यां होमयेद्बुधः ।
हुं फट् हुम्̐ फट् हस्ततालध्वनिर्हसनकूर्दनः ॥ 18
1.29.m:
In the north-east, the wise man should offer oblations with: 'To Padmadaṃṣṭra, to Nara, svāhā.'
With clapping of hands uttering 'huṃ phaṭ huṃ phaṭ', laughing and leaping,

1.29.s:
mṛdanartanagaṇapatirdevasya mudrāṃ tato homaṃ samācaret .
na yadā vaśyā bhavati . .
kṛṣṇatilāhutimaṣṭasahasraṃ juhuyāttrirātreṇa rājā vaśyo bhavati . . 19
1.29.d:
मृदनर्तनगणपतिर्देवस्य मुद्रां ततो होमं समाचरेत् ।
न यदा वश्या भवति ॥
कृष्णतिलाहुतिमष्टसहस्रं जुहुयात्त्रिरात्रेण राजा वश्यो भवति ॥ 19
1.29.m:
[and] the hand gesture of the god Gaṇapati, dancer of the mṛdaṅga, he should then perform the homa.
When [a person] is not subdued,
one should offer eight thousand oblations of black sesame seeds; within three nights the king becomes subdued.

1.29.s:
tilayavahomena sarve janapadā vaśyā bhavanti .
ati rūpavatī kanyā gacchantamanu(?)cchati . . 1.29.20
1.29.d:
तिलयवहोमेन सर्वे जनपदा वश्या भवन्ति ।
अति रूपवती कन्या गच्छन्तमनु(?)च्छति ॥ 1.29.20
1.29.m:
Through homa of sesame seeds and barley, all subjects of the realm become subdued.
An exceedingly beautiful maiden pursues [him] as he walks.

1.29.s:
caṇatandulahomenājito bhavet .
nimbapatrasamaistailairvidveṣaṇaṃ karoti . .
somagrahaṇe udakamadhye avatīrya aṣṭasahasraṃ japet .
saṅgrāme aparājito bhavati . . 21
1.29.d:
चणतन्दुलहोमेनाजितो भवेत् ।
निम्बपत्रसमैस्तैलैर्विद्वेषणं करोति ॥
सोमग्रहणे उदकमध्ये अवतीर्य अष्टसहस्रं जपेत् ।
सङ्ग्रामे अपराजितो भवति ॥ 21
1.29.m:
Through homa of chickpeas and rice grains, he becomes invincible.
With oils mixed equally with nimba leaves, he causes enmity.
Descending into water during a lunar eclipse, he should mutter [the mantra] eight thousand times;
he becomes undefeated in battle.

1.29.s:
( oṃ lambarājñe namaḥ .)
ādityābhimukho bhūtvā aṣṭasahasraṃ japet .
ādityo varado bhavati . . 22
1.29.d:
( ओं लम्बराज्ञे नमः ।)
आदित्याभिमुखो भूत्वा अष्टसहस्रं जपेत् ।
आदित्यो वरदो भवति ॥ 22

1.29.s:
śuklacaturthyāmupoṣya gandhapuṣpādibhirarcanaṃ kṛtvā tilatandulāñjuhuyāt .
śirasā dhārayaṃstairaparājito bhavati . . 23
1.29.d:
शुक्लचतुर्थ्यामुपोष्य गन्धपुष्पादिभिरर्चनं कृत्वा तिलतन्दुलाञ्जुहुयात् ।
शिरसा धारयंस्तैरपराजितो भवति ॥ 23
1.29.m:
Having fasted on the fourth day of the bright fortnight and worshipped with perfumes, flowers, and the like, he should offer sesame seeds and rice grains.
Bearing them on his head, he becomes undefeated by them.

1.29.s:
apāmārgasamidbhiragniṃ prajvālya ekaviṃśatyāhutīryo juhuyāt .
trirātrācchatruṃ vyāpādayati . . 24
1.29.d:
अपामार्गसमिद्भिरग्निं प्रज्वाल्य एकविंशत्याहुतीर्यो जुहुयात् ।
त्रिरात्राच्छत्रुं व्यापादयति ॥ 24
1.29.m:
Having kindled the fire with kindling sticks of apāmārga, he who offers twenty-one oblations
kills his enemy within three nights.

1.29.s:
athottareṇa mantraṃ vyākhyāsye .
vṛkṣamūle kajjalaṃ saṅgṛhya saptabhirmantritaṃ kṛtvā netrāṇyañjayedyaṃ paśyati sa vaśī bhavati . . 25
1.29.d:
अथोत्तरेण मन्त्रं व्याख्यास्ये ।
वृक्षमूले कज्जलं सङ्गृह्य सप्तभिर्मन्त्रितं कृत्वा नेत्राण्यञ्जयेद्यं पश्यति स वशी भवति ॥ 25
1.29.m:
Now I shall explain the subsequent mantra:
Gathering collyrium at the root of a tree, empowering it seven times [with the mantra], one should anoint one's eyes; whomever he beholds becomes subjugated.

1.29.s: puṣpaṃ phalaṃ mūlaṃ cāṣṭasahasrābhimantritaṃ kṛtvā yasmai dadāti sa vaśyo bhavati . . 26
1.29.d: पुष्पं फलं मूलं चाष्टसहस्राभिमन्त्रितं कृत्वा यस्मै ददाति स वश्यो भवति ॥ 26
1.29.m: Having empowered a flower, fruit, or root eight thousand times, to whomever he gives it, that person becomes subdued.

1.29.s:
yatkiñcinmūlamantreṇa karoti tatsidhyati .
sarve grahāḥ suprītā bhavanti . .
nagaradvāraṃ gatvā aṣṭasahasraṃ dvāraṃ nirūpayet . . 27
1.29.d:
यत्किञ्चिन्मूलमन्त्रेण करोति तत्सिध्यति ।
सर्वे ग्रहाः सुप्रीता भवन्ति ॥
नगरद्वारं गत्वा अष्टसहस्रं द्वारं निरूपयेत् ॥ 27

1.29.s:
puraṃ dvāreṇa gṛhyate prāṅmukho yajati sa uccāṭayati .
sammukho japati corānvidrāvayati . . 28
1.29.d:
पुरं द्वारेण गृह्यते प्राङ्मुखो यजति स उच्चाटयति ।
सम्मुखो जपति चोरान्विद्रावयति ॥ 28
1.29.m:
The city is captured through the gate; facing east, he who sacrifices drives away [enemies];
facing straight ahead, he who mutters puts thieves to flight.

1.29.s: tṛṇāni lūnayati . kāṣṭhāni cchedayati . . 29
1.29.d: तृणानि लूनयति । काष्ठानि च्छेदयति ॥ 29
1.29.m: He cuts grasses; he chops pieces of wood.

1.29.s:
1gajarājena yuddhayati . jalamadhye saptarātraṃ japet . akāle varṣayati . kūpataḍāgāñchoṣayati . .
pratimāṃ nṛtyayati . ākarṣayati . stambhayati . yojanaśatātstrīpuruṣānākarṣayati . . 1.29.30
1.29.d:
1गजराजेन युद्धयति । जलमध्ये सप्तरात्रं जपेत् । अकाले वर्षयति । कूपतडागाञ्छोषयति ॥
प्रतिमां नृत्ययति । आकर्षयति । स्तम्भयति । योजनशतात्स्त्रीपुरुषानाकर्षयति ॥ 1.29.30
1.29.m:
He battles with the king of elephants. One should mutter [the mantra] within water for seven nights: he causes rain out of season; he dries up wells and ponds;
he makes an image dance; he attracts; he paralyzes; he attracts women and men from a hundred yojanas away.

1.29.s: gorocanāṃ ca sahasrābhimantritāṃ kṛtvā haste baddhvā yojanaśatasahasraṃ gatvā punarāgacchati . . 31
1.29.d: गोरोचनां च सहस्राभिमन्त्रितां कृत्वा हस्ते बद्ध्वा योजनशतसहस्रं गत्वा पुनरागच्छति ॥ 31
1.29.m: Having empowered gorocanā a thousand times and bound it to his hand, having traveled a hundred thousand yojanas, he returns again.

1.29.s: atha mārayitukāmaḥ khadirakīlakaṃ kṛtvā strīpuruṣaṃ vicintya hadaye nikhanayet . kṣaṇādeva mriyate . . 32
1.29.d: अथ मारयितुकामः खदिरकीलकं कृत्वा स्त्रीपुरुषं विचिन्त्य हदये निखनयेत् । क्षणादेव म्रियते ॥ 32
1.29.m: Now, wishing to kill, having made a peg of khadira wood and meditated upon the woman or man, he should drive it into the heart; [the victim] dies in an instant.

1.29.s: sarvapātakavimukto bhavati . agnitejāḥ sarvebhyo'parājito bhavati . . 33
1.29.d: सर्वपातकविमुक्तो भवति । अग्नितेजाः सर्वेभ्योऽपराजितो भवति ॥ 33
1.29.m: He becomes liberated from all sins; possessing the fiery splendour of fire, he becomes invincible to all.

1.29.s:
oṃ vakatuṇḍāya svāhā . oṃ ekadaṃṣṭrāya svāhā . oṃ kṛtakṛṣṇāya svāhā . oṃ gajakarṇāya svāhā . .
oṃ lambodarāya svāhā . oṃ vikaṭāya svāhā . oṃ dhūmravarṇāya svāhā . oṃ gaganakūjāya svāhā . .
oṃ vināyakāya svāhā . oṃ gaṇapataye svāhā . oṃ hastimukhāya svāhā . . 34
iti śrībhaviṣye mahāpurāṇe śatārddhasāhasryāṃ saṃhitāyāṃ brāhme parvaṇi caturthīkalpe
gaṇapatikalpavarṇanaṃ nāmaikonatriṃśo'dhyāyaḥ . 29 .
vināyakapūjāvidhivarṇanam
1.29.d:
ओं वकतुण्डाय स्वाहा । ओं एकदंष्ट्राय स्वाहा । ओं कृतकृष्णाय स्वाहा । ओं गजकर्णाय स्वाहा ॥
ओं लम्बोदराय स्वाहा । ओं विकटाय स्वाहा । ओं धूम्रवर्णाय स्वाहा । ओं गगनकूजाय स्वाहा ॥
ओं विनायकाय स्वाहा । ओं गणपतये स्वाहा । ओं हस्तिमुखाय स्वाहा ॥ 34
इति श्रीभविष्ये महापुराणे शतार्द्धसाहस्र्यां संहितायां ब्राह्मे पर्वणि चतुर्थीकल्पे
गणपतिकल्पवर्णनं नामैकोनत्रिंशोऽध्यायः । 29 ।
विनायकपूजाविधिवर्णनम्
1.29.m:
Om, to Vakratuṇḍa, svāhā! Om, to Ekadaṃṣṭra, svāhā! Om, to Kṛtakṛṣṇa, svāhā! Om, to Gajakarṇa, svāhā!
Om, to Lambodara, svāhā! Om, to Vikaṭa, svāhā! Om, to Dhūmravarṇa, svāhā! Om, to Gaganakūja, svāhā!
Om, to Vināyaka, svāhā! Om, to Gaṇapati, svāhā! Om, to Hastimukha, svāhā!
Thus ends the twenty-ninth chapter, titled 'Description of the Ritual Procedure of Gaṇapati', in the section on the fourth-day observances of the Brāhmaparvan in the venerable and great Bhaviṣyapurāṇa containing fifty thousand verses. 29.
Description of the rules for the worship of Vināyaka.
